title: MLC election results: BJP wins big, but Congress and Samajwadi Party send a message from Nagpur, Varanasi
text: BJP's big win in MLC elections comes with setbacks in Nagpur and Varanasi The MLC elections across four states brought both shock and cheer for the BJP and Congress. While the Congress suffered a humiliating defeat in Karnataka, where it is in power but failed to win a single seat, the BJP faltered in two constituencies which mattered the most. One being Nagpur, which is home to the RSS headquarters, and Varanasi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi's parliamentary constituency. The BJP nevertheless emerged as the largest party, winning 13 of the 28 seats contested, while its allies took the NDA's tally to 16. The alliance swept all four seats in Karnataka, won six of the 11 seats in Uttar Pradesh and secured four of the eight seats in Bihar. In Maharashtra, the ruling Mahayuti won two of the five seats, while the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi secured three. The Congress's only victory came from Nagpur, a political stronghold of Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and Union minister Nitin Gadkari. In Uttar Pradesh, the Samajwadi Party retained the Varanasi Teachers' constituency and was heading towards victory in the Graduates' seat, both of which it had won in 2020. BJP-led NDA secured 16 of the 28 MLC seats across four states, while the SP won five seats in Uttar Pradesh and Congress retained Nagpur in Maharashtra. What began as celebrations and sharp jibes at the Congress on Wednesday turned into a war of words on Thursday, as the results in Nagpur and Varanasi gave the opposition grounds to question the BJP's claims of electoral dominance. BJP mocks Congress over 'zero' seats As the early results came in on Wednesday, BJP leaders targeted the Congress over its poor performance, particularly in Karnataka, where the party is in power but failed to win a single seat. PM Modi took a swipe at the opposition party on X, pointing out that voting in the four states had taken place using ballot papers. "Guess how many seats Congress won?" he asked. The remark came amid the Congress's repeated allegations over electronic voting machines and its demand for a return to ballot-paper voting. BJP president Nitin Nabin also targeted the Congress, saying the party had failed to win public support despite voting being conducted using ballot papers. "The people are repeatedly rejecting Congress' anarchist politics," Nabin said, adding that public trust remained with PM Modi irrespective of whether elections were conducted using EVMs or ballot papers. BJP president Nitin Nabin targeted Congress over its poor performance in the MLC elections, pointing out that voting had taken place using ballot papers. BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi also attacked Rahul Gandhi over his allegations of vote theft "Kamchori ki aadat chhodiye. Vote chori ka shabd apke muh se khud chhoot jayega," he said, asking the Congress leader to give up what he described as a habit of avoiding hard work. Nagpur win gives Congress a chance to respond Congress candidate and sitting MLC Abhijeet Wanjari defeated BJP's Sudhakar Kohale to retain the Nagpur Division Graduates' constituency after more than 40 hours of counting. Kohale had initially taken the lead before Wanjari overtook him through preferential votes. Nagpur is important for the BJP. Besides housing the RSS headquarters, it is associated with Fadnavis and Gadkari, both of whom campaigned for Kohale. The Congress had wrested the seat from the BJP in 2020, when Wanjari defeated Sandip Joshi. By retaining it in 2026, the party prevented the BJP from reclaiming a constituency it had dominated for decades. The Maharashtra Congress also targeted Fadnavis over a social media post in which he had claimed that the party had failed to win a single seat. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh questioned the BJP's setbacks in Nagpur and Varanasi after PM Modi mocked the party's performance in the MLC elections. Sharing a screenshot of what it said was a deleted post by Fadnavis, the party accused him of celebrating before counting was complete. The post had described the Congress's performance as a "big fat zero". The Congress said Fadnavis had been forced to delete the post after the Nagpur result and warned that the outcome was only a trailer of future political battles. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh also responded to PM Modi's remarks, questioning the BJP's losses in Nagpur and Varanasi. "The Prime Minister needs to introspect, but instead, he's lecturing others! Before counting Congress's seats, I wish he'd also reflect on why the BJP lost both seats in his own parliamentary constituency of Varanasi, and how Congress managed to defeat the BJP in RSS's stronghold of Nagpur?" Ramesh said. "Mr. Modi, stop the trolling," he added, accusing the government of failing to address inflation, unemployment and weak private investment. Ramesh claimed that voters in Varanasi, Nagpur, Lucknow, Prayagraj and Patna had expressed dissatisfaction with the Centre's policies. Varanasi setback gives SP a boost ahead of 2027 The BJP's biggest setback in Uttar Pradesh came from Varanasi, where the Samajwadi Party retained the Teachers' seat and established an unassailable lead in the Graduates' constituency. The BJP retained six of the 11 seats contested in the state, while the SP won four and was heading towards a fifth. The SP had won both Varanasi seats in 2020 as well. Six years later, the BJP has failed to dislodge the party from either constituency despite its strong presence in the region. Although the two MLC constituencies cover a wider geographical area than PM Modi's Lok Sabha seat, the results carry political significance given Varanasi's association with the Prime Minister since 2014. They also come after PM Modi's victory margin in Varanasi declined from nearly 4.8 lakh votes in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections to around 1.5 lakh in 2024. Across Uttar Pradesh, the SP's tally is set to rise from three seats in 2020 to five, while the BJP has retained its tally of six. The SP had also emerged as the largest party in Uttar Pradesh in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, winning 37 of the state's 80 parliamentary seats against the BJP's 33. BJP deputy chief minister Keshav Prasad Maurya acknowledged that the party had expected a better performance. "These elections are decided by highly educated and qualified voters. The BJP has repeated its previous performance, but we expected to win more seats. We will examine why we fell short," Maurya said. The SP, meanwhile, has repeatedly accused the BJP of electoral irregularities, allegations the ruling party has rejected. On polling day, Akhilesh Yadav had claimed that the BJP was attempting to influence even the MLC elections, which have a limited electorate. "If the BJP can do this in MLC polls for teachers and graduate constituencies where a limited number of people cast votes, one can imagine their preparation for the assembly polls," he had said. What do the results mean for 2027? The NDA's overall tally shows that the BJP and its allies remain ahead in these Legislative Council contests. But the results in Nagpur and Varanasi also show that the party has struggled to regain certain seats despite its strong presence in both regions. In Uttar Pradesh, the SP and Congress are preparing to contest the 2027 assembly elections together, hoping to build on their performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. Akhilesh Yadav has said the alliance will continue in 2027, although the two parties still need to settle their seat-sharing arrangement. The MLC results, however, cannot be treated as an indication of how the state will vote in the assembly elections. These contests involve a limited electorate of registered graduates and teachers, unlike assembly polls, which are decided by a much wider voter base. For the BJP, which is seeking a third consecutive term in Uttar Pradesh, the challenge will be to counter the opposition's gains. For the SP-Congress alliance, the question is whether it can repeat its 2024 Lok Sabha performance when the state's 403 assembly seats go to the polls in 2027. title: Haryana Congress gears up for Nov 1 rally in Delhi, seeks CECâs resignation
text: AICC general secretary in charge of Haryana Sanjay Dutt and state Congress president Rao Narender Singh address mediapersons on Saturday Chandigarh: Haryana Congress has launched a mobilisation drive for the Nov 1 âVote Bachao, Desh Bachaoâ rally at Delhiâs Ramlila Maidan, demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumarâs resignation and an independent probe into alleged electoral irregularities. They also appealed to farmers, labourers, youth, students, women and other citizens to join the rally. The Congress said the Nov 1 gathering would press for electoral transparency, accountability of the poll panel and protection of every eligible citizenâs right to vote. title: ECI to review UP Assembly poll readiness, 18 districts to be assessed in Meerut on November 2
text: The Election Commission of India is set to convene in Meerut on Monday to evaluate the election preparations (Representative image) LUCKNOW: The Election Commission of India ( ECI ) will review preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections across 18 districts of western UP during a meeting in Meerut on Monday. Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Manish Garg, along with other senior ECI officials, will assess election-related arrangements and the progress made by district administrations. Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Navdeep Rinwa and other senior officials from the CEO's office will also attend the meeting. The review is scheduled to begin at 10.30 am on Monday at Urja Bhawan, the headquarters of Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam, on Jail Chungi Road in Saket, Meerut. The meeting will cover 18 districts falling under the Meerut, Saharanpur, Moradabad and Aligarh divisions. These include Meerut, Baghpat, Bulandshahr, Gautam Buddh Nagar, Ghaziabad, Hapur, Saharanpur, Muzaffarnagar, Shamli, Amroha, Bijnor, Moradabad, Rampur, Sambhal, Aligarh, Etah, Hathras and Kasganj. Divisional commissioners, police commissioners, inspectors general and deputy inspectors general of police, district election officers, senior superintendents of police and superintendents of police from the respective jurisdictions will participate. Officials have been directed to make PowerPoint presentations detailing the progress of election preparations and administrative arrangements in their respective districts. The exercise is part of the Election Commission's preparations ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. title: Centre suspends census in Manipur amid âNRC firstâ demands by Meiteis, Nagas
text: Guwahati: The Centre has now put the entire census in Manipur on hold. Until now, only the house-listing had been kept suspended by Registrar General of India (RGI) since Sept following demand by Meitei and Naga civil societies for compilation of a National Register of Citizens (NRC) first before the population count. The RGI on Friday notified the schedule for the nationwide next phase of Census 2027 starting from Jan 25, but excluded Manipur âtill further declaration,â along with Goa, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Uttarakhand, Ladakh and the snow-bound non-synchronous areas of Himachal Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir. The five states â Manipur, Goa, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Uttarakhand â are headed for assembly elections early in 2027, while Ladakh is preparing for local-body and autonomous hill council polls. The population enumeration in the other states and UTs will be carried out till Feb 28, 2027, followed by a revisional round from March 1 to March 5. Self-enumeration will be open from Jan 10 to 24, before house-to-house enumeration begins. The reference date is 00:00 hours on March 1, 2027. Manipurâs exclusion carries particular weight in the state where the Meitei and Naga civil society organisations want NRC first, citing concerns over alleged illegal immigration, demographic changes and the need for a verified record of the indigenous population. The demand has legislative backing. The Manipur Legislative Assembly adopted a resolution in 2022 seeking the NRC before the census, and reaffirmed it in 2024. On Sept 5, the Manipur high court directed that house-listing be kept in abeyance. The Centreâs decision to defer it came at a meeting between Union home minister Amit Shah and CM Y Khemchand Singh in New Delhi on the same day. title: â200 seats haq hai hamaraâ: Congress puts its UP poll ambitions on Lucknow walls
text: State Congress leaders are said to have framed the 200-seat demand using an âA, B, C, Dâ grading model. LUCKNOW: Posters declaring â200 seat haq hai hamaraâ (200 seats are our right) have appeared outside the Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee (UPCC) headquarters in Lucknow ahead of the 2027 assembly elections. The posters feature photographs of Rahul Gandhi , Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, and Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi. The assertion comes as the Congress has reportedly submitted a wishlist of 200 assembly constituencies to its INDIA alliance partner, the Samajwadi Party (SP). 'A,B,C,D' grading model State Congress leaders are said to have framed the 200-seat demand using an âA, B, C, Dâ grading model based on organisational growth under its nationwide Sangathan Srijan Abhiyan. The demand could complicate seat-sharing negotiations between the two parties, with the SP having emerged as the dominant partner in their alliance in Uttar Pradesh. The state has 403 assembly constituencies, meaning a demand for 200 seats would put Congress in contention for nearly half of them. The posters also reflect a push within the party to seek a larger role in the state rather than continue as the junior partner in the alliance. Congress has sought to build on its performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, when it won six parliamentary seats in Uttar Pradesh. The SP won 37 seats, giving the INDIA bloc a strong showing against the ruling BJP. Congress also led in 38 assembly segments and finished second in another 42 during the general election. Party workers could use these figures to argue for a bigger share of constituencies in 2027. For Congress, the negotiations will involve translating its improved electoral performance into a stronger position within the alliance. For SP, led by Akhilesh Yadav , accommodating the demand could mean giving up a substantial share of constituencies in a state where it has traditionally been the principal opposition force. The display of the posters in Lucknow comes as the Congress is reportedly seeking to conclude seat-sharing talks by mid-November. With the 2027 election looming, the two allies face the challenge of reconciling their respective ambitions while maintaining a united front against the BJP. title: Powering fourth: Karnataka moves up in Indiaâs TOEFL league, leapfrogs Gujarat
text: Karnataka overtakes Gujarat, with 9.3% share of Indiaâs test-takers in FY 2025-26 Bengaluru: Karnataka has overtaken Gujarat to become the fourth-largest state in terms of TOEFL-takers, according to data shared by Educational Testing Service (ETS), which administers the English-language test. The stateâs share of test-takers has seen a consistent increase, up from 8.1% in FY 2023-24 to 8.7% in FY 2024-25 and 9.3% in FY 2025-26. Telangana leads overall with a share of 18.1%, followed by Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh (15.1% each). Karnataka is marginally ahead of Gujarat at 9%. âBengaluru continues to be a significant centre for TOEFL participation. The city ranked fourth among Indiaâs leading TOEFL iBT test-taking cities in 2021 before moving to third place in 2022 and 2023. Mysuru also featured among the countryâs top 10 test-taking cities in 2023,â said Karan Lalit, executive director â South Asia, TOEFL & GRE, ETS. According to ETS, it currently has more than 60 active institutional partners across Karnataka, including Bengaluru, Mangaluru, Mysuru, Hubballi and Dharwad. These partnerships support student outreach, awareness initiatives and access to TOEFL preparation resources. However, access to testing infrastructure remains concentrated in Bengaluru, which has four TOEFL test centres. ETS said it is in discussions with several universities and colleges across Karnataka to strengthen student support, particularly in test preparation and registration. While the US, UK, Canada and Australia continue to be popular choices among Indian students, interest in destinations such as Germany, France, Ireland and countries in the Middle East is also growing. âAt a global level, TOEFL score reports sent to universities in Japan increased by 10% in FY 2025-26, while reports sent to universities in Hong Kong increased by 24% in 2025. These figures reflect global ETS data and should not be interpreted as trends specific to Karnataka,â Lalit said. ETS said students are increasingly evaluating multiple countries before making study-abroad decisions, taking into account visa regulations, affordability, admission requirements, and post-study work opportunities. âGermany enrolled approximately 59,000 Indian students in the 2024-25 winter semester, representing a year-on-year growth of around 20%. France recorded approximately 9,100 Indian students in 2025. Ireland recorded 9,175 Indian students in 2024-25. The Niti Aayog report on internationalisation of higher education also identifies the UAE as a destination for Indian students. These figures illustrate the range of international education markets attracting Indian students,â he said. TOEFL iBT is accepted by more than 13,500 institutions across over 160 countries as a common English-language proficiency assessment when applying to universities in different destinations. title: US midterms 2026: Pooja Sethiâs journey from law and business to Texas politics
text: Meet Pooja Sethi, Indian-American Democrat running for Texas House Pooja Sethi, a Democratic Party candidate, is running for the Texas House of Representatives from District 47 in the November 3, 2026, general election. She advanced from the Democratic primary held on March 3, 2026, and brings experience in law, small business ownership and Democratic Party leadership to the race. Sethi has worked as an attorney and small business owner. She earned a Bachelor of Arts degree from George Washington University and a Juris Doctor degree from Syracuse University. Her political experience includes serving as chief of staff to Texas state Representative Vikki Goodwin and chairing the Travis County Democratic Party. Texas's political landscape Sethi's candidacy comes amid increasingly heated debates in Texas over immigration, demographic change and national identity. The state has one of the largest immigrant populations in the United States, with established communities from Mexico, India, Vietnam, China and other parts of the world. Despite this diversity, Texas has remained firmly Republican at the state level, creating a political environment in which immigration and demographic change are frequently discussed through a conservative lens. Cities such as Austin, Dallas, Houston and San Antonio have attracted skilled workers from across the world. Indian professionals have become increasingly visible in the state's technology, healthcare and business sectors, while Indian students and families have established communities around major cities and universities. Indian-American community and immigration debate The growing visibility of Indian Americans in Texas has also placed the community within wider debates over immigration and the H-1B visa programme. Critics argue that companies rely too heavily on foreign workers, while supporters maintain that skilled immigrants play an important role in the US technology economy. Against this backdrop, Sethi is seeking election to represent District 47 in the Texas House. Her professional background in law and small business, along with her experience in Democratic Party leadership, forms part of her profile as she enters the November general election. title: Six Gujarat RUPPs report over â¹2,692cr in donations over five years
text: Gandhinagar : Six registered unrecognised political parties (RUPPs) in Gujarat reported total donations running into hundreds of crores of rupees over five financial years from 2020-21 to 2024-25, according to data compiled by the independent election watchdog Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) on the partiesâ income, expenditure, donations and electoral performance. Over the past month, Gujarat Police have registered four FIRs against such parties for allegedly receiving massive funds, routing them back to donors in cash via shell entities, and charging a 2% to 10% commission to facilitate tax evasion. According to ADRâs compilation, Bharatiya Rashtriya Janata Dal reported total donations of Rs 0.36 crore in 2020-21, Rs 189 crore in 2021-22, Rs 576.5 crore in 2022-23, Rs 191.6 crore in 2023-24 and Rs 198.8 crore in 2024-25. Its reported donations over the five years totalled Rs 1,156.1 crore. New India United Party reported total donations of Rs 407.5 crore in 2022-23 and Rs 291.6 crore in 2024-25. Its total donation figures for 2020-21, 2021-22 and 2023-24 were unavailable in the compiled data. The partyâs reported cumulative total was Rs 699.1 crore. Swatantra Abhivyakti Party reported nil donations in 2020-21, Rs 75.9 crore in 2021-22 and Rs 395.4 crore in 2022-23. Its total donation figures for 2023-24 and 2024-25 were unavailable. The cumulative figure reported in the document was Rs 75.9 crore. Satyavadi Rakshak Party reported total donations of nil in 2021-22, Rs 85.7 crore in 2022-23 and Rs 330.6 crore in 2023-24. Figures for 2020-21 and 2024-25 were unavailable. Its reported cumulative total was Rs 416.2 crore. Saurashtra Janata Paksh reported zero donations in 2020-21, Rs 131.3 crore in 2021-22, Rs 53.3 crore in 2022-23, Rs 15.9 crore in 2023-24 and Rs 10.8 crore in 2024-25. Its cumulative total was reported at Rs 211.2 crore. Jan Man Party reported total donations of Rs 97.1 crore in 2021-22, Rs 35.3 crore in 2022-23 and Rs 1.2 crore in 2023-24. Its figures for 2020-21 and 2024-25 were unavailable. The document reported its cumulative total at Rs 133.6 crore. The electoral records listed alongside the financial disclosures show that the six parties did not win any seats in Lok Sabha and assembly elections of various states. Shelly Mahajan, research manager at ADR, said that it has been observed that in earlier reports too, unrecognised political parties have received a large number of donations. âThe FIRs are a welcome development, but there is still no clarity on the delisting aspect. Authorities have not specified for how long such entities will remain delisted,â she said. title: BJP plans six mega marches across UP under outreach drive
text: Lucknow: The BJP will launch six mega foot marches across its six organisational regions under the banner of âSave Democracy, Remove Anarchyâ as part of an extensive organisational and voter outreach blueprint in Nov. Presenting the partyâs election preparedness roadmap at the BJPâs state working committee meeting, state general secretary (organisation) Dharampal Singh said each march is expected to draw at least 25,000 party workers, indicating the scale of the mobilisation exercise the party intends to undertake ahead of the crucial assembly polls. The foot marches will begin on Nov 3, with the Awadh regionâs march scheduled in Lucknow in the presence of Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan. On the same day, the Braj region will hold its march in Bareilly, which will be attended by Union minister and former BJP national president JP Nadda. On Nov 4, Gorakhpur regionâs march will be attended by BJP national president Nitin Nabin and state president Pankaj Chaudhary. The Kashi regionâs march in Prayagraj will have deputy chief minister Keshav Prasad Maurya, while deputy CM Brajesh Pathak will participate in the Kanpur regionâs march. Chief minister Yogi Adityanath will lead the western regionâs march in Ghaziabad on Nov 5. Singh assigned a series of responsibilities to party functionaries, laying particular emphasis on maximum voter outreach, effective deployment of workers and strengthening the organisational network at the grassroots. A key component is to identify and deploy a dedicated team of active workers across the partyâs 1,918 organisational mandals. Singh said a list of 25 active workers would be prepared in every mandal from among its nearly 60-member executive committee. These workers would undertake regular visits to all booths falling within their respective mandals. Their names and mobile numbers would be compiled to facilitate accountability and coordination. Similarly, a five-member team of active workers will be constituted at every polling booth. Assembly constituency in charges and assembly-level organisational coordinators, or vistarak, will visit Shakti Kendras to assess and verify the actual state of the partyâs organisational machinery. The exercise will also involve preparing comprehensive databases of serving and former office-bearers, elected representatives, cooperative sector functionaries, workers associated with party wings and cells, and those who have joined the BJP from other parties. Responsibilities will be assigned to them according to their organisational capabilities. The emphasis on identifying active workers and mapping their deployment suggests that the BJP intends to move beyond organisational headcounts to a more targeted system of cadre utilisation and booth-level monitoring. The party has also decided to tap its pool of experienced leaders and former elected representatives to strengthen its election machinery. Social outreach meetings, or samajik chaupals, will be organised, besides assembly-level meetings of leaders who have served as office-bearers for three consecutive terms. The BJP will intensify its beneficiary outreach campaign to establish direct contact with people who have benefited from various welfare schemes of Union and state govts. The outreach will also extend to math and temple establishments, workers associated with the wider Sangh Parivar and influential religious and social leaders. A special drive will target women and young voters, particularly those in the 18-21 age group who will be among the new entrants into the electorate. The BJP will also roll out a dedicated farmer outreach programme through kisan sampark abhiyan, farmer meetings and community feasts with members of cooperative societies. A separate campaign will target small and micro entrepreneurs, with the party planning regular interactions and outreach programmes to address their concerns and keep them connected with the organisation. The election preparedness plan will also define specific responsibilities for mayors, district panchayat chairpersons, Rajya Sabha members, MLCs, MPs, MLAs, the partyâs 2022 assembly election candidates and its 2024 Lok Sabha candidates. UP BJP Plans Tour Calendar for Top Leaders UP BJP state general secretary Dharampal Singh said the party was simultaneously preparing a detailed calendar of proposed visits and public meetings by its top leadership, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi , Union home minister Amit Shah , defence minister Rajnath Singh, chief minister Yogi Adityanath, both deputy chief ministers and state party president Pankaj Chaudhary. The responsibilities for organising meetings during the proposed visits of the national president and home minister, besides programmes involving the chief minister, deputy chief ministers and state president, will be assigned to designated functionaries. Singh asked party leaders to immediately begin preparations after the working committee meeting and ensure that all programmes scheduled for Nov and Dec were completed within the stipulated timelines. title: 'Guilty of centralising electoral rolls': Mallikarjun Kharge lists 6 charges against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, makes 3 demands
text: Kharge accused the CEC of centralising control over electoral rolls and acting at the behest of PM Modi. NEW DELHI: Leader of the opposition in Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge on Saturday accused Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar of facilitating "vote theft" and listed six charges against him at a symbolic "public impeachment" organised by the opposition INDIA bloc. Kharge alleged that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was initiated to remove voters opposed to the BJP. The proceedings began at his residence on Rajaji Marg, with former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar chairing the event. Kharge accused the CEC of centralising control over electoral rolls and acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah. Watch 'Treason': Kharge BLASTS CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Lists 6 Charges At INDIA Bloc's Mock Parliament During the proceedings, Kharge listed six allegations against Kumar: Conspired to steal elections Deleted 13.3 crore voters Rewrote Form 6 without parliamentary oversight or knowledge Seized the electoral rolls through ECINET Breached his constitutional mandate and shut out the two other election commissioners Acted at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Amit Shah Kharge also reiterated the opposition's three demands: The removal of the CEC An end to the SIR exercise Changes to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the chief election commissioner. Kharge also accused PM Modi government of using various means to retain power since 2014, including defections, splitting parties, misuse of central agencies and alleged electoral irregularities. "The proposal we are bringing today is to safeguard the dignity of a constitutional institution. We have no personal enmity with the CEC. Our intention is that the Election Commission should function impartially in keeping with the spirit of the Constitution. The trust of the common man in it should remain intact. No one sitting in Delhi should be able to wrongly delete the voting rights of weaker sections, women, and youth using a computer," Kharge posted on X. He further alleged that the government had repeatedly tried to retain power through various means. "The Modi government has hatched every conspiracy since 2014 to cling to power: stealing MPs, breaking parties, stealing governments, Electoral Bonds, misuse of ED/CBI. And now Vote Theftâcut opposition votes and rule. There are hundreds of examples of Vote Theft," he said. Kharge also criticised the 2023 law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC), alleging that it provided the election commissioner with legal protection. "Gyanesh Kumar is able to carry out this theft because of the 2023 CEC Act. In December 2023, this bill was passed by suspending 145 opposition MPs. This law gives the CEC a lifelong protective shield that even the President and CJI do not have," he added. Questioning the results of the 2024 Maharashtra and Haryana assembly elections, Kharge alleged that the INDIA bloc's strong performance in the Lok Sabha elections was followed by a reversal in the state polls due to electoral irregularities. "In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, we had an excellent performance in Maharashtra and Haryana, but the results flipped in the assembly elections. Reasonâvotes were illegally added before the elections and then all names were removed. This work is being done together by Modi-Shah and Gyanesh," he alleged. title: Like Vanara Sena defeated Ravan, Cong Sena will oust Modi: Revanth
text: Hyderabad: Chief minister A Revanth Reddy on Sunday said just as the 'Vanara Sena' assisted Lord Ram in defeating Ravana, Congressâ own Vanara Sena is now fighting to defeat Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his govt, and they will not rest until victory is achieved. He warned that the protest undertaken by Congress workers at Ramlila Maidan would inevitably lead to the ousting of Narendra Modi from power, forcing him to return to Gujarat. The CM urged party workers to take the message delivered by the leaders of the INDIA Bloc at Ramlila Maidan to every village and household. Addressing Congress workers along with TPCC president B Mahesh Kumar Goud at Telangana Bhavan in New Delhi ahead of the 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachaoâ (Save the Vote, Save the Country) rally at Ramlila Maidan, Revanth alleged that Modi developed a grudge against the poor, Dalits, Adivasis and women for not giving a mandate of 400 seats to BJP in the 2024 elections. Now, the PM was attempting to strip them of their voting rights, he alleged. Already 13.50 crore votes have already been deleted, and there was an attempt to remove another 20 crore votes. âA conspiracy is underway to eliminate votes guaranteed by BR Ambedkar. The conspiracy is to delete 15 to 20% of the total votes. BJP came to power in Bihar, Maharashtra, and West Bengal by systematically deleting votes, and is now conspiring to return to power at the Centre using the same tactic,â Revanth alleged. Revanth alleged that PM Narendra Modi, who rose to power twice by dividing the people along caste and religious lines, had intended to amend the Constitution, abolish reservations, and disenfranchise Dalits, Adivasis and women had the BJP coalition secured over 400 seats in the 2024 elections. The CM mentioned that Rahul Gandhi decided to hold a massive public meeting at Ramlila Maidan, under the aegis of Congress and the INDIA alliance, to counter the conspiracy to remove the names of voters. Revanth criticised PM Modi, alleging that he was attempting to disenfranchise citizens by misusing chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar as a tool to facilitate this move. Revanth lashed out, stating that although trains were arranged to transport 15,000 people from Telangana to the event, they were cancelled at the last minute, despite prior assurances, in an attempt to prevent the party workers from attending the rally. He added that, undeterred, thousands of Congress leaders and workers still reached Delhi. Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah , and Gyanesh Kumar could not break their resolve. The CM asserted that the three were ultimately forced to bow before the strength and the voice of Telangana. title: BFI faction meets Khadse, IOA CEO; demands formation of ad-hoc panel
text: Photo caption: A BFI faction outside IOA headquarters in Delhi on Wednesday NEW DELHI: In a show of strength, a faction of the Boxing Federation of India (BFI) -- which has brought no-confidence motion against president Ajay Singh , on Wednesday claimed the support of 27 of the sports body's 35 state units and eight of its 13 executive committee (EC) members in its bid to bring the regime change. The faction's representatives met union minister of state for sports Raksha Khadse and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) CEO Raghuram Iyer, submitting a memorandum seeking intervention over alleged governance lapses. TOI is in possession of the memorandum, also marked to World Boxing president Gennadiy Golovkin, which calls for corrective measures, including an independent ad-hoc committee and free and fair elections. It also raises concerns over changes to the BFI constitution and the alleged marginalisation of elected office-bearers. Watch Mumbai Indiansâ new coach Luke Williams on Harmanpreet Kaur, WPL auction and plans for 2027 The show of strength came a day after the Punjab and Haryana high court stayed the proposed special general meeting (SGM) and no-trust vote against Singh until the next hearing on Nov 13. The faction said it had appealed against the order before a two-judge bench and was awaiting a decision. Based on the verdict, the faction will again convene and proceed with the no-trust vote against the president. Singh's camp, meanwhile, claimed that it has the backing of 21 authorised state units, which attended a two-day Mission Olympic Podium meeting in Bagdogra. Representatives of 18 units attended in person, while three joined through video conferencing, Singh's faction added. Singh described the participation as evidence of a majority backing the federation's Olympic ambitions. Representatives of the state units subsequently met Iyer. Treasurer Pon Baskaran was among the office-bearers backing the move, along with secretary general Pramod Kumar and other EC members. The confrontation has come amid competing claims over the federation's support base. The rival faction maintained that 27 state units supported its move against Singh, a figure it believed would be sufficient to pursue the no-confidence motion. Out of 35 state units, a clear majority of 23 members or a two-third majority is required for the no-trust vote to succeed. The standoff has intensified the uncertainty surrounding the administration of Indian boxing, with both camps asserting majority support among the federation's state units. title: ECI takes stock of UP poll preparations ahead of 2027
text: The Election Commission of India (ECI) reviews preparations for 2027 UP assembly polls at a meeting in Meerut, attended by bureaucrats of 18 districts of Western UP Meerut: The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Monday reviewed preparations for the 2027 UP assembly elections at a meeting in Meerut, assessing poll preparedness in 18 districts across four divisions -- Meerut, Saharanpur, Moradabad and Aligarh. The meeting, chaired by senior deputy election commissioner Manish Garg, was attended by UP chief electoral officer Navdeep Rinwa and other senior officials from the CEOâs office. Divisional commissioners, police commissioners, inspectors general and deputy inspectors general of police, district election officers, and senior superintendents of police and superintendents of police from the districts concerned also participated. Officials from the 18 districts made presentations on election preparedness, management and administrative arrangements, outlining the progress of measures undertaken so far. âThe Election Commission has taken steps to ensure transparency across all processes, including the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), SSR and continuous updation of electoral rolls,â Garg said. He said the rationalisation of polling stations in UP had been completed as part of the SSR exercise. District magistrates had shared the details with representatives of all political parties, and the proposals had subsequently been forwarded to the CEOâs office and then to the Election Commission. âThe draft electoral roll will be published on Nov 12. Copies will be provided to political parties, while the draft rolls will also be uploaded on the website for public access. Anyone can examine the lists and file objections,â Garg said. He added that the claims and objections process would continue for a month, after which Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) would take final decisions in accordance with the law. The final electoral rolls would also be shared with all political parties and displayed on the official website and at polling stations, he said. The 18 districts covered in the review were Meerut, Baghpat, Bulandshahr, Gautam Budh Nagar, Ghaziabad, Hapur, Saharanpur, Muzaffarnagar, Shamli, Amroha, Bijnor, Moradabad, Rampur, Sambhal, Aligarh, Etah, Hathras and Kasganj. title: ICARâSugarcane Breeding Institute marks 115 years of service to Indian agriculture
text: COIMBATORE: The Indian Council of Agricultural ResearchâSugarcane Breeding Institute (ICARâSBI), Coimbatore, marked its 115th Foundation Day on Tuesday, with Dr Himanshu Pathak, director general of International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT), Hyderabad, attending as chief guest. Addressing the event, Dr Pathak said the instituteâs legacy predates the Indian Council of Agricultural Research and its impact reaches âevery Indian householdâ through sugar. He said more than 80% of Indiaâs sugarcane area is cultivated with ICARâSBIâs âCoâ varieties, highlighting its role in national sugar security. Dr Pathak urged scientists and staffers to pursue selfless, duty-bound work. âAgriculture today faces a changed context driven by advances in science and technology, shifting climate, soil and water constraints, and evolving societal expectations,â he said. He called for innovative, practical research solutions to emerging challenges. Dr Pathak flagged collaboration potential between ICRISAT and ICARâSBI to accelerate sugarcane improvement using advanced genomics, artificial intelligence, precision phenotyping and climate-resilient breeding. He said sugarcaneâs value extends beyond sugar to energy, feed, fuel and pharmaceuticals, and noted the scope for AI tools, including in agricultural extension, alongside new research approaches. In his presidential address, ICARâSBI director P Govindaraj said the institute released three sugarcane varieties in the previous year: Co 18003, a high-quality variety for Peninsular India; Co 21003, a high-yielding variety for Tamil Nadu; and Co 18022, a mid-late maturing variety for the North West Zone. Dr Pathak presented the Sir T S Venkataraman Awards for outstanding research in sugarcane agriculture and the best thesis award for the biennium 2024â25, issued Foundation Day Certificates of Appreciation and released new institute publications. The event drew over 300 participants, including serving and retired staff. title: Karnataka MLC polls: Big setback for DK Shivakumar as BJP-led NDA wins all 4 seats
text: BENGALURU: In a major setback to the ruling Congress and chief minister D K Shivakumar, the BJP-led NDA won all four Karnataka Legislative Council seats that went to polls on October 23, sweeping both teachersâ and graduatesâ constituencies. The NDA fielded three BJP candidates and one JD(S) candidate. JD(S) candidate A P Ranganath defeated Congress veteran and five-time MLC Puttanna in the Bengaluru Teachersâ constituency, while BJP candidate Shashil G Namoshi registered his fifth victory in the North-East Teachersâ constituency, defeating Congress nominee Sharanappa Mattur by 3,297 votes. Namoshi secured 15,596 first-preference votes against Matturâs 12,299. Counting concluded at Kalaburagi, where around 30,253 voters had exercised their franchise. Of the votes counted, 28,380 were valid, while 1,873 were rejected. In the graduatesâ constituencies, BJP candidates SV Sankanur and KM Suresh also emerged victorious, completing the NDAâs clean sweep of all four seats. In the West Graduatesâ constituency, Sankanur secured his third consecutive victory, defeating Congress rival Mohan Limbikai. In the other graduatesâ constituency, BJP candidate KM Suresh won the seat, ensuring that the NDA did not concede any ground to the ruling party in the elections. This is the second biennial legislative council election since Shivakumar became chief minister on June 3. In the June 18 elections to seven council seats from the MLAsâ quota, Congress won five seats and the BJP secured two. However, the ruling party failed to replicate that performance in the teachersâ and graduatesâ constituencies. Ranganath won the Bengaluru Teachersâ constituency on his third attempt, defeating Puttanna by 908 votes. He secured 10,810 first-preference votes against Puttannaâs 9,902. Ranganath had lost to Puttanna in the 2022 and 2024 elections. This time, he capitalised on a sympathy wave to secure victory. Puttanna had contested as a BJP candidate in 2022 before switching to Congress for the 2024 by-election. title: Kamala Harris returns to campaign trail for US midterms amid speculation over 2028 presidential bid
text: Former US vice president Kamala Harris. Former US vice president Kamala Harris has returned to the campaign trail to support Democrats in closely contested races ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, as speculation grows over whether she will make another bid for the White House in 2028. According to news agency Reuters, Harris, the Democratic Party's 2024 presidential nominee, is campaigning in Georgia, Mississippi, Nevada, New Hampshire and Wisconsin. She has made relatively few public appearances this year but is now stepping up efforts to help Democrats challenge Republican control of Congress. Harris began her campaign tour in Las Vegas on Tuesday, criticising President Donald Trump and his administration over what she described as its cruelty and incompetence. Speaking alongside Nevada gubernatorial candidate Aaron Ford, she addressed members of the Culinary Workers Union. "We got a serious fight in front of us," Harris said, accusing the Trump administration of being corrupt, callous and incompetent. Ford, Nevada's first Black attorney general, is seeking to become the state's governor. Harris said his election would make him the first Black governor west of the Mississippi River. Harris continued her campaign appearances in Mississippi, where she rallied supporters of Democratic Senate candidate Scott Colom in Columbus. Colom is attempting to become the first Democrat elected to the US Senate from Mississippi since 1982. He is facing Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith in a closely contested race, Reuters reported. Addressing supporters, Harris encouraged young people not to let others' doubts limit their ambitions, drawing cheers from the crowd. Harris' popularity remains divided along party lines Harris' return to the campaign trail comes as both parties seek to mobilise voters ahead of the midterms. Trump has also been travelling across the country to campaign for Republican candidates facing competitive races. However, Harris continues to face challenges in winning support beyond the Democratic base. A Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted in June found that 39 per cent of Americans viewed her favourably. Her approval was significantly higher among Democrats, at 82 per cent, compared with 7 per cent among Republicans and 33 per cent among independents. Elaine Kamarck, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution and a member of the Democratic National Committee, said parties typically turn to their most prominent figures towards the end of an election campaign. "At the end of a campaign, you bring out your heavy hitters," Kamarck was quoted as saying by Reuters, adding that this was the reason Harris and Trump were campaigning for their respective parties. Will Harris run for president again in 2028? Harris could emerge as one of the leading contenders if she decides to seek the Democratic presidential nomination in 2028. However, her political record includes two unsuccessful presidential campaigns. She lost to Trump in the 2024 election, while her first presidential campaign ended before the Democratic primaries began in 2020. A potential 2028 bid would also bring renewed scrutiny of the events surrounding the 2024 election, when then-president Joe Biden abandoned his re-election campaign amid concerns about his age and mental fitness, leaving Harris to take his place as the Democratic nominee. Harris later criticised Biden's decision to seek a second term as "reckless" in her memoir, 107 Days, named after the length of the presidential campaign she inherited. She has also become more vocal about the Biden administration's approach to Israel's war in Gaza. This month, Harris criticised the Israeli government's "horrific conduct" and said the US should have acted sooner and more forcefully. Harris says 2026 midterms come first Harris has not ruled out another presidential run, but she has repeatedly emphasised the importance of the upcoming midterm elections. During an appearance on the video podcast Baby, This Is Keke Palmer this month, actor Keke Palmer asked Harris whether she would run for president again. "Oh, girl, come on!" Harris replied, laughing. "I haven't decided yet." She then stressed that the immediate priority was the midterm elections. "2028 don't matter if we don't do 2026 right," Harris said. Her return to the campaign trail is likely to keep her in the political spotlight as Democrats seek to regain congressional ground and potential candidates begin positioning themselves for the next presidential election. title: US midterms: Five flashpoints election officials are watching as America votes
text: File photo: US midterm elections 2026 As Americans prepare to vote in the November 3 midterm elections, state and local officials are bracing for possible disruptions ranging from federal intervention at polling places to challenges over voter eligibility and the handling of ballots. The concerns follow a series of unprecedented moves by Trumpâs administration to increase federal control over elections, including demands for unredacted voter rolls, efforts to restrict mail-in voting and investigations targeting people suspected of voting as noncitizens. Courts have blocked several of these initiatives, but election officials and voting rights experts say the administrationâs actions have added uncertainty ahead of polling day. In a report published on Monday, investigative newsroom ProPublica identified five areas that voting experts and election officials are watching: possible federal interference, challenges to alleged noncitizen voters, problems with voting procedures, election security and disputes over results after voting ends. The administration has not explicitly ruled out sending federal agents to polling places or seizing ballots and voting machines. Election officials, however, say they have been preparing for such possibilities while stressing that there is no evidence of a planned federal operation that would prevent voters from casting their ballots. Could federal agents intervene at polling places? An incident in Floridaâs Leon County last month heightened concerns over federal law enforcement at polling sites. Mark Earley, the countyâs supervisor of elections, told ProPublica he was âfuriousâ when two marked US Customs and Border Protection vehicles appeared outside the countyâs busiest early-voting location, despite repeated assurances that federal agents would stay away. Earley alerted the FBI, but later learnt the agents had stopped to vote while travelling out of state. He said their use of official vehicles showed âpretty bad judgmentâ. Washington Attorney General Nick Brown told ProPublica that state officials and voting rights groups had rehearsed responses to possible federal attempts to seize ballots or voting equipment. âWeâve seen the tension and chaos thatâs in the air,â he said, calling the federal government âthe biggest challenge to smooth elections right nowâ. The Justice Department said its election monitors would follow the law, though officials in Wyoming raised concerns after monitors questioned poll workers about their training and sought to inspect voting systems. Could noncitizen voter investigations affect eligible voters? The Trump administrationâs efforts to identify suspected noncitizen voters have raised fears that eligible US citizens could be wrongly removed from voter rolls or discouraged from voting, according to voting rights groups cited by ProPublica. The Justice Department has sued California over more than 20,000 people it considers âlikelyâ to be noncitizens, seeking to prevent their ballots from being counted. California called the allegation âspeciousâ, while a Los Angeles County analysis found that many people on the list were not registered there or had never voted; some had said they were born in the US. Courts rejected the departmentâs bid to block the ballots and later restrained its demand for records from California officials, describing it as an âintimidation planâ. The department also threatened legal action against Washington state over a list of 400 suspected noncitizens. Secretary of state Steve Hobbs called the list unreliable, saying it included citizens, unregistered people and duplicate entries. Sam Trepel of the States United Democracy Center described the departmentâs actions as a âdisturbing use of prosecutorial authorityâ. Voting rights advocates warn that the investigations could deter eligible citizens from voting. The Department of Homeland Security said it was not planning operations targeting polling places, adding that ICE would only make arrests there in response to safety threats. A spokesperson said the DHS and Justice Department remained focused on identifying and prosecuting noncitizens who vote in US elections. Could changes to voting rules and systems cause problems? Changes to voting laws and administrative systems have raised concerns about ballot rejections and hurdles for voters. In North Carolina, new rules require mail-in voters to provide identification and seal two envelopes, with Democracy Docket reporting a sharp rise in rejections over incorrectly sealed inner envelopes. Texas and other states have reduced or relocated polling sites. Tarrant County, for instance, cut its polling locations by nearly a third, potentially increasing queues and confusion, ProPublica reported. Texas also faced registration-system errors that delayed hundreds of thousands of applications, though county officials said the backlogs had been addressed. Meanwhile, election experts told ProPublica that isolated complaints about touch-screen voting machines do not indicate tampering. Manufacturer ES&S said it had received no widespread reports of problems, while experts said attempts to alter machine programming would be detected during pre-election testing. How vulnerable are election systems to cyber and physical attacks? Security concerns have grown after suspicious packages and false bomb threats targeted election offices. Last month, officials in several states, including Arizona, received envelopes containing white powder, later found to be non-toxic in Arizona. During the 2024 election, false bomb threats believed to have originated abroad forced evacuations at vote-counting sites, with a CISA-funded message board helping officials respond after the FBI deemed them non-credible. ProPublica reported that Trumpâs dismantling of CISA has left state and local officials with less federal support, prompting nonprofits and states to take on a larger role in election security. Brennan Center for Justiceâs Derek Tisler said states lack the capacity to manage these threats alone. Could the results face legal challenges after voting? Election lawyers fear the administrationâs actions before the midterms could be followed by legal challenges after voting. The Justice Department sued Alaska to block certification of its Senate result if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan loses, arguing that a second candidate with the same name could confuse voters. A federal judge dismissed the case on Sunday, but the administration is expected to appeal. Trump said he ordered the lawsuit, while The New York Times reported that aides to Democratic nominee Mary Peltola had helped organise the second candidateâs run. The intervention is unusual because federal law bars government interference in an active election, with challenges typically brought by losing candidates in state courts after voting. Washington Attorney General Nick Brown told ProPublica the case amounted to federal interference in the electoral process. Officials are also preparing for local boards to refuse certification over fraud allegations, while some lawyers fear Trump could pressure Congress to block newly elected Democrats from taking their seats. Legal experts cited by ProPublica said an incoming Democratic majority and the courts could resist such an effort, though it might cause temporary delays. Officials prepare for worst-case scenarios Across the country, state and local election officials have spent months training poll workers, coordinating with law enforcement and preparing legal responses in case federal agents or private groups attempt to disrupt voting. Election officials have also warned that threats and allegations of fraud could increase the risk of intimidation and violence against poll workers. Matt Crane, executive director of the Colorado County Clerks Association, told CNN that officials were under pressure because even a minor mistake could be amplified into a national disinformation campaign. Arizona Secretary of State Adrian Fontes said the administrationâs threats could themselves intimidate voters, but stressed that officials had not seen evidence of a planned disruption that would prevent people from voting. He said preparations were precautionary and should not deter people from going to the polls. Election officials have spent months preparing to run the 2026 vote, but the scale of those preparations reflects concerns that the challenges may extend beyond Election Day and into the counting and certification of results. title: Civic polls to test NDAâs popularity, YSRCPâs revival bid in Visakhapatnam
text: The election is being closely watched as results in a politically neutral city such as Vizag are often seen as an indication of public mood. Pic: SS Vijay Babu Visakhapatnam : The Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) election on Su nda y, Nov 1, is set to witness a keen contest between the NDA and YSRCP. The mayor seat has been allocated to the TDP as part of the seat-sharing arrangement among the TDP, BJP and Jana Sena . The election is being closely watched as results in a politically neutral city such as Vizag are often seen as an indication of public mood. The verdict is expected to offer insights into perceptions of the TDP-led govtâs performance, which will complete two and a half years in Dec, and oppositionâs role. With a sizeable, educated and politically aware electorate, the city is also expected to send a message on governance and civic issues. While the outcome in individual wards has attracted limited attention, the main focus is on the two mayoral candidates and the message voters may deliver through their mandate. The TDP is looking to continue its winning streak from the 2024 elections, when it secured a nearly five lakh majority in the Vizag MP constituency. The YSRCP, meanwhile, is equally determined to win the mayorâs post. The TDP has fielded first-time corporator Mukka Sravani, while the YSRCP has nominated senior politician and MLC Varudu Kalyani. The election has also become a prestige battle for the MLAs, as most corporator candidates are their loyalists. The MLAs played a key role in securing tickets for their supporters, making the civic polls a test of their political influence. The ticket distribution has also led to rebel candidates entering the fray, including those who have worked in their respective wards for years or had high hopes of securing party nominations. The seat-sharing arrangement among NDA partners has not gone down well with a section of their cadre. With the TDP winning all assembly seats and the two Lok Sabha constituencies partly falling under GVMC limits in 2024, local MLAs and MPs have campaigned aggressively in their respective areas. The YSRCP, which faced relatively fewer internal disputes over seat allocation, focused on reaching out to voters. Its mayoral candidate, Varudu Kalyani, a seasoned politician, actively campaigned across the city. Though 15 candidates are in the race for the mayorâs post, the main contest is between the TDP and YSRCP. The two parties have also adopted contrasting approaches in their manifestos. The NDA has focused on infrastructure development and improved civic services, while the YSRCP has centred its campaign on the âSave Vizagâ theme and pollution- and environment-related concerns. The NDA has listed nine commitments, including better drinking water supply, underground drainage, roads and street lighting. The YSRCP pledged to address drinking water shortages by improving reservoirs and ensuring a regular supply. It also promised to revive 12 proposed flyover projects, improve roads and drainage, upgrade 42 urban health centres and introduce a grievance redressal app. YSRCP mayoral candidate Varudu Kalyani said the party would protect the cityâs natural resources, environment, public assets and heritage, while ensuring that residents are not burdened with additional taxes. âWe will develop Vizag to place it among the top cities in the country. The TDP has failed to fulfil its promises even after 30 months in power,â she said. TDP mayoral candidate Mukka Sravani said a mandate for the alliance would accelerate development and improve civic services in Vizag. âIf elected, I will consider the position an opportunity to serve the people and take the city forward on all fronts,â said the former corporator. Main contest between the NDA and YSRCP. 573 candidates contesting for 120 corporator positions. Election material distribution centres established in all 10 zones. Gajuwaka has the highest number of polling stations at 329. 82 returning officers and assistant returning officers appointed for election duties. title: 5th term for Harjinder Singh Dhami or Bibi Jagir Kaurâs return? SGPC to elect president on Nov 20
text: In the 2025 SGPC presidential election, Dhami (L) secured 107 of the 142 votes polled during the general house meeting. Jagir Kaur (R), who also contested for the post, received 33 votes. AMRITSAR: Will Harjinder Singh Dhami secure a fifth consecutive term as Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) president, or will the November 20 election bring a change of guard? Amid growing discontent over the SGPCâs management, insiders said an impression was being created that Dhami was no longer keen to continue as president. Meanwhile, speculation that former SGPC president Bibi Jagir Kaur could return to the Badal-led Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and reclaim the top post has added another dimension to the electoral contest. Jagir Kaur had parted ways with the Sukhbir Singh Badal-led SAD and joined the Shiromani Akali Dal (Punar Surjit). The SGPC executive committee met on Friday and convened a general house session at 12 noon on November 20 at Teja Singh Samundri Hall, the committeeâs headquarters, to elect its president and other office-bearers for the coming year. A senior Akali source said the election could prove a significant political test for the Sukhbir-led SAD, which holds a majority in the SGPC general house, particularly as the party seeks to consolidate its position ahead of the 2027 assembly elections. âThe central question is whether Dhami will secure a fifth consecutive term as SGPC president or whether the SAD leadership will spring a surprise by bringing another face,â sources said, adding that Jagir Kaur could also return to the top post despite having left the Badal-led SAD for SAD (Punar Surjit). In the 2025 SGPC presidential election, Dhami secured 107 of the 142 votes polled during the general house meeting. Jagir Kaur, who also contested for the post, received 33 votes. Panthic affairs expert Jagdeep Singh said Dhami had remained relatively less controversial than his predecessor, Jagir Kaur. âDhamiâs decisions have generally received wide appreciation, whereas Jagir Kaurâs tenure was marked by several controversies,â he said. Jagdeep added that Dhamiâs relatively low-profile functioning and ability to maintain working relations within Panthic circles could work in his favour. However, he said the outcome would also depend on political equations within the SAD and the choices made by its leadership. Another source did not rule out a possible rapprochement between the two Akali factions, which could open up fresh possibilities for the SGPC leadership. Recent reports of discussions involving SAD (Punar Surjit) leaders over a possible broader Akali-BJP political arrangement for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections have added another dimension to the developments. However, there is no confirmed agreement on the return of any particular leader to the Badal-led SAD or on a possible SGPC candidature. title: Jharkhand tennis association appeals against voting rights to Goa, Rajasthan
text: Pune: The Jharkhand Tennis Association (JTA) has filed an intervening application in the Delhi High Court against the All India Tennis Associationâs decision to promote Goa and Rajasthan from associate to affiliate membership with voting rights during the Annual General Meeting on September 30. The JTA said that it was not against conferring affiliate membership on Goa and Rajasthan itself, but objected to the manner in which was done and that the two state unitsâ voting rights must be suspended until the matter is adjudicated upon by the court. Chintan Parikh, the AITA interim president, however, said that denying the two associations their voting rights would have been âunfairâ. AITA, which is at present governed by an interim committee supervised by an Administrator appointed by the Delhi HC, is scheduled to hold its elections on November 27. In its appeal, the JTA has argued that the matter was not listed on the agenda for the AGM, which was originally supposed to be an Extraordinary General Meeting, and the promotion of Goa and Rajasthan added four votes â two votes for each association â to the electoral college. Given that the election process was already underway and that Parikh was a prospective candidate, the decision without prior notice raised concerns over fairness of the election process, the JTA said in its application. Parikh indeed announced on Sunday (November 1) his decision to contest for president in alliance with the legendary Leander Paes, who currently heads the Bengal association and will stand for vice president. Parikh said that Goa and Rajasthan had completed the mandatory two-year period of associateship to be eligible for affiliate membership and the decision to promote them was approved unanimously by the General Body. âRajasthan and Goa have completed their mandatory period of two years as associated Affiliates. They sent us an application to be come full state affiliates,â Parikh said in a statement to The Times of India. âThe matter was to go to AGM in November. Due to legal provision in the constitution, annual accounts need to be passed in AGM and that too before September 30th. Hence, we decided to convert the September meeting as AGM. âA communication was sent in advance about it to the members. In an EGM only the mentioned agenda can be discussed, while in the AGM any agenda with permission of the Chair can be discussed. Yes, we could have placed the matter in agenda but that does not change the legal position of the matters that can be discussed in AGM. âThere were 28 out of 30 states present. All of them unanimously approved the matter, because it was not a matter with any hidden agenda. âWhat is unanimously approved by the General Body, a lone state who was absent cannot and should not challenge, whether the matter was an agenda item or not. âThe spirit was not to deprive two states of their voting rights until 2030. This would have been very unfair,â he said. With regard to JTAâs specific claim that Parikhâs decision was âaimed at manipulating the elections by attempting to secure favourable votesâ from Goa and Rajasthan, Parikh said: âThey may vote for anybody. They are independent affiliates. They are given the voting power by the General Body and not by the President. It is a foolish hypothesis.â The matter is expected to be heard on November 6. title: 25 in fray for 7 PUTA posts, final list of candidates out
text: Representational image Patna : The battle lines have been drawn for the Patna University Teachersâ Association (PUTA) elections, with 25 teachers in the fray for seven key posts after the final list of valid candidates was published on Wednesday following scrutiny and withdrawal of nominations. title: Punjab tennis secretary quits amid financial irregularities allegations
text: In a development with major implications for the All India Tennis Association (AITA), interim committee treasurer Dinesh Arora has resigned as secretary general of his home state association, the Punjab State Lawn Tennis Association (PSLTA), following allegations of financial irregularities. Aroraâs resignation came during an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) of the PSLTA in Amritsar on Thursday (Oct. 29, 2026), where a proposal to remove him from office was the principal agenda item. The development followed a letter written earlier this year by senior vice-president Karanbir Singh Osahan to president Anirudh Gupta, highlighting complaints raised by finance secretary Deepak Mittal regarding Aroraâs âacts and omissionsâ in his âfiduciary capacityâ. Osahan had also questioned Aroraâs nomination to represent the PSLTA on the AITA executive committee and his subsequent election as treasurer of the national federation, alleging that Arora had not received authorisation from the state association for the same. Subsequently, a group of PSLTA office-bearers filed a complaint with the Amritsar police commissioner, seeking registration of an FIR against Arora for âcriminal breach of trust, cheating, criminal misappropriation and embezzlement of association funds and government grants ... and criminal conspiracyâ. Faced with strong opposition, Arora pre-empted his removal by stepping down during Thursdayâs EGM. âMr Dinesh Arora has resigned as Secretary General amid opposition from a majority of members to his continuation in office during the pendency of a criminal complaint against him before the Commissioner of Police, Amritsar,â the PSLTA said in a statement. âMr Arora, who also serves as Treasurer of the interim committee of the All India Tennis Association (AITA), has been asked to resign from that position with immediate effect, in view of the pending criminal complaint and concerns regarding his continuation in sports administration while the matter remains under examination,â the PSLTA added. âAs part of the steps towards transparency and accountability, an independent forensic audit of the PSLTAâs financial affairs shall be undertaken and completed within the next 30 days. âMr Karanbir Singh Osahan has been appointed Secretary of the PSLTA.â âAITA INTERIM COMMITTEE HAS TO BE DISSOLVEDâ Following the development, sports lawyer Prasang Raheja called for the dissolution of the AITA interim committee. âMeaningful reform cannot remain confined to the state level. It is time for the AITA Interim Committee to be dissolved with immediate effect,â Raheja said in a press release. âInterim arrangements must not become a substitute for accountable administration. âIndian tennis requires structural reform, independent financial scrutiny and a governance framework that commands the confidence of its stakeholders. âThe present moment offers an opportunity to address the systemic issues affecting the administration of the sport. âAccountability, transparency and playersâ interests must come first. The time has come for decisive institutional reform in Indian tennis.â You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Pune | Silver Rate in Pune | Bank Holidays in Pune | Public Holidays in Pune | Petrol Price in Pune | Diesel Price in Pune | CNG Price in Pune | LPG Price in Pune Stay updated with the latest Pune news. title: US midterms 2026: Indian-American Democrat Aruna Miller seeks re-election as Maryland Lt Governor alongside Wes Moore
text: Aruna Miller Indian-origin politician Aruna Miller is seeking another term as Marylandâs lieutenant governor, running alongside Democratic Governor Wes Moore in the November 3 US midterm elections. Born in Hyderabad, Miller made history in 2023 as Marylandâs first Asian American lieutenant governor and the first woman of colour to hold the office. Miller and Moore are seeking re-election after taking office in January 2023. The Democratic ticket advanced through the partyâs primary on June 23, setting up a general election contest against Republican gubernatorial candidate Dan Cox and his running mate. Miller has made education, childhood poverty and affordability key themes of her campaign. In a statement announcing the re-election bid, she said she wanted to continue improving public schools and help more families afford to live in Maryland. âI am thrilled to stand alongside Governor Wes Moore as we launch our campaign to continue the work to make our public schools the best in America, to end childhood poverty once and for all, and to make sure more Marylanders can afford to live here, buy a home, create wealth for their families, and live a secure middle-class life,â Miller said. From Hyderabad to Maryland politics Millerâs journey into public service began long before she entered elected office. She studied civil engineering at the University of Missouri and earned a bachelorâs degree in Technology in 1989, before entering public service in Maryland. She has been elected to public office twice: first to the Maryland House of Delegates, where she represented District 15 from 2011 to 2019, and later as lieutenant governor in 2022. Her election to the stateâs second-highest office marked a milestone in Maryland politics. Miller joined Moore, who became the stateâs first Black governor, on a ticket that won the 2022 general election with 64.5% of the vote, defeating Republican Dan Cox, who received 32.1%. The pair assumed office in January 2023, becoming Marylandâs executive leadership team. Millerâs role has placed her among Indian-origin politicians serving in senior elected positions in the United States. Miller pushes back against Trump over ballot error Earlier this year, Miller defended Marylandâs election officials after President Donald Trump called for a Justice Department investigation into incorrect mail-in ballots sent to some voters ahead of the stateâs primary elections. Trump accused Governor Moore of allowing the error to benefit Democrats, but Miller told Fox News Digital that the state election board operated independently of the governorâs administration. âI think it was just an error by the vendor,â Miller said, rejecting claims of deliberate wrongdoing. Maryland election officials attributed the mistake to their mail-ballot printing vendor and said safeguards were in place to prevent duplicate voting. Trump said he had asked the Justice Department to investigate, but the department had not publicly announced an investigation. A joint campaign focused on families and affordability Moore has highlighted reducing costs, lowering crime and addressing unemployment as priorities in his re-election campaign. He has also criticised President Donald Trumpâs administration over federal job cuts, Medicaid and rising prices for household essentials. Millerâs campaign statement points to public education, childhood poverty and the cost of living as key areas for the next term. title: Fireworks, flags and celebrations as student-led movement wins in Serbia; can they deliver reforms?
text: In Serbia, can a leaderless student movement, with little experience of governing, turn its electoral victory into lasting political change? Celebrations swept across Serbia after Gen Z-backed candidates defeated president Aleksandar Vucicâs ruling party in a historic election, ending his long grip on power. In Belgrade, crowds filled central squares, cars draped in Serbian flags honked their horns and fireworks lit up the sky as jubilant protesters dismantled barricades around a pro-government encampment near parliament. But beyond the celebrations, a key question remains: Can a leaderless student movement, with little experience of governing, turn its electoral victory into lasting political change? Watch ON CAM: Celebrations & Chaos! Political Earthquake In Serbia As Vucic Loses; Serbia Streets Go Wild The election follows nearly two years of student-led demonstrations sparked by the collapse of a canopy at the Novi Sad railway station in 2024, which killed 16 people. Protesters blamed corruption and cronyism for the disaster, turning the tragedy into a wider campaign for accountability. From street protests to political power Visuals circulating on social media showed crowds taking to the streets of Belgrade and other Serbian cities soon after the election results were announced. The student movement built nationwide support without a single leader and eventually fielded 250 candidates, including academics, lawyers, doctors, farmers, actors and musicians. Its agenda centres on anti-corruption measures, judicial reform and stronger public institutions. The candidates have proposed an independent police unit accountable to prosecutors, transparent appointments to state-owned companies and tighter scrutiny of public infrastructure contracts. However, unity could prove difficult once the movement begins governing. â(The student movement created) such a shift in Serbia's culture; we will just have to see if it lasts,â Katarina Popovic, a professor at the University of Belgrade told news agency Reuters. âWe just hope that there are big goals that can keep them together long enough to deconstruct the system,â she added. Can the new government deliver reforms? Under Serbiaâs constitution, the student-backed candidates have 90 days to form a government after parliament is convened following the announcement of final election results. The immediate challenges include passing a year-end budget, addressing rising public and private debt, reforming the police and intelligence services, and strengthening the judiciary. The students' victory "is likely to trigger broad institutional and policy changes centred on anti-corruption, the rule of law, and better public services. However, bureaucratic resistance to reforms and the movementâs limited governing experience could make the transition challenging," Teneo Global Research said in a report on Monday. The IMF projects Serbiaâs economy to grow 3 per cent in 2026 and 4 per cent in 2027, while inflation rose to 4.1 per cent in September from 2.2 per cent in August. The central bank has held its benchmark interest rate at 5.75 per cent since 2024. âThe new government would have to fight its corner,â warned Bozo Prelevic, a Belgrade-based lawyer and former co-minister of the interior, referring to the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), which is expected to remain a formidable opposition force. The movement has also promised economic changes, including action against retail monopolies to lower food prices, tax relief for lower-income groups, affordable housing initiatives and cheaper medicines. Kosovo, Russia and the European Union Foreign policy could be another test. The student-backed candidates oppose recognising Kosovoâs independence, declared in 2008, while relations with the European Union remain strained over stalled accession talks and the need to normalise ties with Pristina. The movement has also said it does not intend to impose sanctions on Russia, Serbiaâs traditional ally and a major gas supplier. At the same time, the European Commission has offered support for reforms involving the rule of law and media freedom. âI am sure (the Student List) will find a way, just as they have so far, to choose someone capable of governing,â said Savo Manojlovic of the student-friendly Move-Change movement, according to Reuters.
