title: 4 lakh voters aged above 85 years across Karnataka
text: Belagavi district has the highest number of voters and tops the list in Karnataka Mysuru: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has identified nearly four lakh voters aged above 85 years across Karnataka , with five southern districts accounting for about 17% of the total. Belagavi district, which has 18 assembly constituencies, has the highest number of voters aged 85 years and tops the list in Karnataka. Mysuru is second with 25,165 such voters, followed closely by Tumakuru with 24,665, placing these three districts in the top three in terms of senior citizen voter concentration. Mandya has 16,263 voters in the 85+ category, while Hassan has 15,923 in fourth and fifth places. To ensure greater inclusion, the ECI introduced home voting for the first time in a Lok Sabha election in 2024, extending the facility to voters above 85 years of age and persons with disabilities (PwDs) with 40% benchmark disability. The option is meant for those who face difficulties in visiting a polling station. The eligible voters must inform polling officials in advance to avail themselves of home voting. Karnataka has a substantial number of elderly voters Karnataka, which has 224 assembly constituencies, has 33,92,134 voters as per ECI data. Alongside the large overall electorate, the state has a substantial number of elderly voters, requiring targeted planning at the booth level. ECIâs arrangements for home voting add an additional layer of coordination for election officials, particularly in districts with a higher concentration of 85+ voters. Dakshina Kannada and Kalaburagi have more than 14,000 voters each in this age group. Bengaluru Urban has around 13,007, while Dharwad has 10,117 and Bengaluru South has 10,443. Among the smaller districts in this category, Chamarajanagar has 7,943 elderly voters and Kodagu has 4,044. Mysuru illustrates the operational scale required to implement home voting smoothly. The district accounts for about 6.4% of Karnatakaâs 85+ voter base, and officials have to identify and facilitate eligible voters across nearly 2,900 polling booths in 11 assembly constituencies. This requires advance communication, verification and logistical deployment to ensure that home voting is conducted securely and within election rules, while also enabling elderly voters and PwDs to participate with dignity and minimal physical hardship. title: Council poll results raise alarm for GA, open space for JSP
text: Policemen stand guard at a counting centre in Patna on Tuesday Patna : The NDA âs performance in the Oct 23 legislative council elections is certainly a morale booster for CM Samrat Choudhary and JD(U) chief Nitish Kumar âs heir apparent Nishant Kumar, but the results declared on Tuesday may sound an alarm bell to the Grand Alliance (GA) comprising RJD, Congress and Left. The results may also give space to Prashant Kishor âs Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) as people opposed to the BJP look for an alternative, as they did in Bankipur. Prashant, who recently defeated the BJP in its stronghold Bankipur assembly byelection, has been trying to emerge as an alternative to traditional political parties at a time when Gen Z is agitated over the lack of jobs and employment opportunities in the country in general and Bihar in particular. Though graduate and teacher council constituencies are small compared with the electorate in assembly polls, the fact that candidates and voters were either graduates or teachers and considered publicly aware people with discerning judgment made the results significant. While Prashant campaigned for his candidates, RJD national working president and party face Tejashwi Prasad Yadav was conspicuous by his absence during electioneering. The JSP, for the first time since its formation in 2024, contested council polls and fielded candidates on all eight seats at stake. It not only won the Darbhanga Teachersâ seat by defeating sitting Congress MLC Madan Mohan Jha, but also garnered either more or only a few votes fewer than the runners-up in the remaining constituencies. Though RJD had no MLC in any of the eight constituencies in the Oct 23 polls, it was the main opposition party in the last elections. RJD contested seven seats, leaving the Tirhut Teachersâ constituency for ally CPI, which could not retain the seat this time. Congress fielded candidates on five seats, while CPI(M) and CPI(ML) also contested one seat each. Of the eight seats, the NDA held three â Kosi Graduates and Patna Teachers (BJP), and Patna Graduates (JD(U)) â while independent candidates had won three: Tirhut Graduates, Darbhanga Graduates and Saran Teachers. CPI and Congress held Tirhut Teachers and Darbhanga Teachers respectively. A Prashant Kishor-backed candidate, Afaque Ahmad, had won the Saran Teachersâ seat in 2023, giving his campaign its first taste of electoral success. But Afaque lost to independent Rahul Raj, a BJP rebel, this time. title: Speaker accepts resignations of Pathanmajra, Kunwar Vijay Partap; declares their seats vacant
text: Punjab assembly speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan Chandigarh: Punjab assembly speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan has accepted the resignations of former AAP MLAs Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Kunwar Vijay Partap Singh, and declared their assembly seats vacant with effect from Nov 2. Chetan Singh Jouramajra, who resigned from the AAP but not from the assembly, has been summoned by the Speaker for a hearing on Nov 5 after a representation by AAP chief whip Baljinder Kaur sought action against him under the anti-defection law. According to a notification issued by the Punjab assembly secretariat on Monday, Sanour MLA Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Amritsar North legislator Kunwar Vijay Partap Singh submitted their resignations on Nov 1. âKunwar Vijay Partap and Pathanmajra have resigned as per Article 190 (3) (b) of the Constitution on Nov 1,â read the notification. Their resignations were accepted by the speaker and seats were declared vacant with effect from Nov 2. In Jouramajraâs case, Sandhwan initiated proceedings after receiving a representation from Baljinder Kaur alleging that he had joined another political party. An official said the speaker issued a notice to Jouramajra, asking him to submit his response by Nov 5. Replying to a query, the speaker said he had summoned Jouramajra after receiving a representation from the AAP chief whip. He pointed out that the 10th Schedule of the Constitution provides for unseating an MLA if he quits the party on whose ticket he was elected. Earlier in the day, Kunwar Vijay Partap and Pathanmajra posted their resignations from the membership of Punjab Vidhan Sabha on Facebook. AAP leadership said all three functionaries had been suspended from the party over alleged anti-party activities. Kunwar Vijay Partap Singh was suspended from the AAP for five years in June last year for alleged anti-party activities. On Sunday, in a letter to Punjab AAP president Aman Arora, Kunwar Vijay Partap wrote, âThis is to bring to your kind notice that I have tendered my resignation as a member of the Punjab legislative assembly with effect from Nov 1, 2026. I hereby resign from all forms of the Aam Aadmi Party with immediate effect.â Punjab assemblyâs present term ends on March 16, 2027. As such, the Election Commission is unlikely to hold bypolls for these seats. Disqualification Plea Pending A disqualification petition against Banga MLA Sukhwinder Kumar Sukhi, who switched from the Shiromani Akali Dal to the Aam Aadmi Party in Aug 2024, is still pending before Punjab Vidhan Sabha speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan. The petition was filed by advocate H C Arora in Sept 2024, seeking Sukhiâs disqualification under the anti-defection law. The matter remains undecided. title: In 2017, she made headlines for operating Vande Bharat and was invited to PM Modi's swearing-in ceremony; meet Shrini Srivastava, the Ghazipur assistant loco pilot making her mark in Indian Railways
text: Meet Shrini Srivastava Shrini Srivastava has become the new face of Vande Bharat Sleeper. The woman from Ghazipur, Uttar Pradesh has been entrusted with a significant role in the train operations. From being among the women railway employees who operated a Vande Bharat train to taking on a responsibility aboard one of India's newest long-distance trains, Srivastava has come a long way. The assistant loco pilot from Ghazipur, has been selected as part of the operating crew of the VaranasiâNew Delhi Vande Bharat Sleeper Express, which was flagged off on October 31, 2026. Now her journey has become an inspiration of determination, dedication and women's growing presence in India's railway network. From Ghazipur to the Indian Railways Srivastava is from Ghazipur district in eastern Uttar Pradesh. After completing her higher education, she chose a technically demanding profession that requires extensive training and responsibility. After completing her electronics engineering, she joined Indian Railways as an assistant loco pilot in April 2017 and got posted in the Varanasi railway division. As per a 2024 report by Dainik Jagran, Shrini is the youngest of three sisters and her father, Pankaj Srivastava, retired from the Public Works Department. Her mother, Maya Srivastava, is a homemaker. The Vande Bharat milestone that brought her recognition Shrini's association with Vande Bharat trains goes back to the early years of her railway career. In 2024, she made headlines after successfully operating the VaranasiâNew Delhi Vande Bharat Express as an assistant loco pilot. She was reported to be the first woman assistant loco pilot in the North Eastern Railway zone to operate the semi-high-speed train. She made the headlines after receiving an invitation to attend Prime Minister Narendra Modi's swearing-in ceremony in June 2024. She was selected for recognition of her contribution to operating the Vande Bharat Express. A new responsibility aboard the Vande Bharat Sleeper Vande Bharat trains to be exported to several countries in 3-4 years, Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw says And in October 2026, Shrini was again in the spotlight for her selection as an assistant loco pilot in the operating crew of the VaranasiâNew Delhi Vande Bharat Sleeper Express. The train was flagged off from Varanasi on October 31, 2026, in the presence of Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw. As per reports, the 13-member operating crew includes seven women. Shrini is among those entrusted with operational responsibilities, while Jyoti Kumari has been assigned the role of guard. The participation of women in different operational positions makes the new service particularly significant. More about VaranasiâDelhi Sleeper Express The new Vande Bharat Sleeper service is designed to make overnight journeys between eastern Uttar Pradesh and the national capital more comfortable. The train leaves Varanasi at 8:50 pm and reaches New Delhi at 6:10 am the following morning. On its return journey, it departs New Delhi at 9:40 pm and arrives in Varanasi at 7:10 am. The train passes through: Prayagraj Kanpur Central Aligarh Ghaziabad The sleeper version is designed for long-distance overnight travel, with sleeping arrangements, improved passenger amenities and advanced safety features. It also incorporates regenerative braking, an energy-efficient system that helps recover energy during braking. Breaking barriers Breaking barriers Loco pilot duties are often associated with long working hours, demanding schedules and the responsibility of operating trains safely across different routes. Women entering this profession are gradually challenging conventional ideas about which jobs are suitable for them. And Shrini's journey is interesting because her achievements have come through consistent work over the years rather than a single moment in the spotlight. From joining Indian Railways in 2017 to being recognised for her contribution to Vande Bharat operations in 2024 and now being selected for the Vande Bharat Sleeper operating crew, she has continued to take on new responsibilities. title: BJP fields Puri from MP for Nov 12 Rajya Sabha bypolls
text: Hardeep Puri Bhopal: The BJP on Wednesday nominated Union petroleum minister Hardeep Singh Puri as its candidate for the Nov 12 Rajya Sabha by-election in Madhya Pradesh, choosing a leader from outside the state to fill the vacancy in the Upper House arising from the resignation of member L Murugan . The seat fell vacant after Murugan resigned his Rajya Sabha seat on Oct 13. His term was due to end in April 2030. He was elected to the Upper House from Madhya Pradesh in April 2024. The nomination puts to rest speculations around Puri, whose existing Rajya Sabha term from Uttar Pradesh is due to end on Nov 25, amid a rumoured upcoming Union cabinet reshuffle. His election from Madhya Pradesh would now enable him to continue as a member of the Upper House beyond that date. Madhya Pradesh has 11 Rajya Sabha seats. With Muruganâs resignation, 10 are occupied and one is vacant. The BJP is expected to retain the seat given its strength in the 230-member Madhya Pradesh assembly, where it has 164 MLAs against Congressâs 65. The Bharat Adivasi Party has one MLA. The Election Commission has scheduled polling and counting for Nov 12, with Nov 2 as the last date for filing nominations. Puri currently holds the petroleum and natural gas portfolio in the Union cabinet. Murugan, who had represented Madhya Pradesh in the Rajya Sabha, resigned to return to Tamil Nadu and focus on strengthening the BJP ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha election. title: BFI power struggle deepens ahead of October 28 meeting; Boxing fraternity calls for unity
text: Boxing fraternity calls for unity ahead of BFI no-confidence meeting NEW DELHI: Olympians, award-winning coaches and former international boxers on Saturday called for stability, unity and accountability in Indian boxing, as a power struggle within the Boxing Federation of India (BFI) continued ahead of the Oct 28 meeting to consider a no-confidence motion against president Ajay Singh , who has questioned its legal validity. The developments come amid a fresh administrative move in Jharkhand, where an ad-hoc committee has been constituted to address issues within the state association and complete its long-pending elections within six months. The committee, comprising N K Nirwan as chairman, Rajesh Kumar Singh as convener and Smita Kumari as member, has been tasked with verifying district associations, ensuring their registration and overseeing the Jharkhand Boxing Association's (JBA) elections. The BFI's one-man committee had flagged concerns, including the absence of duly registered district associations and elections being delayed by seven months. BFI senior vice-president Rajesh Bhandari questioned the timing of the action. He alleged that the charges were intended to target members opposing the president and participating in the no-confidence meeting. He described the allegations as baseless. The developments come days before the scheduled meeting in Delhi. At a press conference at the Major Dhyan Chand national stadium here, boxing personalities, including Mohammed Ali Qamar and Manoj Kumar, stressed the need to restore order and ensure that the sport's development did not lose momentum amid the administrative dispute. âOur purpose is neither personal nor political. We seek accountability, institutional unity and a stronger future for the young boxers who aspire to represent India internationally,â the group said. Pramod Kumar, BFI's secretary general, also addressed the gathering, emphasising grassroots development and greater opportunities for athletes. He spoke about introducing under-12 boxing in Uttar Pradesh and organising competitions despite financial constraints. title: Economy, not ideology
text: When populists and autocrats lose elections, are voters rejecting their ideas or reacting to their economic problems? Research suggests that democracy is in danger. According to Swedenâs V-Dem Institute, the average person today has about the same democratic freedoms as in 1978. So, election results in Brazil and Serbia may look like victories for democracy. In Brazil, voters narrowly stopped Flavio Bolsonaro, who has shown strong authoritarian tendencies, from winning. They gave Lula another term instead. In Serbia, voters defeated strongman Aleksandar Vucic by a large margin. The result has attracted much attention because the winning side is a student protest movement supported by academics, doctors and others. Serbia has just 65 lakh people and a GDP of $112 billion. But these election results may not mean that democracy is making a comeback. As Harvard professor Steven Levitsky pointed out in 2024, voters may simply be unhappy with the people in power. In Brazil, even Lula lost the first round of voting before fighting back strongly. This trend has been clear since 2020, when Covid disrupted economies and governments adopted policies that made money easily available. The result was high inflation. Billionaires benefited, but the middle class and poorer people struggled. Levitsky noted that people had become deeply unhappy with their governments. In 41 of 55 elections and polls held between 2020 and 2024, the party in power lost. He said this was almost certainly linked to inflation caused by the pandemic. Were young Serbians, who protested against Vucic for two years, fighting for a political idea or for a better economic future? Britain offers another example. The Labour Party won a huge victory in the election, but became unpopular within months. Germanyâs Social Democrats are also struggling. In the US, voters first removed populist Donald Trump and elected Joe Biden, only to bring Trump back four years later. Now, with US midterm elections scheduled for November 3, voters may use their chance to weaken Trumpâs control of Congress. Why? He promised to tackle the rising cost of living, but his war on Iran has made peopleâs economic problems worse. Israel is another test for democracy, with elections taking place today. Opinion polls do not show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu winning a clear victory. But whoever wins is unlikely to take a softer stand towards Palestinians. Young Israelis, including first-time voters, do not appear to feel much sympathy for people in Gaza either. What they are tired of is endless war, the mental strain it causes and corruption. Everywhere, voters are asking their leaders a simple question: âWhat have you done for us and our future?â Leaders who are already in power are losing elections because they often have no convincing answer. title: Trump's Justice dept steps into US midterm battles before votes are counted, breaks decades-old practice
text: US Justice Department. US President Donald Trump's Justice Department has stepped into election disputes ahead of Tuesday's US midterm elections, breaking with decades of practice aimed at keeping federal law enforcement agencies from appearing to favour a political party or candidate. The department has filed lawsuits challenging election procedures in California and Alaska, raising concerns among critics that its powers are being used to influence contests that could determine control of Congress and several governors' offices, Reuters reported. In California, the Justice Department sought to block mail-in ballots from around 20,000 voters it suspects may be non-US citizens and therefore ineligible to vote. It has also demanded election records as part of a related criminal investigation. California officials have rejected the move, saying the state has safeguards to prevent noncitizens from voting and arguing that the federal government lacks the authority to block the ballots. In Alaska, the department has stepped up a criminal investigation into whether a Senate candidate sharing the name of Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan entered the race to confuse voters. It also moved to prevent certification of the election result if Sullivan narrowly loses. However, a federal judge dismissed the department's lawsuit on Sunday, ruling against its attempt to intervene in the state's election process. The Justice Department has appealed the decision. According to Reuters, courts have now rejected the department's lawsuits involving both California and Alaska. The cases have highlighted the Trump administration's willingness to intervene in election disputes before ballots are counted and results are certified. Critics have warned that such moves could give Trump an opportunity to question the legitimacy of the midterm results. "It appears that the administration wants the department to have an impact that was previously prohibited," Mark Blumberg, who formerly led the Justice Department's election response to civil rights threats, was quoted as saying by Reuters. He has since founded the Rule of Law Project. Attorney General Todd Blanche has defended the department's actions, saying they are lawful and intended to protect election integrity. "The Department isn't helping any campaign. It's enforcing the law," Justice Department spokesperson Kiersten Pels said. Trump's claims of voter fraud Under the US Constitution, individual states are responsible for administering elections. However, Trump has repeatedly accused Democratic-led states of failing to prevent noncitizens from voting, although voting by non-US citizens is already prohibited under federal law. Trump has also continued to make false claims that widespread voter fraud cost him the 2020 presidential election. Independent investigations and state audits have found that voter fraud is rare. During his first term, Justice Department officials resisted pressure to intervene in efforts to challenge Trump's 2020 election defeat. Outside groups aligned with the Republican leader subsequently filed more than 60 lawsuits disputing the results, but none succeeded. Lis Frost, a voting rights lawyer with Elias Law Group, which frequently represents Democrats in court, said the situation had changed. "The right-wing fringe outside groups are not going to have to do that this year because the DOJ is clearly standing ready and willing to do it," Frost told Reuters. Traditionally, the Justice Department's election-related interventions have focused on enforcing federal laws that protect the voting rights of racial minorities and other vulnerable groups. Alaska election becomes legal battleground Alaska has emerged as a major focus of the dispute following a New York Times report that Democratic candidate Mary Peltola's campaign was involved in recruiting retired teacher Daniel J Sullivan to challenge Republican Senator Dan Sullivan. The Justice Department's lawsuit, which Trump said he had directed the department to file, sought to halt certification of the results and order an investigation if the victory margin indicated that voter confusion could have affected the outcome. However, US District Judge Sharon Gleason in Anchorage dismissed the case on Sunday, saying Alaska could not conduct such an investigation while maintaining the secrecy of ballots. Legal experts had questioned whether the Justice Department had the authority to pursue the case, warning that the move could create the impression that the federal government was favouring the Republican incumbent. Peter Keisler, who served as acting attorney general under former Republican President George W Bush, said the department needed to maintain political neutrality to retain public trust. "For the department to be trusted in its law enforcement decisions it has to ensure that people understand it does not take sides in political partisan disputes," Keisler told Reuters. He added that the Alaska case had not only created the appearance of political interference but also represented an evident instance of taking sides. Blanche has defended the lawsuit, alleging that Daniel J Sullivan was involved in an attempt to mislead voters. The candidate has denied trying to confuse voters, while Peltola's campaign said it had "no involvement with either Sullivan campaign". Responding to criticism, a Justice Department official said during a press briefing on Thursday that the department filed lawsuits to enforce federal law. Trump allies gain greater control over election investigations The Justice Department has traditionally exercised caution in election-related investigations because federal intervention can create uncertainty and potentially be used by political candidates to challenge results. Its Public Integrity Section, which has career officials specialising in election law, previously advised investigators and prosecutors to wait until election results were certified before taking action, according to former department officials cited by Reuters. However, the Trump administration has reduced the size of the unit and suspended a requirement that federal prosecutors consult it during investigations into election-related corruption. Justice Department officials have argued that individual US attorney's offices are better placed to determine whether criminal charges should be pursued. According to three people familiar with internal discussions, agents and prosecutors have instead been told that political appointees of the Trump administration will decide unresolved disputes. The Deputy Attorney General's Office is also expected to mediate disagreements between investigators and prosecutors, a role former Justice Department officials said it has rarely played in election investigations. title: Meet the three former AAP leaders who switched sides to join BJP ahead of Punjab polls
text: Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, Chetan Singh Jouramajra, Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra joins BJP NEW DELHI: Three Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leaders from Punjab, including two rebel MLAs and a suspended legislator, joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Monday, days after breaking ties with the Arvind Kejriwal-led party. The development comes ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections and has triggered a political exchange between the BJP and the ruling AAP. The three leaders are Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh. While Pathanmajra and Jouramajra resigned from the AAP's primary membership on Sunday, Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, who was suspended from the party, resigned as an MLA on Monday. 1. Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra Pathanmajra represents the Sanour Assembly constituency in Patiala district. He was among the two AAP MLAs who announced their exit from the party on Sunday, accusing the Bhagwant Mann-led government of failing to address issues such as the drug menace, rising state debt and governance-related concerns. His resignation came shortly after the AAP released its first list of 40 candidates for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. Sanour was not among the constituencies for which candidates were announced. 2. Chetan Singh Jouramajra Jouramajra is the MLA from Samana in Patiala district and a former Punjab cabinet minister. He served in the Bhagwant Mann government from January 2023 to September 2024 before being dropped during a cabinet reshuffle. Like Pathanmajra, Jouramajra resigned from the AAP's primary membership on Sunday. He also accused the state government of failing to address key issues facing Punjab. Samana was not included in the AAP's first list of 40 candidates for the 2027 Assembly polls. The AAP had suspended both Pathanmajra and Jouramajra before they announced their resignations. The party also said it would approach the Punjab Assembly Speaker seeking cancellation of their legislative membership, alleging anti-party activities. 3. Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh is the MLA from Amritsar North and a former Indian Police Service (IPS) officer. He was suspended from the AAP for five years in June 2025 over alleged anti-party activities. His suspension followed his criticism of the Punjab Vigilance Bureau's action against Shiromani Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia. Singh had also repeatedly questioned the Mann government's handling of the sacrilege cases. title: Double Olympic medallist PV Sindhu enters her second final in two weeks after defeating compatriot Anmol Kharb at Hylo Open badminton tournament
text: PV Sindhu Double Olympic medallist PV Sindhu continued her impressive form by reaching the final of the Hylo Open Super 500 badminton tournament on Saturday. The Indian shuttler defeated compatriot Anmol Kharb in straight games, winning 21-13, 21-16 in just 32 minutes in the women's semifinal. This marks Sindhu's second consecutive final appearance in as many weeks. She had finished as the runner-up at the French Open last week and will now look to go one step further in Germany. Sindhu controlled most of the opening game and took it 21-13 after building a comfortable lead. The second game was more competitive, with Anmol briefly moving ahead 15-13. However, Sindhu quickly fought back to level the score at 15-15 before taking control and sealing the match 21-16. title: AAP discusses Punjab poll candidates at Kejriwalâs residence; first list due October 31
text: Discussions were led by national convenor Arvind Kejriwal and Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Singh Mann CHANDIGARH: The Aam Aadmi Party 's (AAP) Political Affairs Committee (PAC), the party's top decision-making body, met at the residence of national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Friday to discuss candidates for the upcoming Punjab assembly elections . Kejriwal, Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Singh Mann, party Punjab in-charge Manish Sisodia, AAP leader Satyendar Jain and Jasmine Shah attended the meeting, news agency ANI reported. Punjab finance minister Harpal Cheema and state AAP president Aman Arora joined the deliberations through video conferencing. After the meeting, Mann said the names of assembly candidates had been discussed and that the process would continue at the next PAC meeting. "The names of assembly candidates were discussed today," Mann said. "The names will be discussed again during the PAC meeting tomorrow, October 31. The first list of candidates will be released tomorrow," he added, ANI reported. On Wednesday, a delegation of the Election Commission of India (ECI) conducted a district-wise review of poll preparedness for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. The delegation comprised senior deputy election commissioner Pawan Kumar Sharma, deputy election commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu, director general (IT) Seema Khanna and director general (Media) Ashish Goyal. During the meeting, the delegation interacted with all 23 district election officers, commissioners of police and senior superintendents of police. Officials gave presentations on the status of election preparedness in their respective districts, ANI reported. The visiting officials emphasised strict compliance with ECI guidelines, transparency in administrative processes, timely execution of pre-poll activities and robust enforcement measures across the state. The chief electoral officer of Punjab assured the delegation that all election-related tasks would be carried out diligently and within the stipulated timelines, in accordance with the Election Commission's instructions, to ensure free, fair, transparent and inclusive polls. Meanwhile, Hardev Singh Ubha, a senior Punjab BJP leader, met Harjit Singh Grewal, chairman of the National Commission for Minorities, at the Commission's office in New Delhi and raised several public issues concerning Punjab and Mohali, ANI reported. During the meeting, Ubha highlighted concerns over drug abuse and the alleged death of a young man in Mansa, recurring fires at the Phase 5 dumping ground in Mohali, lack of canal water supply in several residential areas and villages, compensation for farmers affected by land acquisition in Sector 87, and delays in constructing a bridge connecting Sectors 66/67 with Sectors 80/81. He requested that the issues be brought to the attention of the concerned authorities for appropriate intervention and timely resolution in the public interest. Ubha also raised the death of Daljit Singh alias Jeeta, son of Sardar Jarnail Singh and a resident of Bhamme Kalan village in Mansa district, allegedly due to a drug overdose. title: TOI Youth Icons Summit: Para-badminton champ Suhas says youth should aim to rank among top 5% in their fields
text: Suhas Lalinakere Yathiraj at TOI Youth Icons Summit. Para-badminton champion and IAS officer Suhas Lalinakere Yathiraj addressed young achievers and emerging leaders at the TOI Youth Icons Summit & Awards â UP Chapter in Lucknow on Tuesday, sharing lessons from his journey in sports and public service and urging young people to strive for excellence in their chosen fields. Speaking at the summit, Suhas emphasised the importance of taking the first step towards one's goals, despite the fear of failure and concerns about societal judgement. âFirst step, the most difficult because we think what people and society will think if we lose,â he said. Sharing his approach to success, the badminton champion said, âI have a thumb rule which I believe most of the successful people here have too, Whatever stream you are in, aim to reach the top 5 per cent of that particular stream, if you become a lawyer become the best one, if doctor become the bestâ¦whatever field you chooseâ¦Can you make it to the top 5 per cent of the pyramid.â He also spoke about the importance of perseverance, noting that setbacks are an inevitable part of life. âUps and downs will always be a part of life, Just like the stock market. But just as the stock market, you will be successful in the long term,â he said. Encouraging young people to take chances rather than live with regret, the para-athlete said, âIts better to try and fail, than to not try at all and regret as you grow old.â He also cautioned against complacency after achieving success. âRemember it is easier to reach the peak than to stay there consistently; the enemy of success is complacency so we should not be complacent in any case,â he said. The TOI Youth Icons Summit & Awards â UP Chapter brought together achievers, emerging leaders and influential voices to celebrate young Indians shaping the country's future. The awards recognised outstanding achievers from Uttar Pradesh across categories including enterprise, sports, society, culture and social media. The summit also featured discussions on Uttar Pradesh's transformation over the years, including improvements in job opportunities for young people, safety and connectivity. The event focused on recognising young people whose ambition, ideas and achievements are contributing to India's future. Addressing the issue of addiction among young people, Suhas called it a rising problem and stressed the need to recognise the consequences of one's actions. âAddiction amomg youth is rising problem, we must realise that every action has consequences, so does addiction,â he said. Suhas is an Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer and para-badminton player. He has won silver medals at the Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 Paralympic Games and gold at the 2024 BWF Para Badminton World Championships. He currently serves as secretary of the department of sports and youth welfare and director general of youth welfare and Prantiya Rakshak Dal in the Uttar Pradesh government. title: BJP-Akali alliance: Talks on to hammer out seat-sharing arrangement ahead of Punjab polls
text: BJP keen to offer a respectable deal to splinter Akali group NEW DELHI: BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal are in an advanced stage of negotiations for reviving their alliance for the Punjab assembly elections . A couple of thorny issues, including the precise seat-sharing arrangement and the accommodation of the rebel Akali faction, seen close to BJP, continue to persist but several functionaries from the two parties believe they can be addressed in the coming days. Before Sukhbir Singh Badal-led Akali Dal snapped ties with BJP due to its opposition to now-repealed farm laws in 2020 as a section of farmers launched protest against the reforms, his party was the decidedly big brother in Punjab. Its decline since, brought afore by the 2022 assembly and the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, and BJP's gains since mean that their equation is likely to be rearranged. BJP on its part has maintained it is preparing to contest on all seats after bagging over 18% votes, its best ever, in 2024 when two main rivals for office- governing AAP and the main opposition Congress- pulling around 26% votes. SAD's share fell to a little over 13%. title: 16-year-old Dhinidhi Desinghu scripts history at Youth Olympics, becomes first Indian swimmer to win a medal
text: Dhinidhi Desinghu (Agency Photo) India's Dhinidhi Desinghu created history at the 2026 Youth Olympics in Dakar, Senegal, by becoming the first Indian female swimmer to win a medal at the competition. The 16-year-old secured bronze in the women's 100m freestyle, clocking 56.27 seconds. Croatia's Ana Bobanovic won gold in 55.89 seconds, while New Zealand's Alyssa Lawson took silver in 56.13 seconds. Watch Kynan Chenai: The 38-Year-Old Gun Barrel, Asian Games Gold and the LA 2028 Dream | TOISA Spotlight The medal adds another milestone to Desinghu's growing swimming career. She had earlier become the first Indian female swimmer to reach a Youth Olympics final after finishing third-fastest overall in the heats with a time of 56.80 seconds. A promising swimmer with another medal opportunity Her coach, Nihar Ameen, praised her hard work and recent performances, highlighting that she had broken the national record three times this year. "She has been working really hard. This year, she has broken the national record three times. She is in form. She has another shot at a medal in the 200m freestyle event. In fact, she has a better chance of winning another medal there," he said. "Dhinidhi is mentally very tough. She has already competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics. We are very hopeful that she will win another medal at this Youth Olympics." Desinghu was the youngest member of India's contingent at the Paris Olympics. She is now looking to add another medal in the 200m freestyle at Dakar. title: Tipra Motha founder Pradyot meets CM Saha, discusses Tiprasa Accord
text: Pradyot Kishore Debbarma Agartala : Tipra Motha founder Pradyot Kishore Debbarma met chief minister Manik Saha on Wednesday night and separately held discussions with chief secretary JK Sinha on the implementation of the 2024 Tiprasa (tribal) Accord after Durga Puja. Pradyotâs meeting with CM came ahead of the urban local body elections and triggered speculation within political circles. Tipra Motha, an ally of the BJP-led Tripura govt, had earlier declared its intent to cut electoral ties with BJP if the accord is not implemented and tribal land rights are not guaranteed. Pradyot had declared his plan to retreat from active politics three weeks ago. He had said his involvement was driven by the continued denial of dignity and rights to tribal communities. After the meetings, Pradyot described the discussions as productive and said he had received assurances on the timely implementation of the accord. He did not disclose details of the issues discussed, saying the chief minister should also present his views. Pradyot said despite distancing himself from active politics, he continued to represent the voices of Tripuraâs people instead of his party. He clarified that the meeting did not involve political discussions or seat-sharing for the urban local body elections. He said he met Saha in his capacity as chief minister to discuss the rights of the Tiprasa community and the wider public, and not to negotiate with BJP. title: Navy rescues 20 crew members of fishing vessel from armed pirates over 3,000km from Mumbai, Rajnath praises 48-hr op
text: Navy rescues all 20 crew members of fishing vessel Azini from armed pirates in a 48-hour operation in the Arabian Sea, with support from the Indian Air Force NEW DELHI: The Indian Navy has rescued all 20 crew members of a fishing vessel from armed pirates after a 48-hour operation in the Arabian Sea. Defence minister Rajnath Singh praised the Indian Navy for executing the meticulously coordinated 48-hour operation with support from the Indian Air Force. âThe swift localisation, interception and safe release of the crew and vessel from significantly-armed pirates, with timely support from the IAF, speak well of the Indian Navyâs high operational readiness and ability to respond decisively to maritime threats across the region,â Rajnath said. A photograph shared by the minister on his post on X shows destroyer INS Kolkata standing by as heavily armed commandos guard what appear to be the pirates, seated on the deck of the fishing vessel. India continues to stand resolute in ensuring SAFE SEAS and a free, open and secure IOR,â he said. title: Indian national charged in US over false citizenship claim to vote in 2024 election; faces up to 10 years in prison
text: Mukeshkumar Somabhai Chaudhari/Image: US Department of Homeland Security An Indian national has been charged in the United States for falsely claiming to be an American citizen to vote in the 2024 general election in Minnesota, according to the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS). Mukeshkumar Somabhai Chaudhari was indicted by a federal grand jury in Minnesota on September 10 on two counts linked to the alleged offence. The indictment accuses him of knowingly claiming US citizenship to cast a ballot. According to the indictment, Chaudhari signed a voter signature certificate on November 5, 2024, as required under Minnesota law to vote in the general election. The document required him to swear or affirm that he was a US citizen. Prosecutors allege that he was not a citizen and knowingly made the false declaration to vote. US Immigration and Customs Enforcementâs Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) arrested Chaudhari, DHS said. The charges include providing false information in voting and making a false claim of citizenship to register to vote or cast a ballot. If convicted, Chaudhari faces a maximum prison sentence of five years on each count. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the administration would pursue cases involving alleged unlawful voting by noncitizens. âVoting is reserved for US citizens, and falsely claiming citizenship to cast a ballot is a serious crime,â HSI St. Paul Special Agent in Charge Travis Pickard said. He added that the agency would continue working with law enforcement partners to investigate such cases and protect election systems. You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. title: 'Nobody told me..that's very confusing': Indian man Kamlesh Shah charged with election fraud in US says he didn't know he was not supposed to vote
text: Indian man Kamlesh Shah charged with voter fraud in California says nobody told him that he was not allowed to vote in US elections. 67-year-old Kamlesh Navnitlal Shah, a retired dentist from California, said he had no idea that he was not supposed to vote in the 2024 election, as he was a permanent resident but not a citizen. He has now been charged with fraudulently registering to vote in US elections. After his name came up in the list of foreign nationals who voted in the election in California, he said he was scared as he was not aware of the situation. Dr Shah said he met an accident five to six years ago and was in a coma for six months, and can hardly talk or walk. Apart from Shah, another Indian on the list is 30-year-old Amandeep Kaur, a resident of Rancho Palos Verdes. According to the law enforcement record, Kaur is seeking to become a US citizen, and fraudulently registered to vote in December 2022 and then voted in the November 2024 US election. Shah said he went to the community center "to vote with my blind roommate". He said his was asked to produce his ID. "I showed them the ID and my Social Security card. They did something...I don't remember...it was a long time ago. They gave me the paperwork to vote. I thought I was registering to vote. I didn't know about my pending citizenship. I thought I must be a citizen. I had no idea I wasn't," Shah said, adding that nobody told him that he was not a citizen and was not supposed to vote. What is 'Operation Protect the Vote'? The administration said Operation Protect the Vote is a coordinated effort among all four California-based US Attorney's offices to combat and root out fraud in US elections. 11 foreign nationals among 28 total charged were arrested for voter fraud. All these 28 foreign nationals have Green cards but they are not US citizens and no one except US citizens are allowed to vote in US elections. The criminal charges include making false statements in a naturalization application and some of the defendants also are charged with fraudulent voter registration. Both charges are felonies that carry a maximum penalty of five years in federal prison. On October 13, the federal government provided a list of these individuals to California to ensure that their vote-by-mail ballots were set aside until these individualsâ citizenship status could be confirmed. California declined to assist the federal government in setting aside their ballots, prompting a lawsuit by the United States that seeks a court order to prevent the unlawful dilution of American citizensâ votes and to uphold the integrity of our elections. âEvery illegal vote cancels out the vote of a lawful American citizen,â said Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter. âEach of the 28 defendants charged today appears on the list of more than 20,000 likely noncitizen registrants we provided to California election officials last week. California refused to look at that list. Today's charges show exactly what that refusal puts at risk. California must verify the citizenship of those more than 20,000 registrants before mail-in ballots are counted. â You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

title: Zeeshan Siddiqui appointed Mumbai NCP president by Sunetra Pawar
text: Zeeshan Baba Siddique, Sunetra Pawar MUMBAI: The Nationalist Congress Party (NCP), led by Sunetra Pawar, has appointed Zeeshan Siddiqui as president of its Mumbai unit, signalling a generational shift in the partyâs city leadership while also carrying significance for its outreach to the Muslim community. Siddiqui, son of former Maharashtra minister Baba Siddique, takes charge at a time when the party is looking to strengthen its connect with younger voters. His appointment also assumes political significance amid the NCPâs alliance with the BJP as part of the Mahayuti coalition in Maharashtra. By elevating a Muslim leader to a key organisational position in Mumbai, the party could seek to signal that it continues to value the community despite its association with the BJP. Baba Siddique was shot dead on October 12, 2024, outside his sonâs party office in Bandra. The appointment marks another significant step in Zeeshan Siddiquiâs political career after a setback in the November 2024 assembly elections, when he lost from the Bandra East constituency. He returned to the legislature in May 2026 after being elected to the Maharashtra Legislative Council (MLC). Reacting to his appointment, Siddiqui said the responsibility would require him to work with party members and people across communities. âBeing appointed as the President of the Nationalist Congress Party for Mumbai is a massive responsibility. Sunetra Pawar and Parth Pawarâwho is like an elder brother to meâhave given me this opportunity and entrusted me with the responsibility for Mumbai. It is now my duty to work alongside the entire NCP family and serve people from every section of society. My goal is to engage the youth, connect with the elderly, and work with our senior members,â he said. title: State election commissioner seeks report from DGP on alleged police bias and violence in AP local bodies polls
text: State election commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha issued a directive instructing AP DGP to examine the veracity of the charges and submit a comprehensive compliance report within 24 hours Tirupati : Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission (SEC) has directed the director general of police (DGP) to conduct an urgent inquiry into serious allegations of police inaction, political bias, and failure to prevent electoral violence during the ongoing 2026 local body elections. State election commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha issued a directive instructing AP DGP to examine the veracity of the charges and submit a comprehensive compliance report within 24 hours. The action follows three formal representations submitted by Tirupati Lok Sabha member Maddila Gurumoorthy, which were forwarded to the commission by the governorâs secretariat at Lok Bhavan, Vijayawada. The parliamentarian detailed widespread disruptions across several municipalities, including Punganur, Pulivendula, Kamalapuram, Badvel, Rajampet, and Yerraguntla, citing instances of electoral violence, obstruction, and candidate intimidation throughout the nomination process. In his submissions, the MP highlighted supervisory failures and alleged partisan conduct by senior police officers, specifically naming DIG Dr. Koya Praveen, Annamayya SP Dheeraj Kanubilli, and Kadapa SP Shelke Nachiket Vishwanath. The complaints allege that these officers failed to maintain law and order or enforce protective orders previously issued by the high court of Andhra Pradesh. Additionally, the representation requested an investigation into Dr Koya Praveenâs current deployment in light of past election transfer orders and noted derogatory public remarks allegedly made by the officer. To ensure free and fair elections, the commission has forwarded the details to the district collectors, district election officers, and superintendents of police across Tirupati, Chittoor, Annamayya, and YSR Kadapa districts for immediate necessary action, while directing the state police chief to quickly furnish the compliance report. title: 'Educated voters don't turn up in assembly polls': UP minister OP Rajbhar plays down MLC results
text: NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh minister Om Prakash Rajbhar shrugged off the legislative council election results after the Samajwadi Party defeated the Bharatiya Janata Party in the Varanasi Graduates' constituency, saying the election reflected the mandate of educated voters rather than the general electorate. Speaking to reporters, Rajbhar said the MLC elections had no connection with the assembly elections. âThis is the peopleâs mandate, the mandate of educated voters, and we welcome the verdict,â Rajbhar said. âHowever, these elections have no connection with the assembly elections. Historically, educated voters often do not turn up to vote in assembly elections and instead treat the day as a holiday,â he added. title: 72% of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh political parties fail to disclose finances: Association for Democratic Reforms
text: 72% of T, AP political parties fail to disclose finances: ADR Hyderabad : Nearly three-fourths of registered unrecognised political parties in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh failed to publicly disclose either their annual audit statements or contribution reports for 2024-25, raising fresh concerns over transparency and financial accountability in the political system, according to a report released by the Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) on Thursday. The report also highlighted discrepancies in donation disclosures made by two Telangana-based parties. Of the 169 registered unrecognised political parties (RUPPs) in the two states, 123, or 72%, had neither annual audit statements nor contribution reports available on the websites of the respective chief electoral officers. 31 parties have both statements online Telangana accounted for 78 of the 123 parties without either disclosure, representing 75% of its 104 RUPPs. In Andhra Pradesh, 45 of the 65 such parties had not made either report available. Only 31 parties across both states had uploaded both the audit statement and contribution report. Telangana accounted for 17 of these parties, while Andhra Pradesh had 14. Another 15 parties had only one of the two disclosures available. In Telangana, six parties had uploaded only audit statements and three only contribution reports. In Andhra Pradesh, two parties had only audit statements available, while four had uploaded only contribution reports. Donation figures differ The ADR report also flagged inconsistencies in the financial disclosures of two Telangana-based parties. A Hyderabad-based political party reported zero income and zero total donations for 2024-25, but disclosed receiving â¹1.29 lakh in contributions above â¹20,000. The party reported expenditure of â¹300 during the year. It had contested seven seats in the 2023 Telangana assembly elections, polling 49,423 votes without winning any seat. Similarly, Vishwa Bharath Party, registered in Dec 2021, declared an income of â¹900, total donations of â¹200 and expenditure of â¹5,000. However, its contribution report showed donations exceeding â¹20,000 amounting to â¹30,000. The party contested one assembly constituency in the 2023 elections, securing 55 votes. The two Telangana parties were among 14 parties across the country whose reported contributions above â¹20,000 exceeded their declared total donations. ADR noted that the reasons for such discrepancies can be established only after examining the partiesâ original accounts and contribution reports. The report also noted that the Andhra Pradesh CEOâs website did not provide consolidated information on the submission status of annual reports for 2024-25. In contrast, Telanganaâs CEO website carried details on the status of audit report submissions by political parties. Available disclosures showed that Telangana-based parties reported a combined income of â¹18.9 lakh and expenditure of â¹15.8 lakh. Parties in Andhra Pradesh reported income of â¹70.8 lakh and expenditure of â¹78.2 lakh. Together, the parties declared total donations of â¹82.7 lakh, while contributions exceeding â¹20,000 amounted to nearly â¹1.9 crore. Nationally, ADR examined financial disclosures of 2,074 registered unrecognised political parties, of which only 461 had both audit statements and contribution reports available. title: BJP organises march in city to counter INDIA blocâs rally against SIR
text: BJP members take part in the rally which began at Bapu Vatika in Morabadi and concluded at Birsa Munda Memorial Museum Ranchi: A day after the Congress-led INDIA bloc held a rally at Delhiâs Ramlila Maidan against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demanded the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, the Jharkhand BJP unit on Monday organised a âSave Democracy, Remove Anarchyâ march in the city. The march was part of the BJPâs nationwide campaign to counter the INDIA blocâs narrative on the revision of electoral rolls. Hundreds of BJP workers took part in the procession, which began at Bapu Vatika in Morabadi and concluded at Birsa Munda Memorial Museum near Jail More, passing through Kutchery Chowk. Union minister Jual Oram, BJP national general secretary and Jharkhand in-charge Gajendra Singh Patel, state BJP president Aditya Sahu, leader of opposition in the assembly Babulal Marandi, former chief minister Arjun Munda and JD(U) MLA Saryu Roy were among those who participated in the programme. Targeting the INDIA bloc, Oram said parties questioning the electoral process lacked faith in democratic institutions. Taking a swipe at Congress MP Rahul Gandhi , he said, âIf you want to become Prime Minister, win the election. One cannot become PM by holding a mock Parliament.â Sahu accused Congress of selectively questioning constitutional institutions. âCongress is opposing SIR on the pretext of vote theft. It raises questions about electoral institutions only where it sees no political advantage,â he said. He also criticised the JMM-led state govt over the law-and-order situation. Marandi alleged that Rahul and other INDIA bloc constituents were attempting to create an atmosphere of instability. He said the march was aimed at exposing what he described as âanti-democraticâ politics. Reacting to the BJPâs campaign, Congress state general secretary Lal Kishore Nath Shahdeo said it was an attempt to divert attention from inflation, unemployment and other public issues. âIt is ironic that a party with a history of toppling democratically elected govts and misusing central agencies is now claiming to defend democracy,â Shahdeo said. title: Vivek Ramaswamy goes low in Ohio's race to the bottom
text: TOI Correspondent from Washington: American political campaigns have long operated on the principle that if you cannot convince voters that you are the best person for the job, you must at least persuade them that your opponent is a terrible human being. Vivek Ramaswamy , the Indian-American running for governor of Ohio, has presented a particularly grim illustration of that practice. The Republican Trump surrogate has embraced a $4 million campaign ad featuring the estranged mother of his Democratic opponent, Amy Acton, calling her daughter a liar. The ad, widely panned as distasteful, drags Actonâs deeply painful childhood that included neglect and sexual abuse by her stepfather -- resulting in her removal from her motherâs custody -- into a race where Ramaswamy is trailing in most polls. Watch Trumpâs Jon Husted FIXATION EXPLODES: Prez Goes On ANOTHER Bizarre Rant About Ohio Senatorâs Rear While Actonâs brother and a raft of supporters have publicly defended her and condemned Ramaswamy for exploiting her childhood trauma, even Republicans are aghast by the ad, which pundits say illustrates desperation on part of Ramaswamy. âHow low can Vivek go? Even lower than we thought,â conservative commentator Bill Kristol said. Pro-Trump talking head Scott Jennings described it as an extremely risky strategy while conceding that âto throw out a piece like this at the end of a race is not confidence-inspiring. .." Ramaswamy however has doubled down on the attack ad after initially distancing himself from it, living up to the electionâs billing as one of the ugliest in this midterm election cycle. The local Columbus Dispatch newspaper on Wednesday announced it was endorsing Acton, saying Ramaswamyâs âreckless behaviorâ¦canât be ignored.â MAGA bosses, including President Trump and veep JD Vance, who was born and raised in Ohio and was elected Senator from the state, have backed Ramaswamy but have not commented on the controversial ad. While it is hardly an American invention to turn politics into character assassination, the U.S political echo system has now perfected the art, complete with television production values, ominous music and enough selective editing to make an ordinary candidate appear capable of anything short of eating the family pet. Trump himself is on a tear on the campaign trail, demonizing immigrants while referring to developments in France and warning âthat is what the radical Democrats wanna do to America," with echoes of his 2024 âthey are eating the dogs, they are eating the catsâ vilification of immigrants. Both Acton and Ramaswamy are accomplished local Ohioans with very different backgrounds. Acton is from the rust belt town of Youngstown who overcame poverty and childhood sexual abuse to earn a medical degree from Northeastern Ohio University College of Medicine and a master's degree in public health from Ohio State University. Ramaswamy is the Cincinnati-born son of Indian immigrants, whose father was a General Electric engineer and whose mother was a geriatric psychiatrist. He earned billions in biotech after graduating from Jesuit-run St. Xavier High School and earning degrees from Harvard University and Yale Law School. Ohio has only ever elected white Christian men as governor, and either Acton or Ramaswamy would make history if elected. Acton would be the first woman and the first Jewish person elected to the role and Ramaswamy would be the state's first Indian-American governor who is also a self-professed Hindu-American. Previous governors of Indian origin were Nikki Haley (South Carolina 2011-2017), a Sikh who converted to Christianity, and Bobby Jindal (Louisiana 2008-2016), a Hindu who converted to Christianity. Louisiana also demonstrated that voters can cut a lot of slack for campaigns suffused with sleaze. Long before voters became so forgiving of Trumpâs peccadilloes, Edwin Edwards, the state's flamboyant governor, famously boasted during his 1983 re-election campaign that the only way he could lose was âif I'm caught in bed with either a dead girl or a live boy.â He won. title: Man gets two years of rigorous imprisonment for showing obscene films to minors
text: Thiruvananthapuram: A fast-track court in Attingal sentenced a 45-year-old man to two years of rigorous imprisonment and imposed a fine of Rs 50,000 for showing obscene films to two minor girls. Judge C R Bijukumar, who pronounced the verdict, said that in default of payment of the fine, the accused would have to undergo an additional two months of rigorous imprisonment. Attingal fast-track court found Benny Thankachan, a native of Edamulakkal in Kollam, guilty under Section 354A(2) read with Section 354A(1)(iii) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Section 12 read with Section 11(iii) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act. According to the prosecution, the incident occurred on June 19, 2024. The accused had allegedly shown sexually explicit films to the two girls, both aged 12. Kilimanoor Police registered a case on June 20, 2024, and launched an investigation. The investigation was conducted by sub-inspector R Rajikrishna, who subsequently filed the chargesheet before the court. During the trial, the prosecution examined 22 witnesses and produced 25 documents as evidence. The court also ordered that, if the fine amount is recovered, Rs 25,000 each be paid to the two survivors as compensation. It further recommended compensation for them through the district legal services authority, Thiruvananthapuram. title: Was just âcuriousâ and left when cops asked: Imran Khan in plea
text: Bombay High Court has adjourned the hearing on Imran Khan Pal's challenge to a notice until November 2 MUMBAI: Bombay High Court on Tuesday posted to Nov 2 the hearing on actor Imran Khan Palâs challenge to a notice directing him to leave India and till then kept the notice in abeyance. The Oct 28 deadline under the Oct 14 notice issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) under the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, was extended till the next hearing after Additional Solicitor General Anil Singh appearing for the Centre sought a short adjournment. Khan, born in the US, has been in India for almost 42 years since the age of two years. He holds an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) status under the Citizenship Act, 1955. The HC bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna recorded in the brief order that senior counsel V R Dhond appearing for the actor had âfairlyâ not opposed such a request for adjournment. Khanâs plea says power to remove a person under Section 29 of the Foreigners Act was intended to safeguard national sovereignty and security, and could not be used to punish a public figure merely for being present near a protest site or expressing concern over restrictions on the movement of people in the city. His expulsion could undermine confidence of the US-based Indian diaspora in the OCI regime and raise concerns for the US, whose citizen he is. On Tuesday, lawyer Sunil Kumar, represented by advocate Subhash Jha, intervened in the matter, contending that the FRRO notice falls under criminal jurisdiction and that Khanâs civil petition could thus not be heard. Khanâs senior counsel, V R Dhond, questioned the intervenerâs locus to raise the objection. The matter was kept back for Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to appear online for the FRRO, a central govt authority, from New Delhi. However, ASG Anil Singh later sought an adjournment to enable the solicitor general to appear, following which the court posted the matter to Nov 2. The notice followed an FIR registered against him for allegedly participating in a protest in Mumbai on Oct 10 in support of the Cockroach Janata Partyâs (CJP) agitation against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi. Khanâs plea said he was merely âcuriousâ when he was passing by and saw the crowd and had left immediately when the police asked him to. Khan (around 44), also represented by lawyers Zulfiquar Memon, Parvez Memon and Kunal Vajani, contended that the notice was arbitrary, disproportionate and issued without hearing him, thus flouting his fundamental rights to equality and life under Articles 14 and 21, which apply to non-Indian citizens as well. Arguing that the notice imposed the ultimate consequence on the basis of a mere allegation, the petition said the authorities could not proceed with his expulsion without allowing the criminal justice process to take its course. title: Vijayawada municipal polls record 55% turnout, parties concerned
text: Vijayawada : The overall polling percentage recorded in the just-concluded Vijayawada Municipal Corporation (VMC) elections has left the two main political parties in a tizzy, with the turnout remaining significantly below expectations at just 55.35 percent. This was considerably lower than the 62.88 percent polling recorded in the 2021 municipal general elections. Political party leaders attributed the decline in voter turnout to several factors, including voters working in neighbouring states not turning up to vote and the failure to distribute voter slips to voters, which made it difficult for some to locate their polling booths following the delimitation of wards in the city. âMany had anticipated the polling percentage to cross 70 percent, but the voter turnout was just around 55 percent, which was 7.53 percentage points lower than the figure recorded in the previous municipal elections. This could result in mayoral candidates securing lower victory margins, as the total number of votes polled was only around 4.40 lakh, significantly lower than the nearly six lakh votes expected to be polled in the municipal elections,â a senior political party leader in the city said. Some leaders said that although voters enthusiastically turned up to exercise their franchise, the failure of booth-level officers (BLOs) to distribute voter slips had forced several voters to leave polling stations without casting their votes. Another reason cited by political leaders was the failure of working professionals and their families residing in neighbouring states to return to the city to cast their votes. Some voters originally from Vijayawada but currently residing in neighbouring states reportedly abstained from voting, stating that municipal elections would not have any impact on the incumbent state government. title: IOC chapters mobilise for Rahul Gandhiâs âDelhi Chaloâ rally
text: Indian Overseas Congress functionaries Amritsar : The Nov 1 âDelhi Chaloâ rally called by Congress leader and leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has triggered a mobilisation drive among Indian Overseas Congress (IOC) chapters worldwide, with leaders urging members and office-bearers to travel to India to strengthen the partyâs campaign against alleged electoral irregularities. With the âVote Bachao, Desh Bachaoâ mega rally scheduled at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi, IOC leaders across Europe and other regions are working to encourage greater participation. Several overseas office-bearers have already arrived in India. These include IOC Germany president Balwinder Singh Gurdaspuria and IOC UK president Kamal Dhaliwal, who are already camping in the country ahead of the rally. Talking to TOI on Tuesday, IOC general secretary for Europe Mohamed Irshath appealed to people to participate peacefully in the Nov. 1 march, linking electoral confidence with Indiaâs international standing. âFrom Europe, we see how Indiaâs democratic reputation shapes the respect it commands abroad. That reputation must be sustained by institutions that answer citizensâ concerns openly,â he said. Backing Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, Irshath urged people across political affiliations to join the campaign, saying electoral fairness was fundamental to public trust in democratic institutions. Kamal Dhaliwal, who is also preparing to contest the upcoming assembly elections from the Amargarh assembly constituency in Malerkotla district, said there was considerable enthusiasm among IOC members worldwide to participate in the campaign. He alleged that several decisions of the BJP-led government had failed to benefit Indians living abroad and said overseas Indians had concerns that needed to be raised. The mobilisation, he added, reflected the desire among Congress supporters overseas to strengthen the party and back Rahul Gandhiâs political campaign. IOC Austria president Ausaf Khan said he held a virtual meeting with representatives of more than a dozen IOC chapters on Monday and urged them to reach Delhi for the rally. He said the effort was aimed at bringing overseas Congress workers together to strengthen the organisation and demonstrate support for the party leadership. He said the rally was part of the Congress-led Oppositionâs campaign against alleged irregularities in electoral rolls and its demand for accountability from the Election Commission . He added that Rahul Gandhi had called upon students, farmers, labourers, women, youth and traders to join the march, arguing that protecting voting rights was essential to safeguarding democracy. The rally has faced objections from Delhi traders, who fear traffic restrictions and security arrangements could affect festive-season business. title: BJP can surpass 2017 tally if poll prep is completed early: Tawde
text: Left to right: state general secretartty (organisation) Dharampal Singh, UP BJP chief Pankaj Chaudhary and BJP national general secretary Vinod Tawde Lucknow : BJP national general secretary and UP in-charge Vinod Tawde on Saturday asserted that by completing preparations well ahead of schedule, the party could achieve better results in 2027 Assembly elections and even surpass the 2017 tally. Chairing an organisational meeting at the state party office in Lucknow, Tawde emphasised that the upcoming election hinges on âmicromanagement,â requiring meticulous attention to every aspect of the action plan. The meeting was attended by UP BJP chief Pankaj Chaudhary; state general secretary (Organization) Dharampal Singh and state co-in-charges Medha Kulkarni, Jagdish Patel, Anant Ojha, and Pradeep Verma. State office-bearers, regional presidents, heads of various morchas, district presidents, and district in-charges were also present. Tawde directed that the appointment of âpravasi prabharisâ at the Assembly constituency level be expedited, and that election management committees be constituted at both the district and Assembly levels. Tawde said that members of the Mahila Morcha and Yuva Morcha will serve as the visiting in-charges at the Assembly level. He instructed all district in-charges to complete their visits to the Assembly constituencies and asked all Assembly-level in-charges to visit the Shakti Kendras. Tawdeâs observations underlines BJPâs poll urgency as it tries to scale up organisational work for the Assembly elections. His directions came a day after the UP state working committee rolled out the formal blueprint of the organisational exercise which the party would take to build on an electoral momentum. He said that âvistaraksâ (full-time party workers) must immediately begin holding meetings with active party members at the âmandal (local/zonal) level and ensure visits to the âShakti Kendrasâ. He added that, as part of the partyâs âdoor-to-door outreachâ campaign, one party worker will be assigned the responsibility for every 50 households. Tawde stressed the need to develop a comprehensive plan for door-to-door public outreach. This involves formulating specific strategies to engage with various segments, including women, youth, first-time voters, beneficiary farmers, small-scale traders, intellectuals, ex-servicemen, and various social and religious organisations. He said the party must reach out to the beneficiaries of the public welfare schemesâimplemented by the Central and state govt. Furthermore, he said, the party was required to engage with the public to discuss the bold decisions taken at the national and state levels, as well as topics concerning development, security, and the nationâs economic and strategic progress. Chaudhary emphasised that the mantra for winning elections lay at the âboothâ and the voters associated with them. âWe must prioritize the verification of electoral rolls and the special revision campaign,â he said, stressing the need for having a robust team of party workers who can be engaged at all 1,918 âmandalsâ. Dharampal Singh said that as part of preparation, âDistrict Election Steering Committeesâ and âAssembly Election Steering Committeesâ were required to be formed. He noted that the most significant initiative leading up to Diwali was the series of âpadyatrasâ (foot marches) to be organised at the regional level under the âSave Democracy, Eliminate Anarchyâ. Singh said that various segmentsâsuch as youth, women, intellectuals, labourers, the business community, street vendors, and micro-entrepreneurs (including those selling tea, paan, groceries, vegetables, etc.)âmust be identified and listed to facilitate outreach and dialogue. title: AIPTMMK president âsacksâ Sasikala from party
text: File photo Chennai: All India Puratchi Thalaivar Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AIPTMMK) president P Sakkaravarthy said he was âexpellingâ party general secretary V K Sasikala from the outfit on Wednesday. Sakkaravarthy told reporters that there were no efforts on the part of Sasikala to nurture the party. Multiple attempts to meet her after the assembly elections failed, he said. âNot just me, she has not met any of the functionaries and cadres. How can someone who doesnât meet the functionaries run the party. Hence we decided to remove her,â he said. Sasikala allied with the PMK faction headed by S Ramadoss and fielded candidates in more than 70 constituencies during the assembly election. title: AIADMK to rework bypoll strategy, eyes 65% anti-govt vote: Dindigul Sreenivasan

title: GVMC completes arrangements for Sunday polls, commissioner Ketan Garg urges every voter to participate
text: At the East Zone distribution centre Officials take the material for election duty at the Gajuwaka distribution centre At the East Zone distribution centre Officials take the material for election duty at the Gajuwaka distribution centre At the East Zone distribution centre 1 2 Visakhapatnam : GVMC commissioner and additional election officer Ketan Garg said all arrangements have been completed for the second general election to Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation. He appealed to every eligible voter in the city to exercise their franchise in the election on Sunday, Nov 1. According to officials, campaigning, canvassing for votes and displaying flags and posters are strictly prohibited within 100 metres of polling stations. Except for election observers and polling and security personnel, no one is allowed to carry mobile phones or wireless sets within this 100-metre radius. Ministers, MPs, MLAs and persons provided official security are also not allowed to enter polling booths with their security personnel. They can visit polling stations only to cast their votes. Elected representatives and govt employees cannot be appointed as election or polling agents. Political parties and candidates can set up booths beyond 200 metres of polling stations, with prior permission from officials. Such booths can have only one table, two chairs and an umbrella or tarpaulin. Voter slips distributed at these booths must not carry the candidateâs name or party symbol. Officials warned that cases would be registered against both those distributing and accepting cash, liquor or gifts to influence voters. Violators could face imprisonment of up to one year. Transporting voters to polling stations in vehicles is also an offence. Violators could face vehicle seizure and imprisonment of up to three months. As part of election restrictions, all liquor shops and bars within the city limits will remain closed until 5 pm on Sunday. Cash exceeding Rs 50,000 carried illegally will be seized if the person concerned fails to produce supporting documents. Garg said the right to vote is one of the most valuable aspects of democracy. He urged every voter to participate in protecting democracy by exercising their franchise. He also urged people to follow the voter awareness messages issued by Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission and actively participate in the electoral process. title: Widespread sentiment in favor of BJP across UP: Chaudhary
text: Lucknow: The UP BJP state working committee signalled the formal start of campaign for the 2027 Assembly elections, with partyâs state president Pankaj Chaudhary asserting that the party was moving ahead with a firm resolve to return to office in UP for the third consecutive term. title: Spain train crash: Four Americans, one Canadian among 69 killed
text: Images from the high speed train crash in Spain. Authorities in Spain have identified 66 of the 69 people killed in last week's high-speed train collision, including four Americans and one Canadian. Spanish nationals made up the majority of the victims, with 54 confirmed dead. The crash occurred last Wednesday in the province of Toledo when a high-speed train slammed into another train that had stopped on the tracks. Among the other foreign nationals identified were citizens of France, Japan, Argentina, Mexico, Portugal, Tunisia and the Czech Republic, with one victim from each country. Authorities said three bodies were yet to be identified. Three people also remain missing â two Australians and one Japanese national. The latest collision came just nine months after another train crash farther south on the same Madrid-Seville line killed 46 people. The two incidents have shaken public confidence in Spain's rail network, which has long been recognised for its high speeds and safety record. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has promised a full investigation and improvements to restore trust in the railway system. The network carried around 45 million passengers last year, including millions of tourists. The crash occurred a month before the November 29 general election, in which Sanchez is seeking to extend his eight-year tenure as prime minister.
