title: EC can't monopolise voter awareness campaigns: SC; sets aside order denying permission to civil society
text: Voter awareness not EC's monopoly, says SC; sets aside SEC order BEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday said Election Commission did not have a monopoly over conducting âvoter awareness campaignsâ while disapproving ECâs refusal to permit a civil society group led by Aruna Roy from running a campaign to educate voters to choose representatives carefully and not barter their votes for bribes. Setting aside Rajasthan State Election Commissionâs Oct 9 refusing permission for the civil society in this regard, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana gave 48 hours to the SEC to consider their representation to run voter awareness campaigns for the final phase of Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti elections scheduled for Nov 14. SEC, through advocate Amit Kuri, said permission was refused keeping in mind the imposition of prohibitory orders for maintenance of law and order situation before the elections to keep at bay unwanted and anti-social elements. Royâs counsel Prashant Bhushan said it is a voter awareness campaign and not political activity and questioned the legitimacy of blanket imposition of prohibitory orders under Section 163 of BNSS to prohibit congregation for any political purpose. title: CAG Flags NMCâs Rs1,646cr Pending Utilisation Certificates, Negative Balance In Smart City Account
text: CAG Audit Nagpur: A Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) inspection audit of Nagpur Municipal Corporation (NMC) has flagged several financial and accounting lapses, including pending utilisation certificates (UCs) worth Rs1,646 crore, unadjusted advances of Rs4.2 crore and a negative balance of Rs52.44 crore in the Nagpur Smart and Sustainable City Development Corporation Ltd account (NSSCDCL). The audit observations raise questions about the civic bodyâs financial management, monitoring of govt grants and internal accounting controls. The findings are part of the inspection report on the accounts of NMCâs chief accounts and finance officer for the period covered by the audit. One of the major concerns is the non-submission of utilisation certificates worth Rs1,646 crore. The pending certificates relate to grants received from govt agencies and are required to establish that funds were spent for their sanctioned purposes. The delay could complicate financial accountability and affect the processing of future grants. The audit also highlights a negative balance of Rs52.44 crore in the account of NSSCDCL. The provisional balance sheet for 2024-25 showed the deficit under grants and contributions for specific purposes. The report also recorded a reduction in the grant balance for special city development projects. Another observation concerns advances of Rs4.20 crore paid to various officials and department heads that remain unadjusted. The audit sought details of pending advances, indicating shortcomings in monitoring and reconciliation of expenditure. The report also raised concerns over statutory accounting procedures. While NMCâs annual accounts for 2023-24 were examined and approved by the chief auditor, the accounts for 2024-25 had been prepared but further action was still underway. The audit sought an update on compliance with statutory requirements. Among other outstanding observations are a loan liability of Rs94.41 crore pending for over 16 years and avoidable interest payments linked to delays in loan-related procedures. Former NCP corporator Vedprakash Arya submitted a memorandum to municipal commissioner Vipin Itankar, demanding a high-level inquiry into the financial irregularities and accountability of officials concerned. title: âHe still has a lot to proveâ: Waqar Younis makes bold claim on Jasprit Bumrah
text: Jasprit Bumrah (ANI Photo) Former Pakistan captain Waqar Younis has hailed Jasprit Bumrah as the standout bowler in modern-day white-ball cricket but believes the Indian fast bowler still has more to establish in the Test format. Despite Bumrah 's impressive record of 234 wickets in 52 Tests at an average of 19.7 and a strike rate of 42.8, Waqar feels the pacer has not played enough red-ball cricket to be placed ahead of other leading fast bowlers. Watch Tilak Varma press conference: Indiaâs 3-0 lead, batting approach & more âThereâs no modern-day bowler of the same calibre as Bumrah with the white ball. Leave out Test cricket. He still has a lot to prove in Tests; he hasnât played as much. There are plenty of others, like Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood. You canât ignore some of the English bowlers either. But when you talk about T20 and one-day cricket, I feel that in terms of impact, Bumrah always delivers in crunch scenarios. And thatâs what matters,â Waqar said on the Shubhankar Mishra podcast. Waqar's assessment comes despite Bumrah's significant achievements in the longest format. The India pacer became the fastest Indian fast bowler to reach 50 Test wickets in 2018, accomplishing the milestone in his 11th match. He went on to claim his 100th Test wicket in his 24th appearance. Bumrah also became only the third Indian bowler to take a Test hat-trick in 2019. His performances in 2024 earned him the ICC Men's Test Cricketer of the Year award, while he finished the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy with 32 wickets in five Tests, a record haul for the series. The right-arm pacer has also been highly effective in England, taking 51 wickets in 11 Tests. One possible reason behind Waqar's assessment is Bumrah's limited availability in Test cricket compared with Australian quicks Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood. Injuries and workload management have affected his participation, and he is yet to play a Test for India this year. Bumrah is expected to return for India's two-match Test series in New Zealand next month, with a place in the World Test Championship final at stake. Waqar recalls Bumrah's match-winning spell against Pakistan While questioning Bumrah's standing in Tests, Waqar was unequivocal about the Indian pacer's influence in ODIs and T20Is. He particularly remembered Bumrah's decisive contribution in India's six-run victory over Pakistan at the 2024 T20 World Cup in New York. Waqar believes that spell demonstrated why Bumrah is such a valuable asset in high-pressure situations, particularly when a captain needs a breakthrough. âWhenever an India captain is in trouble, he always gives the ball to Bumrah. title: Is Jagan Reddy's 'regret' message a calculated alliance pitch for Congress?
text: A successful alliance with the INDIA bloc hinges on the YSRCP and Congress aligning, which could be Jagan Mohan Reddyâs biggest challenge NEW DELHI: Is YSRCP supremo YS Jagan Mohan Reddy signalling a drift towards the Congress-led INDIA bloc? Or is he trying to break free from the image of being soft on the BJP ? The former Andhra Pradesh chief minister has provided issue-based support to the BJP-led NDA government on several key legislations in Parliament while he was in power in the state. However, he has stayed away from joining any alliance till now. So, when Jagan Reddy recently regretted his âmistakeâ of supporting the 2023 NDA legislation for selecting the Chief Election Commissioner, it fuelled speculation about his future political moves. "We regret supporting the process under which the ruling party nominates the Chief Election Commissioner at the Centre. Neither the CEC nor the SEC should be appointed by the ruling party. The selection committee should comprise the Prime Minister, the leader of the opposition and the Chief Justice of India (CJI), with all three exercising their voting rights," the YSRCP chief said recently, calling the current selection system "flawed. " The timing and context of Jaganâs remarks are significant. So, is he rethinking his âsoloâ politics? And if yes, will the Congress be ready to tango with him in Andhra Pradesh? After all, alliances with regional parties have been the Congressâs biggest Achilles heel across states. Jaganâs support for NDAâs key Bills Jagan Mohan Reddyâs MPs backed the Modi government several times between 2019 and 2024, both in Lok Sabha and in Rajya Sabha, on many important legislations. However, when it came to stitching an alliance for the 2024 elections, the BJP ignored Jaganâs help and joined hands with his arch-rival Chandrababu Naidu. Together, TDP and BJP swept the polls in Andhra Pradesh, winning 164 out of 175 seats in the assembly and 21 out of 25 seats in Lok Sabha. The YSRCP was reduced to 11 seats in the assembly and 4 in Lok Sabha. Despite being spurned by the BJP and his partyâs shock defeat, Jagan Mohan Reddy remained confident about his BJP ties. After all, he still had 15 MPs (4 in Lok Sabha and 11 in Rajya Sabha) to provide the much-needed support to the BJPâs minority government at the Centre. Jagan even announced that his MPs would extend issue-based support to the NDA government in matters concerning national and state interest. But with the BJP heavily dependent on Chandrababu Naiduâs support for survival of its government at the Centre, there was little room for the saffron party to accommodate Jagan Reddy. Nearly two and a half years down the line, Reddy seems to have accepted this harsh reality and is perhaps gearing up to chart a new path for the next political challenge in 2029. Jagan vs Congress However, for any successful alliance with the INDIA bloc - the YSRCP and the Congress will have to be on the same page. And that perhaps would be the biggest challenge for Jagan Mohan Reddy. Jagan Mohan Reddy had a bitter parting from the Congress in 2010, a year after the death of his father YS Rajasekhara Reddy. YSR Reddy was in his second term as the chief minister of Andhra Pradesh when he died in a helicopter crash on September 2, 2009. Jaganâs supporters, who were many in number, lobbied hard with the Congress high command for the top post, but Sonia Gandhi did not budge and made K Rosaiah the chief minister. The Congress leadership did not approve of Jaganâs Odarpu Yatra, which was part of his announced plan to meet the families of many people who had sacrificed their lives after his fatherâs death. That set the stage for his eventual exit from the Congress, which he announced on November 29, 2010 in an open letter to Sonia Gandhi carefully written to ensure there was enough public sympathy for his second phase of political career. In the 2014 assembly elections, the YSRCP made an impressive debut and won 67 out of the 175 seats with a vote share of 44.46%, while the Congress could manage only a vote share of 2.8%. The Congress decision to bifurcate the state and create Telangana played a huge role in the partyâs declining political fortunes in the state. On November 6, 2017, Jagan embarked on the Praja Sankalpa Yatra and covered 3,648 km in 341 days, crossing 134 assembly constituencies. The Yatra, from YSR Ghat at Idupulapaya to the northeastern tip of Ichchapuram, powered Jagan Mohan Reddy to a historic mandate of 151 seats in the 175-member assembly in the 2019 elections. The Congressâs vote share was reduced to less than 1%. The Congress, since then, has been making efforts to reclaim its lost political space in the state. It roped in Jagan Reddyâs sister Y S Sharmila as part of the partyâs revival plan. Sharmila, who started her political career with her brother Jagan Mohan Reddy eventually drifted towards the Congress and was appointed president of Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee in January 2024. However, both Jagan Mohan Reddy and his sister Y S Sharmila failed to make an impact in the 2024 elections. The 2024 elections saw a dramatic collapse of Jaganâs electoral fortunes, and his party was reduced to only 11 seats. The Congress once again failed to make its presence felt. The 2029 challenge And that brings us to the 2029 elections - a do-or-die challenge for both Jagan Mohan Reddy and the Congress. Jaganâs remark on backing the CEC appointment Bill is his first open âregretâ for backing the BJP. But does this âopen regretâ mean an olive branch for the Congress? Former Congress leader and senior political commentator Sanjay Jha strongly feels that Jagan and Congress should come together, though he admits that this may not be easy. âPolitics is the art of the possible and I'm sure Jaganmohan Reddy is aware that Chandrababu Naidu has been an extremely close alliance partner of the Modi government. While the Congress doesn't have a base in Andhra like it used to have once upon a time. The support base of Jaganmohan Reddy is basically the Congress vote which moved away from the traditional Congress to the Congress that Jaganmohan Reddy, branded as the Congress of his father. So, if the merger were to happen, it would, frankly speaking, give them a huge advantage because then both the Central Congress and the Jaganmohan Congress could be on the same page,â Sanjay Jha says. However, he accepts that merger of the two parties could be a difficult process while stitching an alliance may be easier. âOnce a political party becomes independent and has power, they don't like to give it up in a hurry. The TMC or the NCP are good examples. In which case it could be an alliance,â Sanjay Jha adds. The third option, according to Sanjay Jha, is for the Congress to resurrect itself on its own strongly in Andhra by capturing both the anti-incumbent votes against Chandrababu Naidu and winning back the loyalist voters of the Congress who had moved over to Jaganmohan Reddy. We have seen several states across the country where the Congress has lost its government and eventually its support base but does little to reclaim it. In Andhra Pradesh, Chandrababu Naidu and the BJP are going all out to consolidate their position. title: AUSTRAHIND 2026 concludes with 36-hour joint validation exercise
text: AUSTRAHIND 2026 Thiruvananthapuram : The fifth edition of the India-Australia joint military exercise AUSTRAHIND 2026 concluded in the city on Saturday. Indian and Australian troops conducted an intensive 36-hour joint validation exercise involving simulated military operations across forest, island and coastal terrains. The final exercise, conducted on Oct 30 and 31 under Chapter VI of the United Nations Charter, tested the operational coordination and interoperability of the two forces in complex security and emergency situations. The joint operations involved sea and air insertions, securing beachheads and port facilities, casualty evacuation, humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR), protection of vital installations and counter-insurgency and counter-terrorism operations. The exercise brought together Indian Army and Australian Defence Force, with support from Indian Navy, Indian Air Force, Vizhinjam International Port Authority and Kerala Fire and Rescue Services. The participation of multiple agencies enabled the forces to test coordinated responses across land, sea and air domains. The final validation was witnessed by Major General Matt Burr of Australian Defence Force; Major General Kapil Rana, GOC, 54 Infantry Division, Indian Army; and Commodore A J Dowling, New Zealand Defence AttachÃ© to India and Australia. AUSTRAHIND 2026 began on Oct 19 at Foreign Training Node in Thiruvananthapuram and involved around 120 personnel each from the Indian and Australian armies. The Indian contingent comprised troops from the Garhwal Rifles and personnel from other arms and services, while the Australian contingent included soldiers from its 13 Brigade. A New Zealand observer delegation also participated for the first time. The annual bilateral exercise, conducted alternately in India and Australia, is aimed at strengthening military cooperation, developing interoperability and enabling the two armies to exchange operational experience, tactics and procedures. The fourth edition was held at Irwin Barracks in Perth, Australia, in Oct 2025. The latest edition reaffirmed Indiaâs and Australiaâs commitment to strengthening defence cooperation, joint operational preparedness and regional peace and stability. title: Officer who presided over Gokul meet promoted
text: Kolhapur : Maharashtra govt has promoted deputy collector Mausami Chougule to the rank of additional collector and posted her as assistant commissioner (rehabilitation) at the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar divisional commissionerate. However, she will continue in her present assignment until the completion of the Special Intensive Revision exercise, as she is currently on election duty. The promotion order also makes it clear that the elevation is temporary and subject to the outcome of petitions pending before the Bombay high court and Supreme Court over seniority disputes. Govt said the promotion has been granted under the provisions of the General Administration Departmentâs May 7, 2021 decision governing such cases. Chougule is currently serving as sub-divisional officer of Karvir division in Kolhapur district. She recently presided over the meeting convened to elect the chairperson of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers Federation, popularly known as Gokul Dairy. The meeting was adjourned without electing a chairman after she cited lack of quorum. The chairpersonâs election has since become the focus of a political and legal tussle. The Satej Patil-led Samavichari Aghadi holds 13 elected directors, while the Mahayuti-backed panel has 12. The Mahayuti directors stayed away from the meeting, resulting in the quorum falling short. Under the federationâs bylaws, 14 directors must be present to conduct the meeting, while the chairperson can be elected by a simple majority. The decision to adjourn the meeting has been challenged in the Bombay high court. The matter is scheduled to come up for hearing on Monday. Chougule was unavailable for comment. However, officials said her transfer is part of a larger round of promotions involving several deputy collectors. âShe currently holds the post of sub-divisional officer. If the HC directs that the adjourned Gokul meeting be reconvened, she can still preside over it,â a senior official said on condition of anonymity. Meanwhile, speaking to reporters in New Delhi on Sunday, Satej Patil said Nov 3 is the deadline for electing a new chairperson. âThe first meeting was adjourned on the technical ground of quorum. We hope the high court decides the matter on Monday,â Patil said. He also warned that any attempt by state govt to appoint expert directors with voting rights to alter the balance of power would be challenged in court. âI do not think Mahayuti will succeed. No director from our side will leave us. Mahayuti should start preparing for the next election due after five years,â Patil said. title: Debates before PUTA poll bring teachersâ concerns to fore
text: Patna University Patna : The Patna University Teachersâ Association (PUTA) election has generated unusual interest this year, with candidates for president and general secretary posts participating in the associationâs first-ever debates ahead of the Nov 4 polls. The debates have revived discussion about PUTAâs role in safeguarding university autonomy, protecting teachersâ financial interests and representing the academic community of Bihar . Elections are being held after a gap of more than three years for seven key posts, including president, two vice-presidents, general secretary, two joint secretaries and treasurer. Results are likely to be announced on the polling day. For an organisation that has long played a leading role in Biharâs teachersâ movement, the election is about more than choosing office-bearers. The next leadership will inherit a body closely associated with struggles over salaries, promotions, pensions and teachersâ rights. PUTA emerged after the 1952 reorganisation of Patna University as a teaching-cum-residential institution and the creation of Bihar University for colleges outside Patna. It soon became one of the most influential teachersâ associations in the state. One of its early leaders was Vina Mazumdar, who joined Patna University as a political science lecturer in 1951 and later became the associationâs first secretary. Teacher activist Nawal Kishor Chaudhary said Mazumdar represented a generation that combined academic work with public engagement. Among PUTAâs earliest campaigns was the successful effort to protect Patna Universityâs teaching-cum-residential character. Teachers from other universities joined the movement, forcing the withdrawal of a proposed government Bill. The association later became part of wider state-level teachersâ movements through the Federation of University Teachersâ Associations of Bihar, formed in 1967, and the Federation of University Service Teachersâ Associations of Bihar, formed in 1971. The two bodies launched joint agitations in 1979. PUTA has also taken up issues directly affecting teachers. In 2003, it organised a demonstration against disputed pay fixation for promoted readers and professors. In 2010, it moved the Patna high court over a three-month delay in salary payments. In 2017, it urged the state govt to ensure regular salary and pension payments in universities across Bihar. title: Fake US voters? China-linked accounts flood X with divisive posts ahead of midterms
text: China-linked accounts pose as US voters on X A China-linked influence operation known as Spamouflage is active ahead of the US midterm elections, with accounts allegedly posing as American voters and circulating divisive political content on X. The findings were reported by New York-based social media intelligence firm Graphika, which tracks online influence networks. In a blog post published on Friday, Graphika said it had identified a network of accounts linked to the long-running operation that were posting content targeting US politics, social issues and the electoral process. The activity, it said, closely resembled tactics documented ahead of the 2024 US presidential election. âThe accounts post content questioning election integrity and the legitimacy of US democracy,â Graphika said in its blog. The findings come amid longstanding warnings from US intelligence and national security officials about foreign influence operations targeting American voters. Russia, China and Iran have previously been identified as countries running online campaigns aimed at shaping political narratives and influencing public opinion. Watch Trumpâs Cheesecake Factory Controversy EXPLODES as Kimmel Launches Fresh Attack However, analysts, quoted by news agency AP, have said China's approach has largely focused on undermining public confidence in US democratic institutions rather than supporting one presidential candidate over another. China has rejected allegations of election interference. Liu Chang, spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in Washington, said Beijing âhas never and will never interfere in the US elections." Despite the concerns raised by Graphika, some researchers have questioned the network's ability to influence mainstream political opinion. Darren Linvill, who co-directs Clemson University's Watt Family Innovation Center Media Forensics Hub and has tracked Spamouflage activity, said the operation was unlikely to sway political discussions. âThere is no chance it tips the balance in any real political conversation,â Linvill told AP. âSpamouflage is famously bad at mimicking real Americans," he added. âIt's outside their wheelhouse.â Linvill said the network's impact was more evident in its efforts to suppress information and target individuals, particularly members of the Chinese diaspora. The accounts linked to the operation âvery frequently attack and harass members of the Chinese diaspora communityâ, he said, describing the activity as part of a wider effort by Beijing to silence views it opposes. Graphika also identified specific accounts that appeared to have changed their identities or content strategies to target US political audiences. The firm also flagged four accounts with a history of Spamouflage activity that have since adopted MAGA-style personas, amplifying content associated with the political movement. Another account, which has more than 2,00,000 followers and presents itself as a Philippine culture blog, was found posting pro-China material alongside divisive content focused on US politics. Graphika said it could not establish whether the account had been hijacked, sold or otherwise transferred to a different operator, leaving questions about who currently controls it. title: US midterms 2026: Who is Ami Bera, Indian-American Democrat seeking re-election from California's newly redrawn district
text: Bera was first elected to the US House in 2012 and took office in January 2013. Indian-American Democratic Congressman Ami Bera is seeking re-election to the US House of Representatives in the November 3, 2026, general election, but will contest from California's newly redrawn 3rd Congressional District instead of the 6th District he currently represents. Bera will face Republican candidate Robb Tucker, a member of the Nevada County Board of Supervisors, in the race. The 3rd District covers large parts of Placer, El Dorado and Nevada counties and extends into the city of Sacramento. Bera, who lives in Elk Grove, California, has represented the state in Congress since 2013. He is the longest-serving Indian-American member of the US Congress and serves on the House Foreign Affairs Committee and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence. Who is Ami Bera? Born in Los Angeles to Indian immigrant parents with roots in Gujarat, Bera is a physician by training and a lifelong Californian. He earned his bachelor's degree and medical degree from the University of California, Irvine. After graduating from medical school in 1991, he completed his residency in internal medicine at California Pacific Medical Center, where he eventually became chief resident. He then practised medicine in the Sacramento area and held leadership positions in healthcare management. Bera later served as medical director of care management at Mercy Healthcare, where he developed strategies to improve care across its seven-hospital system. He also served as chief medical officer for Sacramento County, focusing on healthcare access, affordability and job creation. He subsequently joined the University of California, Davis, as a clinical professor of medicine and associate dean for admissions and outreach, helping train future doctors and support community healthcare initiatives. Bera's political career and priorities Bera was first elected to the US House in 2012 and took office in January 2013. He has since won re-election six times, building a political career centred on healthcare, economic opportunity and public service. In Congress, he serves on the House Foreign Affairs Committee as ranking member of its Subcommittee on East Asia and the Pacific. He is also a member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and the New Democrat Coalition, a group of Democrats that advocates economic growth, innovation and fiscal responsibility. Bera has said his experience as a doctor shapes his approach to public service, with an emphasis on listening to constituents and working across party lines. His congressional office says it has helped return more than $23 million to local taxpayers through assistance with issues such as delayed veterans' benefits and Social Security payments. It has also helped more than 36,000 Sacramento County residents since 2013. Bera currently represents California's 6th Congressional District, which lies entirely within Sacramento County. Following changes to California's congressional district boundaries, he decided to run in the 3rd District in the 2026 election. The contest will pit Bera against Tucker, a Republican who serves on the Nevada County Board of Supervisors. The outcome will determine who represents the district in the US House for the next term. Bera has lived in Sacramento County for more than three decades with his wife, Janine, who is also a physician. They have a daughter, Sydra. You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. title: HC declines interim order on Kolkata ward delimitation
text: Calcutta High Court Kolkata: Calcutta High Court on Thursday refused to pass any interim order restraining authorities from calling an election to the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) based on delimitation â increasing wards from 144 to 209 â saying that it is for the state to decide âin what manner constituencies or KMC wards will be delimited or alteredâ and it is not for the âcourt to dictate. â âIt is now well settled that it is not for the Court to dictate the manner in which the same would be done. If a delimitation exercise is carried out in conformity with the provisions of the relevant statute, and the constitutional provisions, and no breach of such provisions have been committed, the Court cannot interfere with the same,â the vacation bench held. A resident within KMC limits, Dipu Das, had moved the bench of Justice Hiranmay Bhattacharyya challenging the Sept 11 notification, a formal delimitation notification. Legal questions were raised challenging the KMC municipal commissioner recommending delimitation when the corporation stood dissolved. Justice Bhattacharyya was of the prima facie view that the commissioner, who was appointed as the administrator after the corporationâs dissolution, can make any recommendation for a delimitation exercise as required under Section 601 of the 1980 Act. Though no interim order was passed on the reasoning that it âwould affect the interest of the public at large as the Corporation in that event would have to function in the absence of elected councillors,â the matter was kept for hearing and both KMC as well as Das were directed to file affidavits. Das alleged that the process of delimitation was taken on the basis of electoral rolls instead of the actual population, excluding a substantial number of residents from consideration. It was also claimed that the boundaries of the wards have been drawn without considering geographical contiguity, compactness and administrative convenience. âSuch delimitation exercise was undertaken upon being influenced by previous electoral results with the mala fide intention of securing partisan advantage of the ruling political party. It also resulted in unequal municipal representation,â Dipu alleged. Advocate General Surajit Nath Mitra, representing KMC, stressed that Article 243 ZG of the Indian Constitution bars interference by courts in any law relating to delimitation of constituencies. It was submitted that the Municipal Commissioner was appointed on June 8 and is âvested with all powers of the members of the Corporation.â He further contended that objections and suggestions were invited at every stage of the delimitation exercise but Das had not submitted any objection against the alteration and instead simply approached the court. This was noted by the single judge, who also held that âat various stages objection(s)/suggestion(s) were invited and nothing appears to this Court at this stage that such power was exercised in breach of any provisions of 1980 Act or the provisions of the Constitution of India.â You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in Kolkata Stay updated with the latest Kolkata news. title: Sharing the runway: Lapwings, lizards put RGIA flights at risk
text: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport (RGIA) HYDERABAD: From red-wattled lapwings and barn swallows to Bengal monitor lizards, bats and black-naped hares, a growing range of wildlife is posing a threat to aircraft at the Rajiv Gandhi International Airport (RGIA), with wildlife strikes recording a steady rise over the past three years. According to data obtained by TOI through an RTI application to the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), as many as 442 wildlife strikes involving aircraft were reported at RGIA between Jan 2023 and Aug 2026, with annual incidents climbing from 101 in 2023 to 114 in 2024 and 133 in 2025. The growing frequency of such incidents has also raised concerns over their impact on flight operations. Last month, an IndiGo flight from Pune to Hyderabad, carrying over 100 passengers, suffered a bird strike while approaching RGIA. Although the aircraft landed safely, a subsequent inspection revealed minor damage to its nose section, forcing the airline to cancel its onward Hyderabad-Chandigarh service. In Feb this year, another IndiGo flight operating from Jaipur to Hyderabad reportedly suffered a bird strike during landing. The pilot carried out a safe landing upon noticing the impact. The list of wildlife involved goes well beyond birds. Rabbits and different species of bats, including insectivorous and fruit and wild cats, have figured in the strike records. Among identified bird species, red-wattled lapwings topped the list with eight incidents, followed by barn swallows (six), rock pigeons (five), Indian thick-knees (four) and black kites (three). Food accumulation, garbage dumping, landfills and water bodies around the airport have been identified as potential wildlife attractants. Several areas around Shamshabad, including Katedan and Jalpally, continue to witness frequent roadside garbage dumping, particularly by migrant labourers who dispose of waste while heading to construction sites. âDespite repeated instructions to hand over their waste to Swachh auto vehicles, many refuse to do so. The challenge is compounded by the transient nature of the workforce. By the time awareness efforts begin to yield results, many workers move out and a fresh batch of labourers arrives, making it difficult to sustain behavioural change. Meanwhile, the garbage dumping at Raviryal has been brought to a halt over the past few months, after initiating biomining to clear the legacy waste dump,â said an official in GHMC âs sanitation wing. Landing and approach account for over 60% of strikes What makes the trend concerning is that aircraft are most vulnerable during landing and approach, when they are closer to the ground. Of the 442 incidents, 276 occurred during landing or approach, while another 164 were reported during take-off or departure. In 2025 alone, 88 of the 133 strikes occurred during landing and approach. The consequences are not limited to bird hits. The data shows that wildlife activity resulted in operational consequences, including go-arounds, air turn-backs, precautionary landings, diversions and delays, in 5.5% of cases in 2025. The figure stood at 6.8% in 2024 and 2.6% up to July 2026. Airport adopts multiple wildlife-control measures To contain the threat, RGIA has adopted several wildlife hazard management measures aimed at reducing the presence of birds and animals around aircraft movement areas. These include installing a habitat fragmenter to discourage waterbirds from congregating near flight paths, using black-light traps to reduce nocturnal insects that attract birds and bats, and managing vegetation along approach paths to minimise shelter and nesting opportunities for wildlife. âNylon-net fencing has been installed at vulnerable locations to restrict the movement of rabbits and other terrestrial animals into operational areas. The airport has also undertaken garbage-hotspot mitigation to reduce food sources for scavenging birds. Other initiatives include software-based wildlife surveillance to identify hotspots,â said an official in DGCA. title: US Supreme Court rejects Trump's push to isolate 20,000 California ballots over citizenship claims
text: Trump administration argued that setting aside the disputed ballots was a limited measure that would allow officials to verify voter eligibility without preventing legitimate votes from eventually being counted. The US Supreme Court on Monday rejected the Trump administrationâs emergency request to set aside around 20,000 ballots in California over claims that the voters may not be US citizens. The decision came a day before the final day of voting in the crucial midterm elections, dealing another legal setback to US President Donald Trumpâs efforts to intervene in the electoral process. The court refused to intervene in the dispute involving voters flagged by the federal government as likely noncitizens on Californiaâs voter rolls. It did not explain its decision. No justice publicly dissented. The rejection came without the court asking California officials to respond to the administrationâs appeal. California governor Gavin Newsom welcomed the decision, saying on X, âThe Court rejected Trumpâs emergency request without even asking the other side to respond. Democracy won.â The ruling marks another setback for the administration, which has faced repeated defeats in its efforts to have the disputed ballots kept separate until the votersâ citizenship status is verified. California Attorney General Rob Bonta said courts had rejected the administrationâs attempts to interfere in the stateâs elections four times, including at the district court, the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals and the Supreme Court. âCourts have now rejected the Trump Administrationâs attempts to interfere in Californiaâs elections not once, not twice, not three times, but four times â from the district court to the Ninth Circuit to the U.S. Supreme Court,â Bonta said. âThis latest decision should put an end to the Administrationâs attempt to disrupt Californiaâs elections through emergency court orders," he added. Voting by noncitizens rare in US The Trump administration has made identifying suspected noncitizen voters a priority this year, despite such cases being rare in the US. It argued that setting aside the disputed ballots was a limited measure that would allow officials to verify voter eligibility without preventing legitimate votes from eventually being counted. However, California officials questioned the reliability of the federal government's list, saying it contained errors and could lead to eligible voters being disenfranchised. The administration's request also faced criticism over its timing, with election officials pointing out that it came only weeks before voting concluded. The Justice Department has acknowledged that its list was not entirely reliable. During a hearing on whether to lift an order preventing the administration from threatening to prosecute election workers who allowed potentially ineligible voters to cast ballots, US District Court Judge Trina Thompson questioned the accuracy of the federal data. âWould you agree there's a high error rate?â the San Francisco-based judge asked Justice Department attorney Kenneth Kao. âThat's a fair statement,â Kao said. âThat's why we ask for the registrars' aid in verifying these are all valid voters.â However, Bill Essayli, the federal prosecutor overseeing the Justice Department's Los Angeles office, expressed confidence that the people on the list were not eligible to vote. âThis isnât speculation. This isnât a theory,â Essayli said at a news conference, while later acknowledging that the list could contain errors. Lower courts also reject administration's request The Supreme Court's decision followed a series of rulings in favour of California. A district court had earlier rejected the Justice Department's request, warning that separating the ballots could disrupt the election and undermine public confidence in the democratic process. US District Judge David O. Carter said such a move could âwreak havocâ on the midterm elections. âIf the Executive can discount votes and threaten an ongoing election due to unproven allegations, then our democracy is in danger,â Carter wrote. A 2-1 appeals court panel subsequently upheld his order. One judge appointed by Trump and another appointed by former President Joe Biden voted in favour of California. The third judge, also appointed by Trump, dissented, arguing that the state's refusal to separate the ballots encouraged the âviolation of federal lawâ. In a separate development on Monday, US District Judge James Boasberg ruled against the administration's attempts to make last-minute demands of California election officials, saying they likely violated the Constitution. âThe Executive Branch has likely violated the Constitutionâs Elections Clause, which commits authority over election rules to the states and Congress alone,â Boasberg wrote. However, in a separate ruling later on Monday, Boasberg declined to issue another order restraining the administration. He said the Democratic groups that had filed the lawsuit lacked legal standing and that the issue had already been addressed by states and courts. Millions of California ballots already returned California has been conducting voting by mail since early October. The state sends ballots to all its approximately 23 million registered voters. More than 6 million ballots had already been returned, according to Associated Press election data. State election officials had argued that identifying and separating the disputed ballots at this stage would be logistically impossible. The Supreme Court had also rejected Trump's attempt to restrict mail-in voting across the country in September, although it has sided with his administration in several other emergency appeals. Reacting to Monday's decision, Kristen Clarke, general counsel of the NAACP, criticised the administration's efforts. âThe DOJâs baseless challenge was yet another attempt at federal overreach and voter suppression,â she said. âWe will not stand for the Trump Administrationâs bullying campaign, and we will continue to use every tool at our disposal to ensure the American peopleâs voices are not silenced.â You use AI every day. title: IOC chapters worldwide mobilise for Rahul Gandhiâs âDelhi Chaloâ rally
text: Irshath, extreme left, Dhaliwal, center, Ausuf Khan, extreme right AMRITSAR: The November 1 âDelhi Chaloâ rally called by Congress leader and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has triggered a mobilisation drive among Indian Overseas Congress (IOC) chapters worldwide, with leaders urging members and office-bearers to travel to India to strengthen the partyâs campaign against alleged electoral irregularities. With the âVote Bachao, Desh Bachaoâ mega rally scheduled at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi, IOC leaders across Europe and other regions are making efforts to encourage greater participation. Several overseas office-bearers have already arrived in India, including IOC Germany president Balwinder Singh Gurdaspuria ,IOC UK president Kamal Dhaliwal etc. are already camping in the country ahead of the rally. Talking to TOI on Tuesday IOC general secretary for Europe Mohamed Irshath appealed to people to participate peacefully in the November 1 march, linking electoral confidence with Indiaâs international standing. âFrom Europe, we see how Indiaâs democratic reputation shapes the respect it commands abroad. That reputation must be sustained by institutions that answer citizensâ concerns openly,â he said. Backing Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, Irshath urged people across political affiliations to join the campaign, saying electoral fairness was fundamental to public trust in democratic institutions. Kamal Dhaliwal who is also preparing to contest the ensuing assembly elections from the Amargarh assembly constituency of Malerkotla district said there was considerable enthusiasm among IOC members worldwide to participate in the campaign. He alleged that several decisions of the BJP-led government had failed to benefit Indians living abroad and said overseas Indians had concerns that needed to be raised. The mobilisation, he added, reflected the desire among Congress supporters overseas to strengthen the party and back Rahul Gandhiâs political campaign. IOC Austria president Ausaf Khan said he held a virtual meeting with representatives of more than a dozen IOC chapters on Monday and urged them to reach Delhi for the rally. He said the effort was aimed at bringing overseas Congress workers together to strengthen the organisation and demonstrate support for the partyâs leadership. He said that the rally is part of the Congress-led Oppositionâs campaign against alleged irregularities in electoral rolls and its demand for accountability from the Election Commission adding that Rahul Gandhi has called upon students, farmers, labourers, women, youth and traders to join the march, arguing that protecting voting rights was essential to safeguarding democracy. Interestingly, the rally has faced objections from Delhi traders, who fear traffic restrictions and security arrangements could affect festive-season business. However, the Congress remains focused on its electoral fairness campaign, while IOC chapters worldwide are working to mobilise members and office-bearers for the November 1 gathering. For IOC leaders, the Delhi gathering is also an opportunity to demonstrate that Congress supporters abroad remain engaged with political developments in India and are willing to contribute to the partyâs organisational efforts. title: $12 billion battle for US Congress: Musk, Soros and other billionaires pour in cash
text: The 2026 midterm elections in the U.S. are on track to raise a staggering $12 billion, marking the most expensive campaign in history. The 2026 US midterm election campaign is expected to become the most expensive in the country's history, with total spending projected to reach nearly $12 billion, according to Opensecrets, an independent organisation that monitors campaign finances. A significant share of the expenditure is being driven by outside political groups, particularly super political action committees (Super PACs), which are investing heavily in key electoral contests ahead of the November 3 election. Billionaire businessman Elon Musk has emerged as the biggest individual donor, contributing nearly half a billion dollars to support republican candidates. Much of his spending has focused on Texas, where several of his companies are headquartered. BBC Verify has examined the campaign finance figures to assess how much has been spent, who is funding the candidates and where the money is going. The president says he has held 31 rallies over 27 days, along with many tele-rallies, a term that's been used recently in US media to describe when a politician phones into a rally. How much money has been spent? US campaign finance regulations place limits on the amount individuals, political parties and traditional political action committees (PACs) can contribute directly to candidates. However, Super PACs can accept unlimited donations from individuals, corporations, labour unions and other political committees. Although they cannot donate directly to candidates, they can independently spend money to support or oppose them. The latest filings with the federal election commission (FEC), covering spending up to mid-October, show that more than $9.5 billion had already been spent during the current election cycle. PACs and Super PACs accounted for more than half of the expenditure, contributing approximately $5.5 billion. Their spending almost doubled over the preceding couple of months. Candidates, political parties and outside organisations are required to report their expenditure to the FEC. However, the complete figures will only become available after the elections. Based on spending patterns from previous election cycles, Opensecrets estimates that the final amount could reach $11.9 billion. This would represent an increase of around 30% compared with the 2022 midterm elections. Who are the biggest political donors? According to the liberal-leaning Brennan Center for Justice, the 40 largest donors had contributed a combined $2.4 billion by October 14, marking a record amount for this stage of a midterm election cycle. Michael Beckel, a US campaign finance expert, said the 2026 elections had broken spending records, with an increasing proportion of the money coming from wealthy individuals and organisations. Apart from individual contributions, organisations also provide substantial funding to PACs. Geosor Corp and the Fund for Policy Reform, both established by billionaire financier George Soros, have together donated $102 million to liberal groups. Former New York City mayor and businessman Michael Bloomberg has been another major democratic donor, contributing more than $60 million. On the Republican side, several wealthy contributors have made large donations. These include Jeff Yass, head of a major trading firm, and business supply company owners Richard and Elizabeth Uihlein, who have collectively contributed more than $100 million to Republican causes during the campaign, according to FEC records. Musk, however, remains the biggest individual contributor, having donated nearly $500 million as of October. A large portion of his contributions has gone to America PAC, a Super PAC he established in 2024, as well as the republican-aligned senate leadership fund. Much of the funding has been directed towards the Texas Senate contest, where republican candidate Ken Paxton is facing democrat James Talarico. America PAC has invested more than $45 million in the Texas race. It has also allocated approximately $10 million each to senate contests in Michigan and Ohio. The cryptocurrency industry has also emerged as a significant contributor this election cycle. Brendan J Glavin of Opensecrets said ripple and coinbase had together donated $63 million to Super PACs seeking to advance the interests of the crypto sector. Where is the campaign money being spent? Political campaigns and outside groups use their funds for a range of activities, including recruiting workers for grassroots voter outreach, organising rallies and other campaign events, and conducting internal opinion polls. However, advertising accounts for the largest share of campaign expenditure, particularly television commercials. According to advertising tracking firm AdImpact, $11.15 billion had been spent on political advertising by the end of October. Beckel said traditional broadcast television continued to receive the largest share of advertising expenditure, although spending on digital platforms was also increasing. AdImpact's tracking showed that the biggest advertising investments were concentrated in Senate contests in Michigan, Texas and Ohio, followed by Iowa and Maine. You use AI every day. title: US midterm elections 2026: What they are, why they matter and when results will be out
text: US midterms voting to be conducted on November 3 The US midterm elections are nationwide elections held every two years, halfway through a president's four-year term. This year's elections will take place on Wednesday (early Thursday, as per Indian time) with voters choosing members of Congress as well as several state and local officials. Unlike presidential elections, midterms do not decide who occupies the White House. Instead, they determine which party controls Congress for the next two years, making them a crucial test of President Donald Trump's political standing and his ability to push through his agenda. What are the US midterm elections? The US Congress has two chambers, the House of Representatives and the Senate, and midterm elections determine the composition of both. All 435 seats in the House are contested every two years, as members serve two-year terms. In the Senate, where members serve six-year terms, roughly one-third of the 100 seats come up for election every two years. This time, 35 Senate seats, including two special-election contests, are at stake. Alongside congressional races, voters in several states will also elect governors and other state and local officials. Watch Indian-Americans Give Republicans A 4:1 Cash Edge With $15.8 Million Bet On Trump In U.S Midterms What is at stake in the 2026 midterms? Republicans currently hold narrow majorities in both chambers of Congress. The 435-member House has 218 Republicans, 214 Democrats, one independent who caucuses with Republicans and two vacant seats. A party needs 218 seats for a majority. Meanwhile, the Senate has 53 Republicans and 47 Democrats and allied independents, with 51 seats required for a majority. Democrats need a net gain of four seats in each chamber to take control of both. Chances of Democrats (prediction) The outcome could therefore hinge on a small number of closely contested races. Who might win? Why do the midterms matter for Trump? The party controlling Congress has considerable influence over the president's ability to govern. Congress passes legislation, approves government spending and oversees the executive branch. The Senate also confirms presidential nominees to key government positions, including federal judges and senior administration officials. If Democrats take control of either chamber, they could make it harder for Trump to pass legislation, influence budget negotiations and intensify congressional scrutiny of his administration through hearings and investigations. A Democratic majority in the House could also revive discussions of impeachment, although impeachment by itself would not remove the president from office. Removal requires a two-thirds vote in the Senate. Trump would remain president regardless of the election outcome. He would retain his executive powers and the ability to veto legislation, but a divided Congress could significantly constrain his domestic agenda. The stakes extend well beyond Capitol Hill What issues are shaping the vote? The cost of living, inflation, immigration and the economy are among the major concerns for voters. Foreign policy, including the war involving Iran, is also part of the political debate. Trump's approval ratings and public perceptions of his administration's performance are likely to influence the results. Midterm elections are often viewed as a referendum on the sitting president, with the party in the White House frequently losing congressional seats. Disputes over voting rules, election administration and the drawing of congressional district boundaries have also become contentious issues. When will voting take place and when will results come? Voting will take place on Tuesday, November 3, across the United States. Polling hours vary by state, and there is no single nationwide closing time. The first polling stations in parts of Indiana and Kentucky are scheduled to close at 6 pm Eastern Time, which is around 4.30 am on November 4 as per Indian Standard Time. Results are expected to emerge through the night, but close contests may take longer to resolve. Election officials must count outstanding ballots, verify results and, where necessary, conduct recounts or deal with legal challenges. News organisations may project winners before every ballot has been counted. Such projections are not official results. State election authorities certify the final results, a process that can take days or weeks. The House is where the battle for congressional control is expected to be particularly intense. Where can you check the results? US Election Assistance Commission (EAC): A federal agency that provides election information and links to official state election offices. USA.gov: The US government's official portal, which directs users to state websites for election results and voting information. Federal Election Commission (FEC): The federal agency responsible for campaign finance oversight. It provides information on federal elections but does not publish live results or certify current election outcomes. State election offices remain the primary source for official results, including vote counts, recounts and final certification. What happens if an election result is contested? A close result can lead to recounts, court challenges and disputes over ballot validity. State officials handle the initial counting and certification process, but the US Constitution gives the House and Senate the power to judge the elections, returns and qualifications of their own members. A candidate or sitting member can challenge a congressional election result. In the House, such disputes are referred to the House Administration Committee, while Senate challenges go to the Senate Rules Committee. The respective chamber ultimately decides whether a member should be seated. This power could become significant if a handful of unresolved races determine which party controls Congress. Any House contests still unresolved when the new Congress convenes in January would be considered by the incoming House. The process can become politically contentious, particularly when party control is at stake. A disputed result may also leave a seat vacant while legal or congressional proceedings continue. title: Trump escalates attacks on Muslim Senate hopeful, drawing Arab American rebuke
text: US President Donald Trump (left) and Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed (right), who is seeking to become America's first Muslim Senator. President Trump intensified attacks on Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed at a rally in Port Huron Sunday, calling him a âjihadistâ who was âon the side of the terroristsâ and questioning his loyalty to US. The remarks drew condemnation from a former Trump ally in the Arab American community. Trump said El-Sayed, a former Detroit health official, would âhave to go through a metal detector before heâs allowed to go into Senateâ. He repeatedly invoked the 9/11 attacks and compared blocking El-Sayed from the Senate chamber with passengers fighting hijackers aboard United Flight 93. El-Sayed would become the first Muslim American senator if elected. He has denied any ties to extremist groups and called attacks on his loyalty âshamefulâ. At a Grand Rapids rally later Sunday, he responded to Trumpâs repeated mockery of his name: âI donât even care that he remembers my whole name because he can just go on and call me âsenatorâ after Nov,â El-Sayed said. âI will be Senator Muhammad to you, bro.â Watch Trumpâs âBlonde Beautyâ Moment Backfires? Critics Accuse POTUS Of 'Creepy' Crowd Talk Bishara Bahbah, a founder of Arab Americans for Trump, which helped lead Trumpâs outreach to Arab American voters in 2024, called the comments racist. âThe presidentâs statements are out of line,â he said. âThey are crossing a red line. They are racist.â The organisation has since been renamed Arab Americans for Peace. Bahbah said the remarks were unacceptable to Arab and Muslim communities, including Christian Arabs, and voters would remember them on Nov 3. Trump won Dearborn in 2024, becoming the first Republican presidential candidate since 2000 to carry the city, which has one of the countryâs largest concentrations of Arab Americans. Many voters had opposed the Biden administrationâs handling of the Gaza war. The race between El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers to succeed retiring Democratic Senator Gary Peters is among a handful that could determine control of the Senate. With Republicans under pressure over inflation, fuel prices and the Iran war, Trump has portrayed El-Sayed as a threat to US. Trump also declared he had come to Michigan âto keep a jihadist Muslim Brotherhood member from becoming a United States senatorâ. There is no evidence El-Sayed has any affiliation with the Muslim Brotherhood. Republicans have cited a 2012 social media post by his half-sister, Eman Abdelhadi, who wrote that âmy family has long been MBâ and described their motherâs involvement with the group in the early 1970s. El-Sayed was born in the US to Egyptian immigrant parents who divorced when he was young. He was raised by his father, not his biological mother. Rogers questioned El-Sayedâs loyalty during their final general-election debate, asking, âAre you for America, or are you for these terrorist groups overseas?â El-Sayed replied: âIâm proud of our Constitution that guarantees all of us the right to pray as we choose to pray.â Rogers repeated the Muslim Brotherhood allegation before Trumpâs appearance. Trump attacked El-Sayedâs links to streamer Hasan Piker, who appeared with him during the primary campaign. Piker has said âHamas is a thousand times betterâ than Israel, called some Orthodox Jews âinbredâ and said âAmerica deserved 9/11.â El-Sayed has also faced criticism over his rhetoric. After an attack on a Detroit-area synagogue, he said âhurt people hurt peopleâ. The attacker had lost four relatives in an Israeli airstrike on Lebanon a week earlier. El-Sayed later apologised, saying he had not intended to justify the attack. Senator Bernie Sanders, appearing with El-Sayed in Grand Rapids, accused Trump and his allies of using Islamophobia because they had ânothing to sayâ about healthcare, housing and income inequality. âAll they can do is foment hatred and divisiveness,â he said. title: Barmer poll row: State election chief orders probe, says result can be challenged only in court
text: Jaipur: Rajasthan State Election Commissioner Rajeshwar Singh said Thursday that the commission would investigate how a candidate whose nomination papers were rejected was allotted a symbol, allowed to contest and declared the winner of Gadra Road gram panchayat sarpanch election in Barmer. Singh, who was on a Barmer visit, made it clear that the commission cannot overturn the result. Any challenge to Pooraramâs election, he said, will have to be filed before a competent court through an election petition. Speaking to TOI, Singh said the matter was brought to his notice Thursday, and the commission would look into the facts. âIf any official is found guilty, action will be taken in accordance with the rules,â he said, adding that the commission would investigate whether the election symbol was allotted deliberately or by mistake. In conversation with TOI a day earlier, while Pooraram defended his victory and dismissed the rejection of his nomination as a rumour, his closest rival, Kuldeep Singh , who finished second, alleged through his brother and representative that Pooraramâs nomination was rejected through a public notice issued by the election officials. âThe affected party can approach the court and file an election petition within a month,â Singh Box âCourt can invalidate Barmer sarpanch poll result' SEC canât overturn result after winner is declared: PDT Achary Jaipur: State Election Commission (SEC) cannot overturn an election result once a candidate has been declared the winner, and only a competent court can invalidate it on the basis of an election petition, former Lok Sabha secretary general and constitutional expert PDT Achary said. He was commenting on the Barmer case in which a candidate whose nomination was rejected was allegedly allotted an election symbol and declared sarpanch. Achary said the âOnce a candidate is declared winner, the election is complete and the result canât be overturned by SEC. The SEC can investigate the matter and take appropriate action against the official concerned if found guilty. Since the official is a govt employee, departmental proceedings may also be initiated against him,â Achary said. He added that the court, while delivering its verdict, could also issue directions for action against the official concerned. The matter relates to the sarpanch election held earlier this week in Barmerâs Gadra Road gram panchayat where the returning officer allegedly allotted an election symbol to Pooraram even though his nomination papers were rejected. Pooraram subsequently won the election, raising questions over the poll process. title: US midterms 2026: Polling guru Allan Lichtman, who accurately predicted 9 of last 11 presidential races, sees headwinds for Democrats
text: Historian Allan Lichtman/Image: Getty Images Historian Allan Lichtman, who predicted nine of the last 11 US presidential elections correctly, expects Democrats to take control of both chambers of Congress in next week's midterm elections, forecasting a setback for President Donald Trump's Republican Party. Lichtman, a professor at American University in Washington, DC, said national polling, Trump's approval ratings, voter enthusiasm and early voting trends indicate that Democrats are gaining ground ahead of the November 3 elections. In an interview with The Times (UK), Lichtman said the political environment was particularly unfavourable for Republicans, pointing to the president's low approval ratings and the historical losses suffered by the party controlling the White House during midterm elections. "When the approval rating for a president is as low as Trump's, on average the White House party loses 40 House and six Senate seats," Lichtman said. He clarified that the figures were not his prediction but an indication of the political conditions facing Republicans. Lichtman said Democrats currently hold an advantage of seven to 11% points over Republicans in the generic congressional ballot, which measures voter preferences for which party should control Congress. He considers this measure a more reliable indicator than polls focused on individual races. He also pointed to a shift in voter enthusiasm. While Republicans typically record higher turnout, Lichtman said Democrats appeared more motivated this time. He added that early voting figures were also favourable to the party. The historian puts Democrats' chances of winning control of the Senate at 67%, with a 51-49 majority his most likely outcome. Republicans currently hold a 53-47 advantage in the Senate, meaning Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take control. Lichtman expects the party to make gains in Maine, North Carolina, Ohio and Texas while retaining its seat in Michigan. He also identified Alaska as a potential Democratic pickup, with former Representative Mary Peltola among the candidates he expects to benefit. He pointed to the competitiveness of races in traditionally Republican states as another indication of the changing political landscape. "It's amazing that Democrats are competitive in South Carolina, which Trump won by 18 points," he said. "Kansas has not sent a Democrat to the Senate since the Great Depression in 1932 and yet that's a neck-and-neck race, as is Iowa." Lichtman also expects Democrats to take control of the House, where Republicans currently hold a narrow 218-214 majority. He puts the party's chances of winning the chamber at more than 90%. He attributed some of the Republican Party's difficulties to what he described as weak candidates, naming Ken Paxton in Texas, Roger Marshall in Kansas and Darline Graham in South Carolina. The historian also criticised the influence of wealthy donours and outside spending in the election campaigns. He argued that large financial contributions were affecting the political contest and pointed to billionaire Elon Musk's support for Republican candidates. Lichtman compared the current political climate to the 1966 midterm elections, when Democrats suffered major losses under then-President Lyndon B Johnson amid growing opposition to the Vietnam War and domestic unrest. His latest assessment comes after he incorrectly predicted that Democratic candidate Kamala Harris would defeat Trump in the 2024 presidential election. He also missed the outcome of the 2000 race between Al Gore and George W Bush. You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

title: Amit Shah to join T BJPâs padayatra on Nov 2
text: Hyderabad: Union home minister Amit Shah will participate in a BJP Telangana padayatra in Hyderabad on Nov 2, marking his first visit to the state since May 2024, after several proposed trips were deferred or cancelled. BJP plans to step up its campaign against Congress over the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The Telangana programme, announced by BJP Telangana president N Ramchander Rao on Monday, would be held under the slogan âLoktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao (Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy)â. It comes a day after Congress and other Opposition leaders are scheduled to hold a rally at Delhiâs Ramlila Maidan on Nov 1, alleging irregularities in electoral roll revision and demanding the removal of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The back-to-back programmes are part of BJPâs effort to counter the Oppositionâs allegations over SIR and mobilise party workers through public outreach. Shahâs participation in both Telangana and Haryana is expected to give the campaign a national profile. Shahâs proposed visits to Telangana have faced repeated disruptions. His last visit was in May 2024 for Lok Sabha election campaigning. Several subsequent programmes were postponed or cancelled, including a visit scheduled for Oct 3 and 4 this year. That trip, which was to include events in Toopran and Karimnagar and meetings with party leaders, was cancelled at the last minute. Rao has accused Congress of spreading misinformation about SIR and challenged chief minister A Revanth Reddy to identify eligible voters whose names were wrongly deleted. He also criticised Congress leaders for planning to attend the Delhi rally while Telangana faces rainfall deficits and water shortages. After Hyderabad, Shah is scheduled to participate in a padayatra in Karnal (Haryana) on Nov 5. title: FM Nirmala Sitharaman weighs in on Tata row: 'Should be resolved amicably, internally'
text: Sitharaman calls for an amicable resolution to the Tata Trusts-Tata Sons dispute, saying the conglomerate is critical to the Indian economy and should return to normal functioning MUMBAI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday the dispute between Tata Trusts and Tata Sons should be resolved amicably, describing the salt-to-software conglomerate as a critical component of the Indian economy. In her first public comments on the dispute, she said govt would prefer an early resolution that allowed the group to return to normal functioning. "I know the brand value of Tata, the contribution that the Parsi community has made to make Tata a huge global brand. I also know the expanse of activity in which Tatas are invested in. So, this is a very critical component of the Indian economy, and therefore it has to be amicably settled among themselves," Sitharaman said during a fireside chat organised by Financial Express. FM Nirmala Sitharaman was responding to a question on the govtâs reaction to Congress LOP Rahul Gandhiâs allegations that it was attempting to destabilise the Tata Group . Rahul has accused the Modi govt of attempting to âcriminally destroyâ the group and treating Indian businesses as political playthings amid the dispute between Tata Trusts, which own the holding company, and Tata Sons, which owns the operating businesses. Sitharaman said the matter required commercial judgement and cordiality between the parties. âI think these are very delicate matters and matters where a lot of commercial and business acumen will have to work. Business cordiality will have to work,â she said. Asked whether govt would intervene, she described the issue as sensitive and said she would not like to comment on it. FM also rejected allegations of govt favouritism towards select corporate groups, pointing out that industrial houses targeted in parliamentary criticism were also welcomed and courted for investment by opposition governed states such as Karnataka and Telangana. On 23% growth in GST collections during Oct, she rejected suggestions that high revenues merely reflected a rise in imports (which had risen 42%). She said most imports comprised essential raw materials and intermediate goods required by domestic manufacturers to meet export demand. The minister also rejected allegations that govt was creating instability or undermining democratic processes. She said opposition parties could not have legitimately won elections and formed govts in Karnataka, Telangana and Himachal Pradesh if elections were compromised or regime changes were possible only through street agitation. She criticised the opposition for holding mock parliaments outside legislatures and walking out of legislative debates instead of using their constitutional mandate. With around 100 elected MPs, she said, the opposition should engage in debates on the floor of the House rather than walk out when govtâs responses challenged its claims. You use AI every day. title: EC orders officialsâ transfers ahead of 2027 UP polls
text: TNN Lucknow : The Election Commission of India has issued transfer and posting guidelines for officials directly associated with election duties ahead of the UP Assembly elections, directing the state govt to ensure compliance by Nov 30. UP CEO Navdeep Rinwa said on Tuesday that officials completing three years of service in the same district during the preceding four years, as of May 31, 2027, must be transferred. The guidelines cover district election officers, returning officers, assistant returning officers, ADMs, SDMs, tehsildars, block development officers, divisional commissioners, municipal commissioners and officials of development authorities. Police, excise and transport department officials of sub-inspector rank and above will also come under the transfer policy. The commission has prohibited postings in officersâ home districts. Officials who served in a particular constituency or district during the previous Assembly election or subsequent byelections cannot be retained or reposted there in specified election-related positions. Officials posted at state headquarters, technical personnel unrelated to election work and those serving as sector officers or zonal magistrates are generally exempt. Officials retiring by May 31, 2027, are also exempt but cannot hold key election-related positions. The chief secretary and DGP must submit a consolidated compliance report to the commission by Nov 30. title: AP civic elections: Big cities record poor turnout, polls largely peaceful
text: A young voter comes out of a polling station after casting vote in Visakhapatnam on Sunday. Pic-A Sarath Kumar People stand in a queue to cast their vote for Vijayawada municipalÂ corporation elections, in VIjayawada on Sunday. Pic: Mahesh G. A young voter comes out of a polling station after casting vote in Visakhapatnam on Sunday. Pic-A Sarath Kumar People stand in a queue to cast their vote for Vijayawada municipalÂ corporation elections, in VIjayawada on Sunday. Pic: Mahesh G. A young voter comes out of a polling station after casting vote in Visakhapatnam on Sunday. Pic-A Sarath Kumar 1 2 Vijayawada : Despite an intense electoral battle between the ruling NDA alliance and the opposition YSRCP, voter turnout in major urban centres of Andhra Pradesh remained disappointing in the urban local body elections held on Sunday, with Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Guntur recording polling percentages of around 52 to 57%. A young voter comes out of a polling station after casting vote in Visakhapatnam on Sunday. Pic-A Sarath Kumar The decision of the State Election Commission (SEC) to conduct polling on a Sunday, which was also a general holiday, failed to translate into a higher voter turnout, as a considerable section of urban electors appeared reluctant to come out and exercise their franchise. In contrast, several smaller towns witnessed a better response, with polling touching around 70% in some municipalities. Only 51.47% of voters in Vizag exercised their franchise, according to official data available till 10 pm, the lowest turnout among the major urban local bodies of Andhra Pradesh that went to polls on Sunday. Vijayawada registered a little over 55%, while neighbouring Guntur recorded approximately 57%. The relatively poor turnout in the three major cities stood in contrast to the enthusiastic participation reported in several smaller urban local bodies, where voters turned out in larger numbers despite the electoral contest being less intense. Interestingly, the low participation in the major cities came despite a high-voltage campaign by the NDA alliance and YSRCP, with both sides treating the municipal elections as a prestige battle. The outcome is expected to determine control over civic bodies and provide an indication of the political mood in urban areas. The SEC said the final polling percentages were still being compiled and that it could take several hours to release the consolidated figures. However, preliminary trends indicated that almost all municipal corporations had recorded turnout below 60%, raising concerns over declining voter participation in urban local body elections. Meanwhile, State Election Commission has declared polling held in three wards across three urban local bodies on November 1 void following confirmed incidents of booth capturing and ordered repolling on Monday. State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha issued orders for fresh polling on November 2 from 7 am to 5 pm, based on reports submitted by the respective district election authorities. The commission found that the polling process in the affected booths had been vitiated, depriving voters of their right to exercise their franchise freely. Repolling will be held at polling station No. 14/1 in Ward 14 of Chimakurthy Municipality, polling stations 23/1 and 23/2 in Ward 23 of Macherla Municipality, and polling station No. 30/3 in Ward 30 of Ananthapuramu Municipal Corporation. The SEC directed the local election authorities to widely publicise the fresh polling schedule and make necessary arrangements to ensure peaceful and transparent polling. Voters participating in the repoll will have indelible ink applied to their left middle finger as per the prescribed procedure.
