title: MC to revise Sector 17 parking tender after general house rejects fee hike
text: Free parking at multilevel parking at sector 17 Chandigarh (story pics) Chandigarh: The municipal corporation (MC) is set to lower the proposed annual tender amount for Sector 17 paid parking lots after the general house rejected a hike in parking charges in Sept. The parking committee will deliberate on the revised amount next week, paving the way for the fresh tender to be floated this month. The tender amount, previously finalised at around Rs 3 crore annually based on the proposed higher parking rates, will now be revised to reflect the existing charges. With a newly appointed joint municipal commissioner taking charge of parking, the MC expects to move ahead with the tender process this month. âWith the increased rates, the tender amount was finalised at around Rs 3 crore annually. However, since the general house decided to retain existing parking charges, the amount needs to be revised. As per a rough estimate, it may come down to around Rs 2 crore. The final decision will be taken by the parking committee after considering all financial aspects and calculations,â sources in the MC said. With MC elections approaching, political parties are reluctant to support any increase in paid parking charges. In view of the decision of the general house to retain existing rates, smart features will not be introduced in Sector 17 parking lots. âThe smart features proposed for Sector 17 paid parking lots were planned along with higher charges. Since the rates will not be increased now, these features will not be installed,â sources said. The MCâs plan to introduce a new sector-wise paid parking system, beginning with Sector 17, aims to bring in private agencies or bidders to operate parking lots professionally. Sector 17 has 20 paid parking lots, including an underground multi-level parking facility, all of which were included in this first-of-its-kind initiative. title: Roadways strike brings bus services to a halt across Hisar, Sirsa and Hansi
text: Photo for representation Hisar : Commuters across Hisar, Sirsa and Hansi faced disruptions to their travel plans on Monday as Haryana Roadways employees intensified their strike over pending payments and other service-related demands. More than 380 buses remained off the road across the three depots, affecting long-distance, local and rural routes, as well as services used by school and college students. In Sirsa, more than 100 buses remained off the road after employees under the Roadways Joint Forum began an indefinite strike on Sunday evening. Besides morning services for students, buses to Delhi, Chandigarh, Gurugram, Pokaran and Hanumangarh were suspended. The strike also affected the Dabwali depot, as protesters staged sit-ins at bus stands. Joint Forum representatives Satbir Karwasra and Chiman Lal Swami said kilometre-scheme buses would also remain off the road. Forum members added that employees recruited through the Haryana Kaushal Rozgar Nigam had extended support to the agitation. Alleging that inspectors had been deployed as conductors on a few kilometre-scheme buses early on Monday, Forum representatives said the move was contrary to Roadways rules. According to Swami, a delegation had raised issues concerning pending overtime, night-duty allowance, LTC and medical bills with the general manager. The GM sought time until Dec 2 to transfer the outstanding amount to employeesâ accounts, but workers rejected the assurance. They said TA bills for 2023 and 2024, 13 medical bills, LTC claims and overtime dues dating back to April were still pending. In Hansi, around 72 buses remained off the road for the third consecutive day. Employees staged a protest at the depot and burnt an effigy of the Hisar depot general manager. Committee member Manjit Sorkhi said the affected services included night, rural and long-distance routes. The strike also kept 210 buses of the Hisar depot off the road. Employees said TA-DA, LTC and medical reimbursements had been pending for nearly four years and warned that the stoppage would continue until their demands were addressed. title: Indian Sikh couple's New Zealand asylum claim rejected after NZ$336,000 crore debt dispute with Punjab moneylender
text: New Zealand rejects the refugee claim of an Indian couple who said they feared for their life in India as a moneylender was threatening them. A New Zealand immigration tribunal has rejected the refugee protection claims of an Indian Sikh couple who said they feared threats from a Punjab-based unlicensed moneylender after a loan of NZ$56,000 (approximately â¹30 lakh) allegedly ballooned to nearly NZ$336,000 (around â¹1.8 crore). The couple had approached New Zealand authorities seeking refugee protection in April 2024, claiming that the lender had threatened them and their family over the unpaid debt. However, the Immigration and Protection Tribunal dismissed their appeals, finding that the dispute arose from a financial disagreement rather than persecution on grounds recognized under the Refugee Convention. In its October 29 decision, tribunal member B L Burson also found insufficient evidence that the couple faced a real risk of serious harm if they returned to India. According to reports,, the tribunal noted a growing pattern of migrants seeking refugee protection after taking on substantial private debts to finance overseas education and employment, only to struggle with repayment. How did the couple's debt increase sixfold? The unidentified couple's financial difficulties began in Punjab in 2015, when the wife planned to pursue further education overseas. In December that year, she borrowed money from a bank to finance her studies. Her father-in-law provided land ownership documents as security, while the family also borrowed money from relatives. After her New Zealand student visa was approved in January 2016, her husband and father-in-law borrowed the equivalent of NZ$56,000 from an unlicensed moneylender in March 2016 to repay the earlier debts. The loan carried an interest rate of 2% a month and was supposed to be repaid within two years. The husband joined his wife in New Zealand in May 2016. The loan remained unpaid. By 2018, the lender had started demanding repayment, with the couple alleging that the demands escalated into threatening phone calls and messages. The husband's father signed an affidavit disowning the couple from his property. The situation allegedly worsened in March 2024, when the moneylender assaulted the father and threatened to kill him and his son. Following a complaint to the local village council and police, a compromise was reached under which the lender agreed to stop pursuing the father and deal only with the husband. The following month, the lender sent the husband a calculation showing that the outstanding debt had increased to nearly NZ$336,000. Moneylender allegedly threatened to keep husband in prison Even after the couple moved to New Zealand, the husband continued receiving threatening messages from the lender. The lender allegedly claimed to have powerful connections across India and threatened to initiate multiple court cases against the husband, saying he would ensure that he remained in prison. The lender subsequently initiated legal proceedings in India after two cheques issued by the husband were dishonoured due to insufficient funds. Fearing the consequences of returning to India, the couple applied for refugee protection in New Zealand in April 2024. Why did the New Zealand tribunal reject their asylum claims? The tribunal dismissed the couple's appeals without an oral hearing, describing the claims as manifestly unfounded. Burson concluded that the dispute was fundamentally about a loan default and did not amount to persecution connected to a ground recognized under the Refugee Convention. He also found that the couple had not provided sufficient evidence to establish that they faced a real risk of serious harm that would qualify them for refugee or protected-person status. In assessing the alleged death threats, the tribunal reasoned that killing the husband would undermine the moneylender's efforts to recover the outstanding debt. The tribunal also considered that the couple could seek protection from Indian police and pursue legal remedies through India's judicial system. While acknowledging the difficult circumstances faced by the couple, Burson said New Zealand's international protection obligations were not intended to address every form of hardship. title: 'Already been uprooted': Akhilesh, Awadhesh target Amit Shah over 'Angad's foot' remark
text: NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav on Saturday dismissed Union home minister Amit Shah 's claim that the BJP was firmly entrenched in Uttar Pradesh, questioning him over crimes against women and Dalits in the state. Party MP Awadhesh Prasad also hit back at Shah's "Angad's foot" remark, saying the BJP's political footing had "already been uprooted". According to PTI, Akhilesh made the remarks while responding to Shah's assertion that the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh was firmly established and could not be dislodged. Watch 'Will Implement UCC If...': Amit Shahâs BIG Poll Promise In Uttar Pradesh, Akhilesh Takes A Dig "Home minister should look into why women face so much injustice in Uttar Pradesh, why the state witnesses so many murders and why people from the Dalit community are among the worst affected," Akhilesh said. He questioned the BJP's claims of political stability in the state, shifting the focus to the government's record on law and order and the treatment of women and Dalits. Reacting to Shah's claim that the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh was firmly entrenched, Samajwadi Party MP Awadhesh Prasad said the party had already lost ground in the state. Responding to Shah's comparison of the BJP's position to "Angad's foot", Awadhesh said, "The foot has already been uprooted." Awadhesh said the BJP had failed to retain several seats in the recent Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council elections despite making every effort. He cited the party's defeats in Varanasi, Lucknow and Agra, and also referred to its loss in Prayagraj, a prominent educational centre. He also pointed to the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, saying the BJP had failed to achieve its target of winning all 80 seats in Uttar Pradesh. The SP won 37 seats, while the Congress secured six, taking the INDIA bloc's tally to 43 seats in the state. Shah made the remarks on Friday while addressing the BJP's state working committee meeting at the Dr Ram Manohar Lohia National Law University auditorium in Lucknow. The meeting was attended by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak, and other senior BJP leaders. Shah expressed confidence that the BJP would return to power in the 2027 Assembly elections, comparing the party's position in Uttar Pradesh to "Angad's foot" and saying nobody could dislodge it. title: Vijayawada mayoral race turns into a three-way battle with high political stakes
text: Retired IPS officer AB Venkateswara Raoâs (ABV) entry has added a third dimension to the battle for control of Vijayawada Municipal Corporation, offering voters an alternative to Andhra Pradeshâs dominant political blocs. Congress, CPI and CPM extended their support to his candidature Vijayawada : The mayoral election has become a three-cornered contest over competing political narratives, with the ruling NDA seeking an endorsement of its governance and alliance unity and YSRCP aiming for a comeback after its 2024 defeat. Retired IPS officer AB Venkateswara Raoâs (ABV Rao) entry has added a third dimension to the battle for control of Vijayawada Municipal Corporation, offering voters an alternative to Andhra Pradeshâs dominant political blocs. NDA views victory in the stateâs political epicentre as a validation of its record, while YSRCP sees the election as an opportunity to recover political ground. For NDA, the election is as much about political symbolism as it is about control of the corporation. The alliance has fielded Jana Sena leader Vangaveeti Radha Krishna, whose candidature carries the legacy of his late father, Vangaveeti Mohana Ranga, a name that continues to command influence in sections of Vijayawada politics. Radha Krishnaâs victory would also mark a breakthrough for Jana Sena in NTR district. Despite being a key constituent of the ruling alliance, Jana Sena currently has no elected representation in either Vijayawada city or NTR district. The three assembly segments within the city are represented by TDP and BJP. A victory for Radha Krishna would therefore be projected as evidence of alliance cohesion and Jana Senaâs growing political footprint. The NDA campaign has largely centred on the âtriple-engine govtâ argument, with leaders claiming that alignment between the Centre, the state govt and the municipal corporation would help secure greater funding for civic infrastructure and urban development projects. For YSRCP, the stakes are equally high. After suffering a crushing defeat in the assembly elections, the party views Vijayawada as an opportunity to demonstrate that it remains a force in Andhra Pradesh politics. A victory in one of the stateâs most prominent urban centres would provide a psychological boost and help the party counter perceptions of political decline. However, the factor that has made the election unusually competitive is the emergence of AB Venkateswara Rao, popularly known as ABV, as a serious third contender. Backed by the INDIA bloc, Rao entered the race promising an alternative to both the ruling alliance and the opposition YSRCP. While the INDIA bloc has only a limited presence in Andhra Pradesh, particularly after bifurcation, Raoâs candidature has succeeded in changing the tone of the campaign. Unlike his rivals, who largely relied on broader political messaging, Rao attempted to build his campaign around a detailed civic agenda. He promised abolition of the Vacant Land Tax and a freeze on property tax hikes for three years. By promising tax reliefs, especially on the property tax, which in its reformed form has grown by more than 135% in the last five years, Rao attracted the attention of people. He also promised round-the-clock drinking water supply, better storm-water and underground drainage systems, measures to tackle flooding and waterlogging, and transparent municipal governance. He also sought to position himself as an anti-establishment candidate, attacking both NDA and YSRCP and arguing that Vijayawadaâs long-pending civic issues required professional urban management rather than partisan politics. Political observers say the significance of Raoâs candidature lies not merely in whether he wins but in whether he can convert voter discontent into support for a credible third alternative. A strong performance by the former IPS officer could encourage similar experiments in other urban centres where voters are increasingly focused on civic infrastructure and governance issues. The verdict, therefore, is likely to be viewed not merely as a municipal result but as an indicator of the direction in which Andhra Pradeshâs political landscape may be moving. Congress leader Jandhyala Shankar won as Vijayawada mayor in 1987, although TDP swept the assembly elections a couple of years earlier. T Venkateswara Rao from CPI won as Vijayawada mayor in 1995, at a time when TDP secured the highest majority in the preceding assembly elections. Vijayawada electorate has a history of electing independents and opposition candidates as mayors defying the larger trend. title: Indian-American voter Vasant Bhatt says his decision to speak out in favor of James Talarico was entirely his own. Now his parents are concerned about his safety
text: Vasant Bhatt says his parents are concerned about his safety after he became an online target following his announcement of support for Democratic candidate James Talarico. The Texas midterm took an interesting turn after 21-year-old Vasant Bhatt , a student at the University of Houston, urged the Indian-American community to reject the hatred against India and Hinduism and vote for Democrat James Talarico against Ken Paxton. Bhatt, who identified with conservative politics so far, was mocked online and asked to go back to India. MAGA activists defended their India-hatred, making Bhatt an example of how Indian-origin people who are US citizens by birth take the side of Indian-Americans and consider themselves Indian despite being born in the US. Bhatt was dropped from a conservative news website, Campus Reform, after his viral social media post. Speaking to TOI.com, Bhatt said his parents grew concerned about the amount of public attention his social media post got and the hostility he received thereafter. "Their primary concern has been my safety and well-being," the second-generation Indian-American said. Having interned with Ted Cruz's team earlier, Bhatt developed his alignment with conservative politics, but the India-hatred in Texas by MAGA drove him away. He is now politically homeless, though he said several Democratic political strategists reached out to him in the aftermath of the controversy. "I remain politically independent and my decision to speak out was entirely my own," Bhatt said. Can't be a perpetual foreigner at home On October 19, Bhatt announced that he cast his ballot for James Talarico. "As a second-generation Indian American, I am thoroughly disgusted by the xenophobia, racial resentment, and increasingly brazen attacks on my identity. My family has contributed to the American story through hard work, sacrifice, and an unwavering belief in the opportunities this nation promises. I am every bit as American as anyone else, and I will not tolerate being treated as a perpetual foreigner in the country I call home," he explained the reason and then urged every eligible Texan to go out and vote. "This election is about the kind of state and country we are prepared to defendâand the principles we refuse to surrender," he added. He tagged Talarico's team and Texas Democrats in his post. Ken Paxton vs James Talarico Texas saw historic turnout in the early voting, with more than 4.5 million voters already having cast their ballots. In five of six public polls released over the past week, Talarico leads Paxton. The sixth poll, from Fox News, puts both candidates at 49 percent. Kalshi traders gave Talarico a 65 percent chance of winning on Monday, and the site's margin market points to a win of about 2.2 points. Polymarket had Talarico at 64 percent. No Democrat has won a US Senate race in Texas since Lloyd Bentsen in 1988. Paxton, as the Attorney General of Texas, launched a massive crackdown on H-1B abuse in the state. title: âTata, bye-byeâ to BJP: Dharmendra Kashyap joins Samajwadi Party after being left out of Rajya Sabha candidate list
text: Dharmendra Kumar Kashyap recently joined the Samajwadi Party after not being nominated for the Rajya Sabha (File photo) LUCKNOW: BJP leader Dharmendra Kumar Kashyap joined the Samajwadi Party (SP) on Tuesday, ending speculation triggered by a Facebook post he made after his name was left out of the BJPâs list of Rajya Sabha candidates for Uttar Pradesh. SP president Akhilesh Yadav welcomed the OBC leader into the party, news agency PTI reported. Addressing a press conference alongside Yadav, Kashyap claimed that people in Uttar Pradesh were fed up with the BJP government because of its âpoorâ law and order situation. He also alleged that chief minister Yogi Adityanath âs bulldozer action did not target people from his caste and was directed at the poor. Yadav said Kashyapâs entry would strengthen the SP. According to sources, Kashyap, a former minister, had been hopeful of securing a Rajya Sabha ticket from the BJP but was not included in the partyâs list of candidates, PTI reported. The BJP fielded state minister Dharampal Singh and Shruti Gangwar, daughter of former Union minister and former Jharkhand governor Santosh Gangwar, from Bareilly district. After the BJP announced its list, Kashyap posted a picture of a sunset by the sea on Facebook on October 7, accompanied by the words âTata Bye-Byeâ. The post triggered speculation about his possible return to the SP. Kashyap is considered one of the prominent political faces of the Kashyap community in Rohilkhand, in northwestern Uttar Pradesh, PTI reported. He left the SP and joined the BJP in May 2013. He was elected to the Lok Sabha from Aonla in 2014 and 2019 but lost the seat by a narrow margin in the 2024 elections. The Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections are due early next year. title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay cracks down after 17 prisoners break out of Theni sub-jail; deputy jailor suspended, senior officials transferred
text: Chennai's Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has ordered the suspension of the deputy jail superintendent in charge of Thekkampatti sub-jail. CHENNAI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay has ordered the suspension of a deputy jailor in charge of Thekkampatti sub-jail and initiated disciplinary action against prison officials following the escape of 17 prisoners in Theni district on October 26. All 17 escapees were subsequently recaptured. N Nageswaran, deputy jailor who had been holding additional charge of the sub-jail since August 6, 2024, was suspended with effect from October 30. The suspension order, issued under the Tamil Nadu Civil Services (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, cited lapses in supervision and failure to maintain adequate vigilance over inmates and prison staff. The suspension will remain in force until further orders. The jailbreak occurred on the night of October 26, when 17 remand prisoners allegedly staged a medical emergency, overpowered prison guards and escaped from the facility. Police launched a search operation to track them down. Drones were used to locate eight escapees hiding in thick vegetation away from the prison, and all 17 were eventually apprehended and returned to custody. Watch CM Vijay Urges PM Modi To Keep Lok Sabha Strength At 543, Opposes Population-Based Delimitation Taking serious note of the security breach, the state government has also ordered changes in the prison administration. R Krishnaraj, who was serving as superintendent of Madurai Central Prison, has been transferred to Salem Central Prison in the same capacity. Earlier, the government transferred Director General of Police (Prisons) Sandeep Rai Rathore to Tamil Nadu Generation and Distribution Corporation (TANGEDCO) as chief vigilance officer. K Shankar has been appointed the new additional director general of police for Prisons and Correctional Services. Vijay directed prison officials to discharge their duties with diligence and maintain strict security at correctional facilities. The government made it clear that negligence, lack of vigilance and lapses in the discharge of official responsibilities would invite stringent disciplinary action. The latest measures are part of the state government's response to the jailbreak, which exposed security and supervision lapses at the sub-jail. title: Punjab notifies re-election in 28 Patiala MC wards; polls by Nov 18
text: Patiala : The Punjab government has notified fresh elections in 28 wards of the Patiala Municipal Corporation and directed that the polls be held by Nov 18. The notification was issued by Local Government Department Secretary Ghanshyam Thori under Sections 7-A and 7-B of the Punjab Municipal Corporation Act, 1976. It follows the Supreme Court âs Sept 28 order in SLP (Civil) No. 3894 of 2025 and connected petitions, which set aside the election in these wards. Fresh polls in two additional wards, also covered by the apex courtâs order and taking the total number of affected wards from 28 to 30, are yet to be notified by the state government, said BJP Patiala president Vijay Kumar Kuka. Copies of the notification were sent to the State Election Commissioner for necessary action. The deputy commissioner, additional deputy commissioner (urban development), Municipal Corporation commissioner and the concerned sub-divisional magistrates also received copies, along with the monitoring committee constituted by the Punjab and Haryana High Court Chief Justice. A copy was also sent to the Controller of Printing and Stationery for publication in the Extraordinary Gazette. Reservation The notification lists 13 reserved wards. Nine are reserved for women (Wards 22, 33, 37, 41, 43, 51, 53, 55 and 57). Two are reserved for Scheduled Castes (Wards 26 and 52), while two are reserved for Scheduled Caste women (Wards 1 and 45). The remaining 15 wards (4, 6, 12, 14, 16, 28, 32, 34, 36, 38, 40, 44, 46, 48 and 50) are unreserved. Judicial oversight As per the apex courtâs directions, the monitoring committee headed by retired High Court judge Justice Rajeev Sharma will supervise the process. Senior members of the High Court Bar have been nominated as local commissioners to oversee proceedings, including the filing and scrutiny of nominations, allotment of symbols and polling. All stages of the election process will be videographed, and the recordings will be submitted to the committee if complaints of irregularities are received. The case arose from petitions filed by opposition candidates who alleged that they were prevented from filing nomination papers during the December 2024 civic elections. They accused ruling-party workers of obstruction and alleged inaction by the police. In March 2025, the Supreme Court appointed former High Court judge Justice Nirmaljit Kaur as a one-member fact-finding commission. After examining the claims, the commission submitted its report in Nov 2025. The Supreme Court accepted its findings and annulled the results in the 28 wards. The re-election is expected to intensify political activity among ticket aspirants in the city. Observers say it will serve as a key test of partiesâ organisational strength ahead of the next Assembly elections. title: North Andhra records over 65% turnout
text: People line up to vote at a polling station in Visakhapatnam on Sunday Pic-A Sarath Kumar Visakhapatnam : Municipal elections across North Andhra districts, excluding Visakhapatnam city and Vizianagaram Municipal Corporation, recorded average voter turnout of over 65%, with brisk polling in seven municipalities and two Nagar panchayats. Narsipatnam municipal elections in Anakapalli district became a high-profile prestige battle for the family of Andhra Pradesh assembly speaker Chintakayala Ayyanna Patrudu. His wife, Padmavathi and younger brother Chintakayala Sanyasi Patruduâs wife Anitha were at the centre of the keen electoral contest in their hometown. Narsipatnam has a total of 49,099 voters across 40 wards, with polling conducted at 76 polling stations. Women voters outnumber men in the municipality. Two wards were elected unanimously, with TDP candidates B. Reddy Sattibabu and Marukuri Ramana declared elected unopposed after the nomination papers filed by YSRCP candidates were invalid. In the remaining 38 wards, 84 candidates contested the councillor posts. The TDP fielded 33 candidates, the YSRCP 38, Jana Sena four, CPM and BSP one each, while seven independents were also in the fray. Narsipatnam was upgraded to a municipality in 2011, and its first municipal elections were held in 2014. The chairperson post was reserved for a BC woman. Anitha, wife of Sanyasi Patrudu, contested as a TDP candidate and became chairperson, while her husband served as vice-chairperson. Disputes between the families of the two brothers intensified, and Ayyannaâs brother joined YSRCP before the general elections. The present elections have once again brought the political fortunes of the Ayyanna Patrudu family into the spotlight. Narsipatnam recorded a voter turnout of 72.6 per cent. Of the 49,099 voters, 35,647 exercised their franchise by the close of polling. Nearly half the electorate had cast their votes by 1 p.m. In another keenly watched contest in Yelamanchili municipality in the district, 76.61 % polling was recorded. The municipality has 36,526 voters across 32 wards. Sitting chairperson Pilla Rama Kumari of BJP, contesting as the NDA alliance candidate, faced YSRCP nominee Boddapu Tulasi. A total of 77 candidates contested the 32 councillor seats. As many as 27,981 voters exercised their franchise. Polling in both Narsipatnam and Yelamanchili gathered momentum from the beginning, crossing the 60 per cent mark by 3 p.m. In Vizianagaram district, Vizianagaram municipality recorded 59.64 per cent polling, while Bobbili registered 70.33 per cent. Nellimarla Nagar Panchayat recorded the highest turnout in the district at 77.96 per cent. In Parvathipuram Manyam district, Palakonda Nagar Panchayat recorded 69.64 per cent polling, while Salur municipality registered 65.64 per cent. Parvathipuram municipality recorded a turnout of 63.62 per cent. In Srikakulam district, Ichchapuram municipality registered 64.9 per cent polling, while Palasa-Kasibugga municipality recorded 68.33 %. title: Imran Khan apologises as Bombay High Court slams the actor for participating in protests despite being an OCI card holder: 'If an Indian had done the same thing elsewhere would it have been tolerated?'
text: The Bombay High Court on Monday pulled up actor Imran Khan , a US citizen holding an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card, for participating in a protest related to the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC)-Special Intensive Revision (SIR) issue in Mumbai. The court observed that the fundamental right to protest is reserved for Indian citizens, following which the actor tendered an unconditional apology and assured the bench that he would not participate in any such demonstration in the future. A bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna observed that India's magnanimity was evident from the fact that Khan, despite being a US citizen, was first served a notice asking him to leave the country rather than being deported immediately. Watch Imran Khan Receives October 28 Deadline to Leave India After Joining Mumbaiâs CJP Protest Appearing for Khan, senior advocate Venkatesh Dhond promptly submitted an undertaking on behalf of the 43-year-old actor, assuring the court that he would neither participate in protests in the future nor encourage anyone else to do so. He also tendered an unconditional apology. The court subsequently scheduled Khan's petition challenging the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) notice for further hearing on December 7. The notice had directed him to leave India by October 28 over his alleged participation in a demonstration against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in Mumbai last month. The bench also extended its earlier order keeping the FRRO notice in abeyance until the next hearing. During the proceedings, the court maintained that an OCI cardholder does not enjoy the same rights as an Indian citizen, particularly when it comes to participating in protests. Drawing a comparison with how foreign nationals are treated in other countries, the bench remarked, "If an Indian had done the same thing elsewhere would it have been tolerated? If this had happened in America, the person would have been put on the next flight back to India," The judges also suggested that Khan consider applying for Indian citizenship if he wished to participate in demonstrations concerning issues affecting Indian citizens. While the bench acknowledged that the authorities were within their sovereign powers to issue the notice, it also urged them to consider the circumstances before taking further action. "He (Khan) is ready to tender an unconditional apology. He has been in India since childhood. Show some magnanimity and a big heart now. We have to be 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (the world is one family)," the court observed. At the same time, the judges made it clear that the actor could not take his OCI status for granted. Referring to the powers available to the government under the law, the bench said, "As an OCI cardholder, you (Khan) are at the mercy of this country. Hence, such behaviour cannot be tolerated, but one chance can be given," the HC said. The court also questioned Khan's reason for attending a demonstration concerning an issue linked to Indian electoral processes. Asking what connection the actor had with the SIR exercise, the bench remarked that he had no right to participate in a protest concerning Indian citizens. "For what had he (Khan) gone to a place of protest (in Mumbai)?" the judges asked, adding in a lighter vein that the actor did not even have an upcoming film to promote. "The rights Indian citizens enjoy and the rights available to OCI cardholders are different. If he had been an Indian citizen then the situation would have been different," Chief Justice Tripathi noted. Reiterating its position, the bench added that Khan's OCI status did not entitle him to exercise the same privileges as an Indian citizen. "You (Khan) had no right to participate in a protest of such nature. You have no connection with the SIR (Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls undertaken by EC). The right to protest is not available to an OCI cardholder," the HC said. The judges further took note of Khan's social media activity following his release from police detention, observing that his posts could influence his young followers. "Your social media posts (after he was released from detention by police) amounted to instigation. You have young followers who are bound to get influenced," the court said. The FRRO issued the 'Leave India' notice under Sections 7(2)(C) and 29 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, provisions that empower the government to regulate the movement of foreign nationals and order their removal from the country. Khan was directed to leave India by October 28, failing which deportation proceedings could be initiated. The action followed his brief detention by Mumbai Police during a demonstration held on October 10 at the city's historic August Kranti Maidan. The protest was organised in solidarity with an agitation by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which had demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the SIR of electoral rolls. In his petition challenging the FRRO's decision, filed through advocate Zulfiquar Memon, Khan maintained that he had neither participated in the gathering nor had any association or affiliation with its organisers. Describing the notice as "illegal, arbitrary, perverse and drastic," the actor alleged that the authorities had failed to apply their minds before targeting him because of his public profile. He further argued that the action amounted to "patent non-application of mind and the arbitrary targeting" of a public figure. The petition also contended, "Not only is the notice manifestly disproportionate, if implemented, it would reduce the very principles of natural justice that the authorities are duty-bound to uphold, to nothing but a dead letter." title: After AAPâs first list, 2 MLAs quit; BJP gathering expelled netas, says Aman Arora
text: Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Chetan Singh Jouramajra have stepped down from the Aam Aadmi Party. CHANDIGARH: A day after the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) announced its first list of 40 candidates for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections, MLAs Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Chetan Singh Jouramajra resigned from the partyâs primary membership on Sunday. There was speculation that both would join the BJP . Reacting to it, AAP state president Aman Arora posted on X that the BJP was âgathering expelled individuals because it has no base of its ownâ. Pathanmajra, against whom a rape FIR was registered on Sept 1, 2025, had evaded arrest, fled to Australia and was declared a proclaimed offender before being arrested near Gwalior in March 2026. He was granted bail in May and had said he would decide his political future in consultation with people in his constituency. Before the FIR, Pathanmajra had been vocal in criticising the AAP govtâs handling of floods in his constituency. The state govt had also withdrawn his security cover. Jouramajra was among AAPâs early leaders in Punjab and had served as a minister before being dropped during the Sept 2024 cabinet reshuffle. The party later appointed former SAD leader Surjit Singh Rakhra as its constituency in charge in Samana, represented by Jouramajra. Jouramajra had defeated Rakhra by 39,713 votes in the 2022 assembly elections. Jouramajra announced his resignation on social media in a post in Punjabi. Pathanmajra submitted his resignation to AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal on his official letterhead, writing, âI hereby submit my resignation from primary membership of Aam Aadmi Party with immediate effect.â AAP had appointed Ranjodh Singh Hadana as constituency in charge of Sanaur, represented by Pathanmajra. Reacting to the resignations, Arora wrote, âIf any of our leaders ever engaged in corruption or attempted to act against the interests of Punjab, we took action against them without any hesitation and expelled such people from the party. Now, the BJP is gathering these very expelled individuals because it has no base of its own and doesnât care at all about the interests of Punjab.â Arora added, âWhat good a person do for Punjab who fired shots at the Punjab police and fled, and whom chief minister Bhagwant Mann sent to jail on charges of rape? But thatâs exactly the kind of people the BJP wants. This clearly shows that BJP is completely hollow in Punjab. title: With 15k cadre in tow, Cong plans mega anti-SIR rally in Delhi on Nov 1
text: Hyderabad: Chief minister A Revanth Reddy has set a target of mobilising nearly 15,000 Congress leaders and workers from Telangana for the INDIA blocâs mega rally at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi on Nov 1 against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Telangana Congress president Mahesh Kumar Goud said AICC general secretary KC Venugopal spoke to him and CM Revanth to coordinate arrangements and mobilise party leaders and workers for the rally. Watch 'Treason': Kharge BLASTS CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Lists 6 Charges At INDIA Bloc's Mock Parliament Revanth has directed the state Congress leadership to ensure a massive turnout from Telangana in response to the call given by the AICC leadership. Leaders including CM Revanth Reddy, deputy CM Bhatti Vikramarka, state ministers, TPCC president, district Congress presidents, councillors, corporators and sarpanches are expected to travel to Delhi towards the end of Oct to participate in the rally. The rally, titled âChalo Delhi! Save the Vote, Save the Country: Public March and Mega Rally,â has been called by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi to oppose the SIR exercise and protect voting rights. Rahul has appealed to students, farmers, workers, women, youth and traders, as well as everyone concerned about democracy, to participate in the programme, stating that the vote belongs to the people and that the fight to protect it is also theirs. During a meeting recently, Revanth accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of attempting to create two categories of citizens â the wealthy who retain their voting rights and the poor who risk losing them. He alleged that the electoral revision exercise was being used to undermine democratic rights and weaken the participation of disadvantaged sections in the electoral process. The CM claimed that nearly 13 crore votes had been deleted across the country and that the electorate had declined from 97 crore in 2024 to a projected 84 crore for the 2029 elections. Questioning the figures, he asked how the number of voters could fall despite the countryâs growing population. Revanth further alleged that the BJP-led Centre was using the SIR exercise to counter growing public opposition, concerns over unemployment and protests among Gen Z. Drawing a parallel with the historic opposition to the Simon Commission during British rule, Revanth said the campaign against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar would develop into a movement to protect democracy. He called upon Congress leaders and workers to raise the slogan âGyanesh Go Backâ during the Nov 1 rally. Revanth also urged Telangana Congress leaders to ensure a strong presence at Ramlila Maidan, saying the state should demonstrate the same organisational strength it had recently displayed in Sircilla. The chief minister said the rally would intensify the Congress campaign to protect the voting rights of the poor and strengthen the partyâs efforts to return to power at the Centre in 2029. title: US Midterm Polls: Democrats sniff opportunity, Trump fights to avoid a lame-duck presidency
text: Democrats sniff opportunity, Trump fights to avoid a lame-duck presidency As Americans head into the final stretch of campaigning for the Nov 3 US midterm polls, both Democratic and Republican parties are set to field their big guns â and go on an ad-blitz â across key battleground states. Weighing on votersâ minds are issues like the rising cost of living, Trumpâs war against Iran that has seen fuel prices skyrocket, healthcare and housing. Hereâs a quick primer on whatâs at stake in the polls, why it could be hugely consequential for the Trump presidency, and how it may shape US foreign policy. Betting on the House: All 435 seats in Congressâs House of Representatives are up for grabs. Republicans hold a slim majority of 218 to Democratsâ 214 in the House. But this is widely expected to flip. That hinges on about 50 competitive races. Pollsters say Democrats could end up with a majority of as many as 15 seats. Senatorial action: But itâs the Senate races that will determine whether Trumpâs agenda over the next two years sinks or floats. The chamber has only 100 seats, but senators have staggered six-year terms. That means only 35 seats are up for grabs this time, of which about 10 are really competitive and likely to flip. If Democrats snag them up, they will overturn Republicansâ current majority of 53 to 45. Which is precisely why Republicans are pulling out all stops to boost their candidates in key races. If Dems get House, GOP holds Senate: A likely scenario, although Republicans have been shaken up by reported close contests in red states like Texas and Kansas. Plus, Trumpâs approval rating is down â a record low for him at 31% in the latest poll. So, Republicans are divided over associating themselves with Trumpâs policies. For some, getting the Presidentâs endorsement may actually spell doom in tight races. Midterm in numbers But if Republicans do manage to hold onto their majority in Senate, Trump would still have room to manoeuvre and, more importantly, bat down political challenges emanating from a Democrats-dominated House. If Dems win both houses: Thatâs the nightmare scenario Trump and GOP are trying to avoid. If Democrats control both the House and Senate, they effectively gain control of the legislative agenda. Sure, Democrats would still have to contend with Trumpâs veto power â he could use that to block any Democrats-led legislation. And overturning a presidential veto requires two-thirds majority in both houses â a rarity. But Democrats could still prove a point by forcing Trump to exercise his veto. That in turn could have political implications for presidential polls in 2028, putting Republicans looking for a post-Trump future in a tight spot. Also, unlike the House where a simple majority passes legislation, for bills to pass Senate they require a supermajority of 60 votes. Still, this is a scenario that GOP would like to avoid at all costs. Key races: Naturally, most of them focus on Senate seats. In North Carolina , Democratic candidate Roy Cooper is leading in the polls over Republican candidate Michael Whatley. This is a seat GOP appears to be giving up on, holding back on ad spends in the final two weeks. Texas is turning out to be a humdinger. Polls show a tight race between Democrat James Talarico and Republican Ken Paxton. Talarico is pegged to be slightly ahead at this point. And if he pulls it off on election day, Dems would end their 32-year losing streak in the state. But Republicans are pouring big money into this race, and are slated to outspend Democrats by three times, with overall GOP ad spend on this race set to cross $380mn. Kansas , likewise, is witnessing a neck-to-neck race where Democrat Adam Hamilton is squaring off against GOP senator Roger Marshall. Recent polls showed thereâs practically nothing to separate the two candidates. If Democrats win here, it would be historic â the state hasnât elected a Democratic senator in 94 years. The race in Michigan is grabbing a lot of eyeballs, thanks to Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed who is going up against Republican Mike Rogers. Trump himself has taken potshots at El-Sayed, calling him a Muslim radical, while other Republican leaders have tried to associate him with the Muslim Brotherhood. If El-Sayed wins, he would be the first Muslim senator in US history. Impact on US foreign policy: If Democrats win back both houses, it would certainly reduce space for Trump to act unilaterally on the foreign policy front. However, there are many ways in which Trump could work around any restrictions. For example, his war against Iran has skirted around the 60-day window for congressional approval through White Houseâs clever classification of the military action as aimed at âprotecting American peopleâ. Trump has also argued that since the war has started and stopped several times, the 60-day window for approval has renewed each time. However, if Democrats control Congress, they could curtail any funding for that war. Conversely, they could also try to fast track funding support for Ukraine. But Trump could veto that or simply not act. So, it could be a stalemate between Trump and a Democrats-controlled Congress. A third impeachment: A nuclear option, but not beyond the realm of possibility if Democrats win Congress. More likely though would be Democrats taking control of several committees, launching investigations against Trump officials or Trump family members, and blocking Trumpâs appointments to key govt positions and roles, essentially leading to a lame-duck presidency. title: From France to Portugal, Europe is protesting: How rising rents, living costs are fuelling anger
text: From Lisbon to Athens, housing costs are consuming household incomes, while food, energy and other essentials add to the squeeze. (Representative AI image) NEW DELHI: On Halloween, France is bracing for something far more unsettling than the usual festivities. Thousands are expected to take to the streets on Saturday, as 70,000 police and gendarmes are mobilised across the country amid fears of fresh unrest. Shops have boarded up, security has been tightened and authorities are seeking to prevent a repeat of the violence that erupted earlier this month. Behind the protests lies a familiar frustration: rising living costs, strained public services and the growing difficulty of making ends meet. The anger is not confined to France. Europe has long been associated with high living standards, strong social security and the promise of a comfortable life. But for a growing number of its residents, that promise is being tested by the monthly arithmetic of survival. In Lisbon, two people earning local salaries and sharing a three-bedroom city-centre apartment are left with just â¬253 after paying rent. In Milan, the amount is â¬697. Across the continent, rising housing costs, expensive essentials, stagnant wages and mounting pressure on public services are turning household budgets into a source of public discontent. From housing demonstrations in Spain and Portugal to protests over wages, education and government policies in France, Italy, Belgium and Germany, the grievances differ but point to a broader unease. The question confronting Europe is no longer simply whether people have jobs or earn a salary, but whether their earnings are enough to afford the life they were promised. The contrast with northern Europe is stark. The same calculation leaves a working couple in Zurich with â¬9,140 after rent, while â¬8,783 remains in Geneva. These figures, drawn from Deutsche Bank Research Institute's Mapping the World's Prices 2026 report, compare the combined net salaries of two local earners with the monthly rent of a three-bedroom city-centre apartment. They do not account for groceries, electricity, transport, healthcare or other household expenses. The calculation illustrates the gap between local earnings and city-centre rents rather than the actual spending patterns of every household. How much remains after paying rent The difference is not simply about how much people earn. Zurich has Europe's highest rent in the comparison, at â¬5,502, but also the highest average net salary, at â¬7,321 per person. Lisbon, by contrast, has an average net salary of â¬1,408 against a city-centre rent of â¬2,561. In 11 of the 28 European cities examined, rent exceeds one local net salary. The difference is not simply about how much people earn. Zurich has Europe's highest rent in the comparison, at â¬5,502, but also the highest average net salary, at â¬7,321 per person. Lisbon, by contrast, has an average net salary of â¬1,408 against a city-centre rent of â¬2,561. In 11 of the 28 European cities examined, rent exceeds one local net salary. The rent-to-income gap is only the beginning The housing burden becomes clearer when measured against household income rather than nominal rent. Eurostat's Housing in Europe 2025 report found that EU households spent an average of 19% of their disposable income on housing in 2024. The share was 36% in Greece, 26% in Denmark and 25% in both Germany and Sweden. For households at risk of poverty, housing consumed 37% of disposable income across the EU. The longer-term trend is equally revealing. Between 2010 and 2024, house prices across the EU increased by 53%, while rents rose 25%. General consumer prices increased by 39% during the same period. In other words, housing prices outpaced overall inflation, adding to the pressure on tenants and prospective homeowners. Europeâs housing problem Greece presents one of the clearest examples of the squeeze. Apart from having the highest housing expenditure relative to disposable income among the countries listed, it also recorded a 43% share of people living in households with arrears on mortgage, rent or utility bills in 2024, the highest in the EU. For younger Europeans, the challenge extends beyond finding a job. Eurostat's 2025 data show that 9.1% of people aged 15-29 lived in households spending at least 40% of disposable income on housing. The figure was 25.6% in Greece and 26.9% in Denmark. Across the EU, 26.9% of young people aged 15-29 lived in overcrowded households. The problem is not confined to rent. Food, another unavoidable household expense, accounts for a substantial share of monthly expenditure. Eurostat estimates that food and non-alcoholic beverages accounted for 13.1% of total household expenditure in the EU in 2024. The share was 18.1% in Portugal, 15.7% in Greece and 14.7% in Italy. In Germany, it was 11.1%, while France recorded 12%. Food may be cheaper, but is it affordable? A comparison of food prices across Europe also reveals a gap between the cost of a grocery basket and the ability to pay for it. Eurostat's 2025 comparative price-level index, which sets the EU average at 100, puts food and non-alcoholic beverage prices at 106.8 in France, 105.3 in Greece, 104.5 in Belgium, 102.4 in Germany, 102 in Portugal and 101.1 in Italy. Spain, at 95.3, is below the EU average. Romania recorded one of the lowest levels, at 79.8. How much grocerries cost in different parts of Europe The comparison also exposes why cheaper groceries do not automatically translate into greater affordability. Romanian households, for example, spent 23% of their total expenditure on food and non-alcoholic beverages in 2024, compared with the EU average of 13.1%. Portugal's share was 18.1%. Lower prices can still absorb a larger portion of household budgets when incomes are lower. The latest inflation figures add another layer. Eurostat reported that eurozone inflation reached 3.8% in September 2026, up from 3.2% in August. Energy prices rose 18.9% year-on-year, while food, alcohol and tobacco prices increased 1.3%. Within the food category, unprocessed food inflation was 4%. Food, energy and other necessities get costlier The distinction between inflation and price levels is important. Slower inflation does not mean groceries have become cheaper. It means prices are increasing at a slower pace. The accumulated increases of previous years remain part of household bills. Why are Europeans taking to the streets? The data help explain the economic pressure, but the protests have several immediate triggers. They are not one coordinated European movement, nor are they driven by a single political ideology. In France, demonstrations that began with complaints about school infrastructure, overcrowding and teacher shortages expanded into wider protests over living costs, wages and public services. The country has also witnessed clashes during demonstrations, prompting large-scale security deployments. In Spain and Portugal, housing affordability has become a central grievance. Protesters have opposed rising rents and the pressure of tourism on local housing markets. In Portugal, demonstrations have also demanded higher wages and pensions. In Italy, protests have brought together demands relating to employment, healthcare, education, housing and opposition to rearmament. Belgium has witnessed demonstrations over living costs and education expenses, while Albania's protests have focused on corruption and government accountability. In Germany, youth-led demonstrations have raised demands concerning schools, housing and climate spending, alongside opposition to restoring compulsory military service. What is each country protesting against "Every protest has its own dynamics. One needs to examine the specific reasons behind demonstrations in Spain, France, Belgium or any other country because each has its own history, economic difficulties and political context," Gulshan Sachdeva, Professor of European Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), told TOI. However, he believes there is a common economic thread connecting several of these demonstrations. "What we are witnessing is a combination of several crises: economic stagnation, rising living costs, housing shortages, demographic pressures, immigration-related anxieties and changing political dynamics. It is a broad cocktail of problems rather than a single cause of public unrest," Prof. Sachdeva said. The pressure on housing is particularly visible in southern Europe, where the growth of tourism has added to competition for residential properties. Sachdeva said local residents in cities such as Barcelona and Madrid increasingly feel priced out of their neighbourhoods as properties are used for tourism and short-term rentals. "The cost of living has risen, housing has become increasingly unaffordable, and younger people feel that the welfare state they inherited is no longer providing the same level of support," he said. A crisis of growth, public spending and political trust Economists and political analysts say the problem extends beyond household expenditure. Years of weak economic growth, demographic changes, pressure on government finances and growing competition from emerging economies have reduced the room available to European governments to respond to public demands. Rajan Kumar, Professor at JNU, said the economic difficulties have been compounded by the Ukraine conflict and Europe's move away from Russian energy supplies. Higher energy costs have affected production, transportation and other commodities, adding to the cost pressures faced by households and businesses. Inflation in Europe The pressure on government finances is another part of the problem. Under the EU's fiscal framework, the reference values for government deficits and public debt are 3% and 60% of GDP, respectively. These are not absolute spending ceilings, but countries exceeding them can face corrective procedures. France's public debt, for instance, stood at 119.1% of GDP at the end of the second quarter of 2026. Greece, Italy and Belgium were also above the 100% mark. Kumar argued that governments are finding it difficult to maintain welfare expenditure while responding to demands for higher defence spending. More money allocated to defence could put additional pressure on other spending priorities, including education and healthcare. He also pointed to Europe's ageing population, declining working-age population and loss of some of its traditional industrial and technological advantages to countries such as China and India. "The real issue is that the centre of gravity of global economic development has shifted towards countries such as India and China. Europe's technological and industrial dominance is no longer what it used to be." The growing political focus on immigration is another dimension. Both experts cautioned against treating migration as the primary cause of economic distress. Sachdeva said younger Europeans are more concerned about affordable accommodation, educational infrastructure and employment opportunities than about migrants taking their jobs. "The younger generation is not necessarily worried about outsiders taking their jobs. Its immediate concerns are better university infrastructure, improved educational facilities, better employment prospects and affordable housing." He also rejected the argument that generous welfare systems have made young Europeans unwilling to work. Rather, he said, the problem is that employment opportunities and public services are not expanding at the pace people expect. Meanwhile, right-wing political parties have increasingly used immigration and national identity as political issues, sometimes directing public anger towards migrants instead of the underlying economic problems. Government debt as a percentage of the GDP France's warning and the road ahead The economic pressure is particularly visible in France, where finance minister Roland Lescure warned on October 30 that the country needed a budgetary turnaround to avoid a deeper crisis. France's GDP contracted by 0.1% in the third quarter of 2026, following stagnation in the second quarter and a 0.2% contraction in the first. Lescure warned that without the proposed budgetary correction, the country was "headed straight for a wall". "For three quarters now, there has been no growth. If we fail to achieve the turnaround outlined in the budget, we are headed straight for a wall. The conclusion to be drawn from all this is that, as of 2026, the French economy is at a standstill. " Roland Lescure, French finance ministerOn France's economic performance in 2026, speaking to France Info, October 30. But an economic turnaround alone may not guarantee social stability. Sachdeva pointed out that protests are also being shaped by domestic electoral calculations, with political parties using public discontent to advance their interests. With elections approaching, Spain is set to vote on November 29, 2026, followed by Franceâs presidential election on April 18, 2027, with a possible May 2 runoff. Greece is expected to hold parliamentary elections in spring 2027, while Italyâs election is due by December 22, 2027, though a snap poll in April 2027 is possible. There is no clear timeline for when Europe will return to relative social and political calm. While protests may subside in individual countries, the pressures driving them are unlikely to disappear through a change of government or a temporary slowdown in inflation. If two people working full-time can have just â¬253 left after rent in Lisbon, before accounting for food, electricity and transport, the crisis is ultimately about how much of their earnings they can retain to live. title: Technicians know best who can represent them: Rudranil Ghosh
text: Rudranil Ghosh The two-day election process to choose representatives for the techniciansâ guilds in Tollywood concluded on Sunday, following polling for five guilds on the previous day. Elections were held across 16 guilds, while seven others were uncontested. In a conversation with CT, actor-politician Rudranil Ghosh explains the process, from eligibility criteria and polling arrangements to vote counting and the formation of the Federationâs governing body. A vote for their own Rudranil described the techniciansâ guild elections as an important step towards establishing a transparent and democratic system within the Bengali film industry. âFor the first time in many years, technicians have been able to cast their votes peacefully and without obstruction,â he said, adding that the polling was being conducted under CCTV surveillance and police security, allowing members to exercise their right to a secret ballot. The elections cover 23 guilds representing different professional categories within the industry, including lightmen, make-up artists, assistant directors and other technicians. âThese are professional elections in which candidates contest against colleagues from their own departments, and eligible members of those departments vote for them,â he explained. For instance, members of the make-up department elect their representatives from among candidates belonging to the same department. He emphasised that technicians themselves are best placed to decide who can represent their interests and run their guild effectively, adding, âThere is no reason for hostility between colleagues in this process.â 5,000 technicians eligible to vote The eligibility criteria for candidates and voters are governed by rules laid down by the Labour Commission and the relevant trade union authorities. âThose who hold valid cards and meet the prescribed requirements can contest and vote,â said Rudranil, adding that approximately 5,000 technicians are eligible to vote. A total of 333 candidates are contesting for different positions across the 23 guilds, each of which can have around 12 to 13 posts, including president, secretary, treasurer and other office bearers. While seven guilds are uncontested, elections are being held in the remaining 16, with five guilds going to the polls on the first day and the remaining 11 on the second. Explaining the arrangements to ensure impartiality, he said election commissioners are drawn from other guilds to oversee the process. âWhen the make-up guild holds its election, commissioners from other guilds oversee the process,â he said, adding that the respective guilds nominate colleagues they trust to remain neutral to help ensure that the elections are conducted fairly. Election in progress at a city studio Security, polling and counting arrangements Only technicians whose elections are being conducted are permitted inside the polling premises, with the restriction applying to everyone, including those associated with the industry, ministers and MLAs. âEven Mithun Chakraborty is not allowed inside,â said Rudranil, adding that the police were maintaining the arrangements in a disciplined manner and that technicians were happy with the security provided. The elections are being held over two days across five studio polling centres, all under CCTV surveillance. Rudranil said the process had remained peaceful, with counting beginning within 10 to 15 minutes of the conclusion of voting for each guild. âThe candidates and those concerned sit together during the counting process,â he said, explaining that the arrangement was intended to ensure transparency in the declaration of results and prevent disputes. Federation formation and results The next step after the guild elections will be the formation of the Federation. Five representatives from each guild will form its council body and help constitute the Federationâs governing body. âThe Federation will decide the rules and regulations for technicians across the industry,â said Rudranil, adding that the subsequent election would be held according to prescribed rules, through discussions among the representatives. The process is generally completed within a month. While guild elections are expected to be held annually, the final decision on their frequency will be taken once the new Federation body is in place. Counting will take place on the evening of polling, with guild membership ranging from around 500 to 1,000. Following the results, acting president Jayanta Kundu and other office bearers are expected to hold a press conference to announce details, including the number of candidates, eligible voters, positions and results. The timing and manner of the official announcement of the elected candidatesâ names are yet to be confirmed. Rudranil said constituting the Federation would enable the industry to establish a common framework of rules for technicians across departments. title: Co-op polls deferred indefinitely in Mahaâs drought-hit districts; court-ordered & nomination-stage elections to proceed
text: Kolhapur : State govt has indefinitely deferred elections to cooperative bodies, including district cooperative banks and sugar mills, citing drought conditions in 304 talukas. The cooperation department said proceeding with the polls would divert staff from relief duties, inconveniencing farmers in the affected areas. A notification issued by the cooperation department on Tuesday stated that govt was empowered under the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, to defer polls through a general or special order when holding them was not in the public interest due to natural calamities like drought or floods. The decision will not apply to cooperatives located in non-drought-affected districts. âElections mandated by court orders, as well as those where the nomination process has already begun, will also proceed,â the notification stated. Several district central cooperative banks (DCCBs) are expected to be affected. While the election process for Kolhapur DCCB is likely to be stalled, Satara DCCB polls will continue as nominations have already been filed. Sangli DCCB voting is scheduled for Nov 1, while Solapur DCCB is yet to announce its poll schedule. Govt said drought relief operations required the full attention of the administration, including officials from the revenue, agriculture, animal husbandry, cooperation, rural development, water supply and water conservation departments. âHolding cooperative society elections in these talukas would require govt officers and staff to be diverted to election duties, potentially hampering drought relief operations. It would also make it difficult for farmers and other members in drought-affected areas to take part in the elections,â the notification stated. Authorities are currently conducting crop-loss assessments, supplying water through tankers and ensuring fodder availability for cattle as part of the drought-mitigation effort. Govt argued that prioritising these measures over cooperative elections was essential in the prevailing circumstances. title: Gujarat vessel destroyed in attack off Oman coast; 13 crew rescued
text: Ship attacked off Oman coast Ahmedabad: An Indian-flagged vessel carrying general cargo from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to Somalia was allegedly struck by an unidentified aerial weapon off the coast of Oman on Oct 29 and engulfed in a fire that destroyed it completely. All 13 Indian crew members were rescued, while the vesselâs owner and crew members from Gujarat have incurred substantial financial losses. In a representation submitted to the Union ministry of external affairs on Saturday, Kasam Jafrabadi, a resident of Mota Salaya in Mandvi, Kutch, called for a probe into the incident and compensation for the loss of the vessel, MSV QUBA (MNV 2183). The representation said the vessel belonged to Abdul Matin Maklai and was captained by Abdul Majid Tarmamad Karani. It was transporting general cargo from Shindagah International Port in the UAE to Bosaso Port in Somalia. The vessel left the UAE on Oct 28 at 9.08am UAE time. The alleged attack took place at about 4.30am UAE time the next day off the Oman coast. The strike sparked a blaze, which completely destroyed the vessel, the representation said. Jafrabadi, who is related to the vesselâs owner and captain, said the 13 crew members survived after fishermen rescued them. The representation expressed gratitude to the fishermen for their help, while drawing attention to the financial consequences of the incident for the vesselâs owner, captain, crew members and their families. âThe vesselâs destruction has resulted in heavy financial losses and affected the livelihoods of its owner, captain, crew members and several families who depend on the vesselâs commercial operations,â the representation said. The family has asked the ministry of external affairs to intervene and coordinate with the Oman govt and maritime security agencies to ensure an impartial investigation. It has also called for the weapon used in the attack, as well as the individuals or organisations behind it, to be identified. The representation urged diplomatic action to safeguard Indian maritime interests and ensure the security of Indian nationals involved in international trade. It also called for an evaluation of the financial damage and compensation from those responsible, the countries concerned and insurance companies. The family has sought financial aid and rehabilitation assistance for the 13 crew members and their families, besides information about the investigation. Mandvi-Kutch MLA Aniruddha Dave had reached out to the affected families in Mota Salaya, expressed concern and assured them that a representation would be submitted to the authorities concerned, the letter said. The family has appealed to the Centre to fix legal responsibility and ensure that the probe proceeds beyond its preliminary findings. The representation said the incident was not just a financial setback but had also raised questions about the safety of Indian nationals and an Indian-flagged vessel on a lawful international voyage. title: BJP's Karnataka sweep, Congressâs Nagpur surprise and Akhileshâs gains: What the MLC polls really tell us
text: TOI Newsletter This week, we are tracking: 28 seats, 4 states, and a Nagpur twist: Who really won the MLC polls ? 21 lakh followers, 33 votes: When Instagram fame meets electoral reality No time to settle: How Team Indiaâs batters are rewriting cricket Jioâs record debut: What it means for your SIPs BJP's Karnataka sweep, Congressâs Nagpur surprise and Akhileshâs gains: What the MLC polls really tell us If you followed Wednesdayâs social media feeds, youâd think we had just held a mini general election. PM Modi posted a taunt with an emoji. Opposition leaders declared that paper ballots had humbled âautocracyâ. All this over 28 Legislative Council seats chosen by teachers and graduates in four states. The scoreboard How MLC elections unfolded in 4 states The BJP-led NDA finished with 15 of the 28 seats. The cleanest result came from Karnataka, where the BJPâJD(S) combine took all four, much to the dismay of Congress. UP was a near tie: BJP six, SP five. The BJP held five of the six seats it won in 2020, while the SP kept all three of its seats and added two more. Bihar threw up the most curious mix. The NDA (BJP + JD-U) won 3 of 8 seats, the RJD got 2 and Prashant Kishorâs Jan Suraaj got 1 seat, and independents secured two seats. A Nagpur surprise And Maharashtra? Thatâs where the real drama was. As results trickled in, PM Modi asked on X: âGuess how many seats Congress won?â Devendra Fadnavis went a step further and declared a âbig fat zeroâ. Then Nagpur sprang a surprise and Congressâs Abhijeet Wanjari won against BJPâs Sudhakar Kohale. Fadnavisâs post vanished; the state Congress gleefully circulated a screenshot. Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma chipped in with a mock apology congratulating Congress on its one seat. The ballot-paper argument, again The opposition was quick to credit paper ballots. âIf the elections are held with ballot papersâ¦ even autocracy is defeated,â said Sena (UBT)âs Sanjay Raut. The BJPâs reply: ballots or not, it still won the most seats. If paper ballots were a magic wand, the Congress wouldnât have been wiped out in Karnataka. Quick take These are not assembly elections in miniature. All 28 seats were elected by graduates and teachers, not the general electorate. The electorate is highly selective. These polls can reveal organisational strength and attitudes among particular professional groups, but they do not represent the pulse of the wider electorate. Read more: Guess how many Congress won: PM Modi 'Commit to ballot paper': Congress dares after PM Modi takes swipe over MLC results MLC election: BJP's gains come with a Nagpur, Varanasi reminder from Congress and SP MLC polls: Nitin Gadkari confidant revolt mayâve hit BJP in Nagpur 21 lakh followers, 33 votes: The astrologer who didnât see it coming Omprakash Bishnoi contested for sarpanch of a village in western Rajasthan with roughly 1,600 voters. He polled 33 votes. This should not be a story. However, Bishnoiâs loss is instructive for several reasons. By internet standards, he is a star. He has about 21 lakh followers across social media platforms. He also calls himself an astrologer and face reader. Clearly, the astrologer could not see this one coming. Can CJP be the next AAP? Bishnoiâs result comes at a time when everyone is watching a far larger attempt to turn online reach into political heft. The Cockroach Janta Party began online as a satire. The CJP has already been instrumental in the resignation of the Union education minister over the NEET paper leak, and its Jantar Mantar 2.0 protest brought Delhi to a standstill. A dispersed online community can converge at a particular place on a given date over some grievance. That is what protest needs, and the CJP has delivered it. Elections, village ones above all, need the opposite: Support concentrated in one place and sustained through years of ordinary favours. CJP founder Abhijit Dipke has said he has no plans to turn the movement into a conventional party. But what if CJP decides to go the AAP way? Can it translate its online reach into votes at the ballot box? title: US midterms: At Florida rally, Trump vows action against Cuba after Iran war
text: US President Donald Trump. US President Donald Trump has said he will turn his attention to Cuba once the war with Iran is settled, using a campaign rally in Florida to signal further pressure on the communist-run island ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. Speaking for around 90 minutes in Fort Myers on Friday, Trump suggested that US military forces returning from the Iran conflict could stop near Cuba. His remarks came as his administration continues to tighten pressure on the Cuban government. âWe'll have one of them stop about 50 yards off the coast. They'll raise up their hands, and then we're going to send Marco Rubio in to finish up the deal,â Trump said, referring to the US secretary of state, who has played a key role in shaping Washington's Cuba policy. Trump's comments come as the Iran war continues without a clear end in sight. He reiterated that further military action against Iran could be possible as his administration grapples with rising oil prices, which have put Republicans on the defensive ahead of the midterm elections. Trump steps up pressure on Cuba Trump has increasingly made Cuba a target of his foreign policy in his second term, seeking fundamental changes to the country's government. His administration has imposed an oil blockade that has added to the island's economic difficulties, including fuel shortages and power blackouts worsened by ageing infrastructure. In September, Trump called Cuba a âfailed stateâ during his address to the United Nations General Assembly and declared that âFreedom will be coming to Cubaâ. The remarks prompted the Cuban delegation to walk out. On Friday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio also called for change on the island. In a post on X, he urged people seeking a different future for Cuba to work with the CIA, writing that those disappointed with the Cuban government should âcreate the change you desire through a discrete partnership with the CIAâ. He did not provide further details. Trump's latest remarks follow Washington's broader campaign to increase pressure on leftist governments in the region. Earlier this year, the US ousted Venezuela's leader, adding to concerns about the administration's approach towards governments opposed to Washington. UN human rights experts have criticised the US oil blockade against Cuba, describing it as a violation of international law. Rights advocates have also accused the Trump administration of adopting an imperialist approach to foreign policy. Florida rally targets voters ahead of midterms Trump's rally was aimed at boosting the electoral prospects of Florida Republican Representative Byron Donalds, who is running for governor against Democrat David Jolly. Florida is home to a significant Cuban American population, making its voters an important constituency in US elections. Trump won 68% of the Cuban American vote in Florida in the 2024 presidential election. Alongside his remarks on Cuba and Iran, Trump announced plans to spend $250 million to hire at least 5,000 nurses for elder care facilities across the US, appealing to the state's large population of older residents. The speech was the latest in a series of campaign rallies in Republican-friendly areas as the president seeks to support his party ahead of the November 3 congressional elections.
