title: LA LA land goes Lal? After NYC, an Indian-origin socialist takes aim at Los Angeles
text: TOI Correspondent from Washington: For all the attention that the 2026 midterm elections in the US are attracting over control of the House, Senate, and governorships, a municipal contest in California with strong political and electoral ties to India is challenging the Golden State -- and Americaâs -- reputation as a bastion of capitalism. The Mayoral election in Los Angeles, whose $ 15 billion budget matches that of Costa Rica or Chhattisgarh, pits incumbent Karen Bass, 73, against Nithya Raman, 45, an India-born socialist councilwoman whose challenge has turned into one of the more intriguing political contests of the election season. Polls show the race currently tied, with Bass, a Democrat backed by the establishment, including California Governor Gavin Newsom, Kamala Harris, and Nancy Pelosi, clawing back from a ten-point deficit in September. If however Raman wins on Nov 3, LA will join New York City, now led by Zohran Mamdani, in having a mayor of Indian ancestry identified with democratic socialism. It would underscore the irony of two of America's most economically powerful, globally influential and famously expensive cities being governed by politicians from a movement that Trump and his political allies routinely portray as an existential threat to American capitalism. Raman's story has a typical Indian middle class template. Born in Kerala, she moved to the U.S at the age of six and grew up in Louisiana and Massachusetts, going to become an accomplished urban planner after graduating from Harvard and MIT. She moved back to India in 2009, establishing Transparent Chennai, an urban research and advocacy initiative, and worked on sanitation and water access in the city. Returning to LA in 2013, she became involved in neighborhood activism, particularly around homelessness and affordability. She is married to Vali Chandrasekaran, a Hollywood tv screenwriter, whose credits include episodes for hit sitcoms 30 Rock and Modern Family. In 2020, Raman defeated an incumbent to become the first Indian elected to the LA City Council and went on to build a reputation for activism on affordable housing, tenant protections, and climate policy, eventually identifying herself as a Democratic Socialist. Her Mayoral campaign centers around a simple proposition: LA is a spectacularly wealthy city that is somehow lousy at providing basic services to its residents. She promises more affordable housing, better public infrastructure and a more accountable homelessness program, pointing to a nearly 50% reduction in street homelessness in her council district, even as the city's overall numbers have increased -- a jab at Bass whose term is dogged by rising living costs, infrastructure gridlock and persistent homelessness in the City of Angels. There is, incidentally, an interesting Indian historical footnote to LAâs -- and for that matter Californiaâs and Americaâs -- flirtation with socialism. Long before Mamdani and Raman began making their mark in American municipal politics, several prominent Indian nationalists and intellectuals had encountered the country's radical political traditions first hand. Lala Lajpat Rai spent five years in the U.S between 1914 and 1919, establishing the India Home Rule League and publishing the journal Young India in New York. The radical humanist MN Roy arrived in the US in 1916 as a global itinerant, encountered American radicals and began studying socialism, subsequently moving to Mexico City, where he founded the Communist Party of Mexico in 1919. He later played a foundational role in establishing the Communist Party of India in 1920. B.R. Ambedkar, meanwhile, studied at Columbia University in NYC, encountering some of America's leading liberal and progressive intellectuals, including philosopher John Dewey. And Jayaprakash Narayan spent seven years in America (1922-1929), studying at Berkeley, Iowa, and Wisconsin, where he encountered Marxism and returned to India a committed socialist. All this was at a time socialism was enjoying considerable electoral popularity. In 1912, Socialist Party presidential candidate Eugene Debs won nearly a million votes, then about 6% of the national total. Socialists also held hundreds of municipal offices, including mayoralties. In fact, in the early 1950s Donald Trumpâs father Fred Trump clashed with the folk singer Woody Guthrie, an avowed socialist, over racial segregation and housing discrimination in Brooklyn, causing him to write a song -- a scalding takedown of a predatory landlord -- titled âOld Man Trump" who stirred up racial hatred "in the bloodsport of the human heart. " The subsequent âRed Scareâ and the association of socialism with communism marginalized the movement, but almost a century later âthe times they are a-changing.â Of course, Mamdani and Raman represent a different generation and a more modern version of democratic socialism. Neither is proposing to abolish private property or install a Soviet-style command economy; their politics revolve around housing affordability, public services, redistribution, workers' rights and making the wealthy contribute more towards the common good. For Trump, who has made fighting socialism a defining feature of his political identity, the prospect of New York and Los Angeles being governed by two such politicians, that too of âforeignâ origin, might be particularly galling. For India, meanwhile, there is something deliciously ironic about the possibility that two of America's most influential cities could be led by activists with Indian roots, carrying forward a political tradition that some of India's own intellectual giants first encountered on American soil. title: PUTA polls: Candidates promise family-friendly reforms
text: Patna University Patna : Similar promises, rival teams, and growing demand for family-friendly workplaces are sharpening the battle for the Patna University Teachersâ Association (PUTA), as campaigning gathers pace for elections after more than three years. From Patna Womenâs College to Patna Law College, candidates, accompanied by supporters, are canvassing across campuses, seeking leadership support that will represent teachers on service conditions, academic governance, and university affairs. Altogether, 27 teachers are contesting the seven key offices. Chief returning officer N K Jha said 24 nominations had also been filed for the 19 executive committee seats representing different constituencies. Although the contest is not formally organised along ideological or party lines, two distinct groups dominate the field, alongside several formidable independents. One draws strength largely from experienced teachers; the other projects a relatively younger leadership. The rival line-ups include Shankar Kumar for president and Ashutosh Kumar for general secretary in one team, and Kumar Satyendra Yadav and Deep Narayan Kumar, respectively, in the other. With manifestos offering broadly similar assurances, the contest raises a pointed question: what distinguishes the competing teams beyond their candidates? A sharper distinction is emerging through demands voiced particularly by younger women contestants. Enhanced maternity and paternity leave, child care leave and crÃ¨ches in colleges and departments employing women teachers are bringing workplace support for parents into the campaign. These demands place everyday institutional needs alongside the familiar promises of teacher unity, welfare and academic improvement. For the first time in PUTAâs history, separate debates for presidential and general secretary candidates have been organised to be held at JP Senate House on Saturday. Candidates will present their reform agendas, creating an opportunity to explain how campaign assurances would translate into action. PU has held presidential debates during studentsâ union elections for around 15 years. The stakes extend beyond staff rooms. PUTA has traditionally defended teachersâ collective interests while also providing a platform for those aspiring to public life. Former PUTA president Randhir Kumar Singh recalled the universityâs contribution to debates on democracy, socialism, social justice and educational reform, particularly during the JP movement. That legacy also brings a test: whether political aspirations can coexist with sustained attention to academic responsibilities and teachersâ concerns. Polling will take place from 10am to 3:30pm on Nov 4 at Patna College gymnasium. Counting will follow, with results expected the same evening, Jha said. The last elections were held in July 2023. title: Attack outside Israeli embassy in Serbia: Cop kills knife-wielding attacker shouting 'Allahu Akbar'
text: In a shocking incident, a minor armed with a knife assaulted a security guard near the Israeli Embassy in Belgrade shortly after midnight. (Pic Credit: Reuters) A knife-wielding assailant was shot dead after attacking a security guard outside the Israeli Embassy in Belgrade shortly after midnight on Wednesday, Serbian police said. Serbian interior minister Ivica Dacic said authorities were investigating the incident as a âterrorist attackâ. The government raised the terror threat level to its highest category and increased security at key locations across the country, according to the news agency AP. According to Dacic, the attacker was a minor and was carrying two knives. He allegedly shouted âAllahu Akbarâ, meaning âGod is greatâ in Arabic, while attacking a member of Serbiaâs Gendarmerie guarding the embassy. The officer sustained a minor facial injury but managed to shoot and kill the assailant in self-defence, the minister said. Photographs released by police showed the security booth outside the embassy, with the surrounding area cordoned off using police tape. Armed officers in tactical gear were seen at the scene. Dacic said the attacker was believed to have come from Sabac, a town in western Serbia. He added that security agencies had been monitoring the individual, whom he described as a supporter of the Islamic State group. âHe kept the black flag in support of the Islamic State on his Instagram account,â Dacic said. Attack follows political upheaval in Serbia and Israel The incident occurred days after Serbia held an early parliamentary election on Sunday, following nearly two years of protests against former president Aleksandar Vucic and his long-standing political leadership. A youth-led movement emerged as a major force in the election, although Vucic and his allies continue to control the police while the formation of a new government remains pending. Israel also held a parliamentary election on Tuesday, with exit polls indicating that no clear winner had emerged. The latest incident follows a similar attack outside the Israeli Embassy in Belgrade in June 2024. title: Indian-origin woman among immigrants charged in US voter fraud crackdown; citizenship bid at risk
text: immigrants targeted by federal authorities in California this week for alleged voter fraud. An Indian-origin woman is among more than two dozen legal permanent residents charged by federal authorities in California as part of a crackdown on alleged noncitizen voter registration and voting ahead of the US midterm elections. The charges could jeopardise their efforts to become American citizens, with some facing years in prison and potential deportation. According to the Associated Press, Amandeep Kaur, who has lived in the US for eight years and is in the process of becoming a US citizen, is among those charged. Her husband, Kulwinder Singh, said she obtained her driverâs licence in 2024 and may have registered to vote while applying for it. Singh said his wife took the written driving test in Hindi because she struggles with English. Singh said his wife received and returned a ballot in 2024, but both believed it was a voter registration form. He said Kaur was now distraught over the possibility that she had unknowingly broken the law. âAll she does is cry. Itâs heartbreaking,â Singh, who is a US citizen, told The Associated Press (AP). Federal authorities charged more than two dozen legal permanent residents in California on Monday over allegations of illegally registering to vote or voting as noncitizens. By Thursday morning, prosecutors had filed charging documents in 10 of the 28 cases, providing details of how investigators used voter registration records to pursue criminal charges involving immigration status. Citizenship applications at centre of several cases Most of the immigrants charged had applied for US citizenship and now face allegations of lying on naturalisation applications or during immigration interviews. Such charges could complicate or derail their attempts to become citizens. One of the accused, JosÃ© Antonio BaÃ±uelos-DÃ­az, 42, applied for citizenship in October 2025 after living in the US for 40 years as a legal permanent resident. The government alleges he improperly claimed to be a US citizen when registering to vote in 2007 and later failed to disclose it on immigration paperwork. Authorities have not accused him of casting a ballot. BaÃ±uelos-DÃ­az told AP he did not know he had registered to vote until he was arrested outside his Los Angeles home on Monday. He recalled obtaining a driverâs licence around 2007. In California, people are prompted to register to vote when applying for a driving licence. He was released after his arrest but faces up to five years in prison if convicted. Trump administration steps up scrutiny ahead of midterms The cases form part of the Trump administrationâs broader campaign against alleged noncitizen voting before the November midterm elections, despite data showing that such voting is rare and has not been demonstrated to change election outcomes. The Justice Department said six people would be charged with voting as noncitizens, a misdemeanour. The remaining 22 face a combination of felony charges, including allegedly lying on naturalisation applications, during interviews or on voter registration forms. Noncitizens convicted of illegally voting face up to one year in prison, while those convicted of lying on applications for US citizenship can face up to 10 years. The Justice Department has also sued California over its refusal to verify the citizenship status of roughly 20,000 registered voters whom the federal government suspects may be noncitizens. California, which has more than 23 million registered voters, has maintained that it complies with federal law and argued that the administration's figures are likely significantly inflated. State election officials have also pointed out that once ballots are mailed in, they are separated from individual voter identification, making it impossible to isolate ballots based on the information supplied by federal authorities. The Department of Homeland Security did not explain what initially brought the accused immigrants to investigators' attention. However, it said the agency reviewed naturalisation and other records as part of its investigation. Some court documents refer to a benefits fraud audit conducted by Homeland Security in August that may have helped identify those charged. âThe voting rights of American citizens must be protected,â First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli said in a statement announcing the charges. Naturalisation approvals decline sharply The crackdown comes amid wider immigration enforcement under President Donald Trump and a slowdown in the processing of citizenship applications. Government data showed that officials approved 58,000 naturalisation applications between April and June 2026, less than a quarter of the number approved during the same period in 2025. Green card holders can generally apply for US citizenship after three years if they meet the requirements applicable to spouses of US citizens, or after five years under the standard eligibility route. Applicants must undergo background checks, answer detailed questions about voting, political activities and criminal history, pass a civics test and meet English language requirements. For immigrants already seeking citizenship, allegations involving voter registration or voting can have consequences extending beyond the immediate criminal proceedings, potentially affecting their naturalisation applications and immigration status. title: Sourabh Chandrakar extradition may help unlock Rs 94,000 crore Mahadev betting app probe
text: Sourabh Chandrakar has been extradited from Oman and is a key figure in a significant illegal betting case. RAIPUR: Sourabh Chandrakar, extradited from Oman on Sunday, is considered a prized catch for the central agencies here that are probing a huge illegal betting and money laundering network under the umbrella of Mahadev Online Book, estimated to have generated proceeds of crime of around Rs 94,000 crore. Part of the booty allegedly went into funding elections and sharing 'protection money' with bureaucrats and politicians for its uninterrupted operation. The accused, 116 of them, named by CBI and ED, includes former Chhattisgarh CM Bhupesh Baghel, senior police officers and officials who held top positions in the Chhattisgarh administration. Sources in the agencies expect Chandrakar, who in the past expressed willingness to 'cooperate' before he fled India, to shed light on many sensitive aspects of the case, which investigators have not been able to unravel so far. Meanwhile, ED has moved a special court in Raipur seeking to expedite its pending application for declaring Chandrakar a fugitive economic offender under FEO Act. This can help the agency in confiscating his attached properties worth over Rs 1,800 crore mostly in Dubai. EDâs application is pending in the Raipur court since Nov 2024, and the next date of hearing has been scheduled on Dec 5 after repeated adjournments. Raipur Policeâs EOW, acting on a reference from ED, had registered an FIR against Baghel in March 2024, naming him as one of the accused, along with promoters of the Mahadev app. In Dec that year, CBI had registered another FIR naming Baghel as an accused and carried out searches at his residence. BJP had made Mahadev app case one of its central planks against Congress in the 2023 assembly polls. The attack on the then governing Congress was spearheaded by PM Narendra Modi, who criticised it for not even sparing âMahadevâ in looting people. In 2023, ED also carried out searches at the residence of Vinod Verma, political adviser to the then CM. Later, the agency said another accused ASI Chandrabhushan Verma, through Vinod Verma and money sent by co-accused Ravi Uppal, corrupted the police system at Raipur and Durg. Chandrabhushanâs statement also records that part of the hawala proceeds collected from Nagpur reached a close friend of the then CM and two officers on special duty to the CM. Son of a municipal corporation employee, Chandrakar worked at a juice shop in Bhilai, earning about Rs 15,000 a month, before he ventured into online betting. Within a few years, he was living in Dubaiâs luxury villas and travelling by chartered aircraft. He spent an astonishing Rs 200 crore on his wedding, investigators estimate. Between those two worlds lies the story of Mahadev Online Book â an alleged betting empire that grew out of Chhattisgarh and went on to become one of Indiaâs biggest laundering investigations. title: BJP turns to UCC plank to reignite Hindu consolidation ahead of UP polls
text: Union Home Minister Amit Shah Lucknow: A day after Union home minister Amit Shah pitched for implementation of Uniform Civil Code in UP if BJP form govt for the third consecutive time in 2027, the spotlight is back on the partyâs attempt to revive its Hindu consolidation plank. The move is being seen as a counter to the oppositionâs PDA narrative, which dented the BJP tally in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections in UP. Sources said the push for UCC in UP would allow the party to foreground a major ideological commitment after the abrogation of Article 370 and the construction of the Ram Temple in Ayodhya. Delivering on the promise, they argued, would help reinforce BJPâs credibility among its core nationalist support base ahead of the Assembly elections. Watch SIR, Form 6, Voter Rolls: EC Responds After Report Flags Objections By 2 Election Commissioners The UCC plank, sources said, could allow BJP to challenge the rival parties and portray their resistance to it as âpoliticsâ of minority appeasement. The strong objections from the opposition groups could allow the BJP to present itself as the sole defender of national integration. A senior BJP member said that introducing the UCC will help the party counter the oppositionâs attempt to frame campaigns around caste-based coalition or social justice issues, bringing the debate back to the political terrain where BJP traditionally holds an advantage. âThe party firmly vouches for implementation of UCC that encompasses all sections of society irrespective of caste and communities,â said UP BJP spokesperson Hero Bajpai. He said it would unify all communities and prevent the opposition from wheeling out its divisive agenda. UCC is already operational in states like Goa, which has followed the Portuguese Civil Code of 1867 since its colonial era, which was retained after its liberation and integration into India in 1961. Many BJP-governed states subsequently implemented or started the process of implementing UCC. In Jan 2025, BJP-run Uttarakhand became the first state in independent India to officially implement a new UCC. The UCC has also been passed by the state legislatures of Gujarat, Assam and Madhya Pradesh. States like Rajasthan, Maharashtra and West Bengal -- all governed by BJP -- are in the process of drafting bills, clearing cabinet reviews and setting up expert panels vis-Ã -vis UCC. Experts said that BJP also seeks to promote the UCC while hoisting the banner of gender equality and womenâs empowerment. By highlighting reforms in inheritance, divorce and polygamy, the party seeks to broaden its appeal among women across different communities, including sections of minority women. Shahâs statement on proposed implementation of UCC in UP has drawn sharp responses from the opposition parties which argue that BJPâs push for the UCC was strategically timed around elections to polarise society, create communal divisions and distract voters from pressing economic concerns like inflation and unemployment. Samajwadi Party spokesperson Abdul Hafiz Gandhi said any move towards the Uniform Civil Code must carefully balance Article 44 with the constitutional protections of religious freedom and the rights of different communities. âSuch a sensitive reform requires wide consultation, mutual trust and a gradual, inclusive approachânot political announcements before elections,â he said. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has already held that UCC is not worth implementing. Likewise, senior politician and lawyer Kapil Sibal too has said that BJP made many promises in the past but not a single one got fulfilled. âLet them keep making more promises. Their entire politics revolves around empty promises,â he said in Delhi. title: SC declines to stall AP local body polls
text: Supreme Court of India Vijayawada : Supreme Court on Tuesday refused to interfere with the conduct of local body elections in Andhra Pradesh and declined to permit any further extension of the election process. SC said grievances arising out of polls can be agitated before election tribunals after the process is completed. A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohan heard a petition filed by YSRCP alleging that its candidates were being prevented from filing nominations and participating in the election process. The bench made it clear that the directions issued earlier by it to ensure free and fair elections would continue to remain in force. It also directed that the election process be monitored through CCTV cameras. Senior advocate Maninder Singh, appearing for the petitioners, contended that despite the courtâs earlier intervention, the situation on the ground had not improved. The counsel argued that YSRCP candidates were first prevented from filing nominations in urban local body elections and later faced similar difficulties in MPTC and ZPTC elections. He also contended that adequate police protection had not been provided to the partyâs candidates. Opposing the allegations, solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for State Election Commission along with K Parameswar and N Ashwani Kumar, submitted that the commission had fully complied with the apex courtâs earlier directions. He told the bench that the commission had scrutinised the process in about 100 urban local bodies and that candidates were given an opportunity to file nominations by extending the time wherever necessary. Police protection was also extended wherever representations seeking security were received. Considering the submissions on both sides, the bench observed that further extension of the election process could not be permitted at this stage. It remarked that political battles should be fought in elections and not brought into courtrooms. The judges also observed that parties aggrieved by any aspect of the election process have an effective statutory remedy before election tribunals. Declining to pass any order affecting the election schedule, the bench said its earlier directions aimed at ensuring free and fair elections would continue to operate, effectively clearing the way for SEC to proceed with the elections. title: First in 47 years: CRPF completes 12 months without any operational casualties
text: The previous time the CRPF went such a long period without an operational fatality was before January 1979. NEW DELHI: The Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) has completed 12 consecutive months without losing any personnel in operational fatalities, marking an achievement not recorded in the force in 47 years. CRPF Director General GP Singh congratulated personnel on the milestone, saying the last operational death in the force was recorded on October 30, 2025. The previous time the CRPF went such a long period without an operational fatality was before January 1979. Watch IB Director Dr. Mahesh Dixit Recalls Sacrifice of 10 CRPF Personnel in China Border Clash 1959 Sharing the achievement on X, Singh wrote, âA significant milestone in the history of CRPF - 12 consecutive months (One Year) have passed without any Operational fatality in the force, the last operational fatality in the force being on Oct 30th 2025. This has happened after 47 Years (last such period ended in January 1979).â He attributed the achievement to improvements in equipment, training and operational planning. The force's focus on responding quickly to incidents, particularly by evacuating injured personnel to secondary and tertiary medical facilities, had also played an important role, he said. âItâs especially significant since this has happened while we continue to be deployed and engage intensely in all the major operational theatres, achieving significant breakthrough results. We remain committed to keeping the country peaceful & safe for all its citizens,â wrote the CRPF D-G. title: Trump seeks prosecution of Democrat Mary Peltola over alleged scheme to field Dan Sullivan namesake in Alaska
text: US President Donald Trump. US President Donald Trump has called for the removal and prosecution of Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola after a report alleged that people linked to her campaign discussed recruiting a candidate with the same name as Republican Senator Dan Sullivan to potentially confuse voters in Alaska. Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy has also announced plans to launch a criminal investigation into whether the alleged scheme violated state election laws. The controversy follows a New York Times report published on Wednesday that cited interviews, text messages and documents indicating that Peltola's campaign aides and officials linked to the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC) discussed recruiting candidates named Dan Sullivan to run against the Republican incumbent. Trump called for Peltola and Daniel J Sullivan Jr, a retired schoolteacher who is challenging Senator Sullivan, to be removed from the ballot and prosecuted. In a social media post, he accused Democrats of election fraud and described the alleged operation as voter fraud. Dunleavy said he was directing Alaska's Department of Public Safety to investigate whether the alleged plan warranted criminal charges or civil action. âDeliberately tricking voters into casting their ballots for someone else strikes at the integrity of our elections,â the governor said, adding that anyone found to have broken the law must be held accountable. The allegations have surfaced days before the November 3 midterm elections, with the Alaska Senate race among the contests that could determine control of the US Senate. What the report alleged According to the New York Times, the effort began in 2025, when a Peltola aide was asked to identify Alaskans named Dan Sullivan. The newspaper reported that campaign aides and senior Democratic operatives discussed recruiting candidates who could potentially split support for the Republican senator. The effort eventually focused on Daniel J Sullivan Jr, a retired schoolteacher from Petersburg, Alaska, who has no previous political experience. He qualified for the November general election after the Alaska Supreme Court overturned a state elections official's decision to disqualify him from the primary ballot. The official had concluded that his candidacy had been filed with the purpose of confusing or misleading voters. However, the state Supreme Court ruled that he was qualified to run. The Times report cited interviews with Peltola's former campaign manager, Elisa Rios, and other people familiar with the alleged plan. Rios told the newspaper that Peltola knew about the operation but did not participate directly. The newspaper also reported that Rios later sought to retract her statements. Peltola's campaign has denied involvement in recruiting either Sullivan candidate. The DSCC has also denied recruiting Daniel J Sullivan Jr, despite the report's account of discussions between committee staff and Peltola's campaign. Daniel J Sullivan Jr has maintained that he entered the race independently and had no contact with Peltola's campaign. Political and legal fallout Republican Senator Dan Sullivan's campaign accused Peltola, her advisers and Democratic operatives of colluding to mislead voters. Alaska Senator Lisa Murkowski, who has endorsed Sullivan and is a longtime friend of Peltola, also called for an explanation from the Democratic candidate. The controversy comes as the Trump administration pursues a separate legal challenge seeking to block certification of a possible Peltola victory, citing the presence of the second Dan Sullivan on the ballot. However, legal experts said the allegations reported by the Times would not necessarily affect the outcome of that lawsuit. They noted that while recruiting candidates to split an opponent's vote can be viewed as a dirty political tactic, it is generally legal. The two Sullivans are among four candidates contesting the Alaska Senate seat under the state's ranked-choice voting system, in which voters rank candidates by preference and votes can be transferred when a candidate is eliminated. Peltola, a former Alaska congresswoman, is challenging Sullivan as Democrats seek to win control of the Senate in the November midterm elections. You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. title: 20 complaints in Jamshedpur over fake SIR emails targeting voters
text: EC clarified that district election authorities are not seeking certificates or documents through such emails Ranchi: Around 20 complaints have been received from Jamshedpur after cyber fraudsters sent fake emails to voters, threatening that their names would be deleted from the draft electoral roll prepared under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. The complaints, mainly from Kadma and Sonari areas under the Jamshedpur West assembly constituency, prompted warnings from the office of the chief electoral officer and the East Singhbhum administration. Tata Steel employees and several prominent doctors are among those targeted. Deputy electoral officer of Jamshedpur, Priyanka Singh, said most complaints were received from the two areas. âNo fresh complaints have been reported since Saturday,â Singh told TOI on Monday. The fraudulent emails, purportedly sent by election authorities, ask recipients to click on a link, fill in a âSIR verification formâ and submit personal details and documents. They warn that failure to comply could lead to exclusion from the final electoral roll. Most recipients verified the emails with their booth level officers (BLOs), who alerted the election authorities. A complaint has also been lodged with the cyber security cell and East Singhbhum SSP. One such email, dated Oct 30, carried the subject line: âAction Required: Your Name Has Been Removed from the Draft Voters Listâ. It falsely claimed that discrepancies had been detected during the SIR process and that the recipientâs name had been temporarily removed from the draft roll. Election Commission has termed the emails misleading and part of an attempted cyber fraud . In an advisory, it clarified that district election authorities are not seeking certificates or documents through such emails. Officials advised voters not to click on suspicious links or share personal information, OTPs or documents on unknown websites. For voter verification and SIR-related services, electors should contact their BLOs or use official platforms, including the ECINET app and the voter services portal (voters.eci.gov.in). title: Betul teacherâs David vs Goliath bid: Takes on Puri for RS, first hurdle is to get signatures of 10 MLAs
text: Union ministers Hardeep Puri and BL Verma Hardeep Singh Puri, India's oil minister, during the India Energy Week conference in New Delhi, India, on Tuesday, Feb. 11, 2025. The conference runs through Feb. 14. Photographer: Anindito Mukherjee/Bloomberg via Getty Images Bhopal: On one side is a Union minister backed by 164 BJP MLAs. On the other is a guest teacher from Betul, camping in Bhopal and knocking on doors across party lines for 10 signatures. Hariplal Bihare, 55, is the only person to have picked up a nomination form to contest as an Independent against Hardeep Singh Puri , Union minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas and the BJPâs nominee, in the Nov 12 Rajya Sabha bypoll. For him, the contest has not yet begun â he is still trying to get into it. For the past two days, Bihare has been doing the rounds of the corridors of power in the state capital with a file in hand and a simple request: will you propose my name? He has approached leaders from both the BJP and Congress , hoping that political rivalry will make way for courtesy towards an ordinary citizen wanting to enter the electoral arena. He is also pinning his hopes on BJP leaders from Madhya Pradesh whose names were doing the rounds for the Upper House seat before the party settled on Puri â leaders who, he feels, might empathise with his argument. That argument is at the heart of his unlikely bid. Bihare says he is unhappy with political parties choosing candidates from outside the state for Rajya Sabha. He wants to prove that an ordinary citizen, without a party flag or a deep pocket, can still aspire to contest and win. It is not his first electoral experiment. In 2023, he contested the Assembly election from Amla as an Independent and managed just over 1,000 votes. He knows what defeat looks like, but Rajya Sabha presents a different kind of test â here, before he can ask voters to back him, he must persuade legislators to get his name on the ballot. The vacancy arose after Union minister L Murugan resigned from Rajya Sabha on Oct 13. His term was to end in April 2030. Murugan had been elected to the Upper House from Madhya Pradesh in April 2024. The numbers are stacked against any challenger. The BJP has 164 MLAs in the 230-member House, the Congress 65, and Bharat Adivasi Party one. On paper, the ruling party is comfortably placed to retain the seat. Against that arithmetic, Bihareâs bid may appear quixotic, even audacious. But for the teacher from Betul, the immediate exam is not about outnumbering the BJP. It is about passing the entry test. Election Commission has scheduled polling and counting for Nov 12, with Nov 2 as the last date for filing nominations. Until then, his lesson in practical politics continues: before dreaming of Rajya Sabha, one must first get the numbers right â and in politics, even a teacher needs someone willing to sign his admission form. title: Former Bangladesh air force officer linked to Hasina escape video found dead
text: File photo: Former Bangladesh Air Force officer KM Tahsif Souri DHAKA: A former Bangladesh air force officer, reportedly linked to a video purportedly showing Sheikh Hasina fleeing the country on Aug 5, 2024, has been found dead near a river in Dhaka, with police saying an inquest report has found no external injury marks, though blood was seen coming out from his nose. title: 'I want to build fielding as an attacking weapon': New Mumbai Indians fielding coach T Dilip
text: T Dilip (Image credit: Mumbai Indians) Newly appointed Mumbai Indians fielding coach T Dilip wants to make fielding one of the team's biggest strengths. He believes that a strong fielding unit can change the course of a match and wants to build a culture based on trust, respect and enjoyment. Dilip, who has previously worked as India's fielding coach, was one of three new members of the Mumbai Indians support staff announced on Friday. Watch Tilak Varma press conference: Indiaâs 3-0 lead, batting approach & more Speaking in a video shared by the franchise, Dilip said wearing the Mumbai Indians badge came with both pride and responsibility. "Mumbai badge is a privilege and as well as a responsibility. As a Mumbai Indians team, I want to build fielding as an attacking weapon in the field," he said. Focus on the small things Dilip believes fielding is not just about taking spectacular catches or producing brilliant run-outs. He wants players to understand that even small efforts on the field can make a big difference to the result of a match. "We generally see catches, we generally see run-outs. Once players recognise that it's not the spectacular highlights which is highlighted, but the 1% factors which can impact a game, then automatically they will put in those efforts. "And for us is to make sure that in a practice or a match, we create that environment where players having fun on the field, enjoy the field, and go out there. Sometimes you may have a bad day in your primary skills, whether a batting or bowling, but still you can impact a game through fielding." He also stressed the importance of building trust among players. According to Dilip, it takes time and depends on how teammates connect with each other both on and off the field. "I think it's built over a period, because it's not only just what happens on the field, but I think how we interact and spend time with each other off the field, because it gives you an insight about what that person thinks." 'Trust helps you enter the dressing room' Dilip has worked with several Mumbai Indians players during his time with the Indian team. He said his previous association with them would help him settle into the dressing room, but he knows that building trust within a new setup requires consistent effort. "I have worked with Rohit as a captain when I started, then Surya as a captain, Jasprit Bumrah, Tilak Varma, Naman Dhir, you name anyone, Deepak Chahar, Shardul Thakur. So acquaintance is always there, that really helps. "But trust me, acquaintance helps you to come into the dressing room, but to earn that place in the dressing room, I think it's an everyday work - hard work, what we do and relationship and how can I help the team to take forward, whether it's through culture or work. That is where I want to earn that back again." Wants fielding efforts to be recognised Dilip also spoke about the fielding medal initiative at Mumbai Indians and praised the players for making it popular. However, he said he would first understand the team's existing culture and the head coach's approach before bringing in any new ideas. "I think when it comes to fielding medal, you know, I am very, very happy that a great initiative was taken, and actually, it's the players who made it really big, the way they have taken it. "But I feel end of the day, I am new to this Mumbai Indians setup, and as we know that there are certain traditions which already goes, and my way of working generally is whoever is the head coach is to understand their philosophy. "I'll definitely have a chat with them and see what best can be introduced or in an existing environment what can be done. But definitely fielding is something I would like to be rewarded and recognised." He believes the home crowd gives the players extra confidence, especially during difficult moments. "When it comes to Wankhede, I have seen personally there's always tremendous support because it is small ground, it resonates, it feels like in a tougher situation there is someone else backing you all the time. "I know at times, the results have not gone in favour where they are quite happy because expectations of Mumbai Indians were high, but I'm sure with their support and with the calibre and effort we try to put and we make sure that we bring back the smiles on their face, and we bring up a show where they'll always be entertained." title: Omar Abdullah faces internal storm: Many NC MLAs upset over J&K cabinet rejig; Srinagar MP announces resignation
text: Omar Abdullah and Farukh Abdullah (File photo) SRINAGAR: The government of chief minister Omar Abdullah is facing signs of discontent within the ruling National Conference (NC), with a number of legislators reportedly unhappy over the recent cabinet expansion and seeking greater democracy within the party and resignation of the whole cabinet. The discontent within the party has taken place at a time when the party MP from Srinagar Aga Ruhullah Mehdi is resigning from the party on November 3 leaving Srinagar parliamentary seat open. âI will resign from the National Conference and my Lok Sabha seat on November 3, 2026. The crown prince and his cabal treat J&K as an estate passed down through the family. They expect the people to vote, then know their place. They take us for fools who cannot tell a broken promise from a political necessity. Ask them to honour their own manifesto, and they lecture us on how little we understand realpolitik,â Mehdi wrote on X. Watch Omar Abdullah Moves Full Statehood Resolution In J&K Assembly, BJP Protest Sparks House Uproar âWe demanded the restoration of Article 370, the release of prisoners and the protection of our rights. They sought power on those promises, then treated us as fools for expecting them to deliver. We refuse to lend our name to this humiliation. There is no fixing this rot from within. The seat was won on a promise to the people,â Mehdi added. Mehdi said he would surrender the seat rather than become an accomplice to the betrayal of that promise. Mehdi would address the people on November 3, the death anniversary of his father, Aga Syed Mehdi, at Behisht-e-Zehra Park in Budgam. His father was a Congress leader and prominent Shiite cleric who was assassinated in a terrorist attack on November 3, 2000. Ruhullah Mehdi is an alumnus of Tyndale Biscoe School and holds a bachelor's degree in arts from the University of Kashmir. His political career began in 2002, when he contested and won his first Assembly election from Budgam. He retained the seat in 2008 and 2014. In 2009, he was inducted into the state Cabinet, becoming the youngest Cabinet minister. In 2015, Mehdi was nominated as the chief Spokesperson of the National Conference, the position he held for several years. However, after abrogation of Article 370 on August 5, 2019, he distanced himself from the partyâs stand of maintaining silence over the situation in Jammu and Kashmir after August 5. He would urge the party to take a stand on Article 370 rather than urging the centre to restore statehood which he describes as a scaled down position. In August this year the NC president Dr Abdullah said Mehdi would not have won the parliamentary elections without the NC support. He said that if Mehdi believed Article 370 could be restored, he should fight for it, as no one had stopped him from pursuing the cause. Dr Abdullah had said the NC had not prevented Mehdi from pushing for the restoration of Article 370. Dr Abdullah had said Mehdi should resign and contest elections on his own. In response Mehdi had said that Dr Abdullah has for the first time asked anything from him and he will not disappoint him. MLAs meeting Meanwhile, according to the sources, over a dozen party legislators met Friday evening at the residence of Qaiser Jamshaid Lone, who represents the Lolab constituency, with several others joining the meeting online. They decided to seek resignation of the entire council of ministers and demand that a new cabinet be formed through consensus, based on merit and in keeping with democratic principles, sources said. They also decided to seek the resignation of the chief ministerâs advisor Nasir Ahmad Wani. In a related development, NC president Dr Farooq Abdullah removed Mubarak Gul as the partyâs general secretary. Gul was among the MLAs who attended the meeting at Loneâs residence. After the cabinet expansion on Tuesday, Dr Abdullah had elevated Gul, who wanted cabinet induction for himself, to the post of general secretary. Omar Abdullah and Dr. Farooq Abdullah are in New Delhi. Dismissing reports of widespread discontent within the party and rebellion, NC spokesperson Ifra Jan questioned the claim that 20 MLAs attended the meeting at Loneâs residence. âThey are saying 20 MLAs held this particular meeting. Where is this figure of 20 coming from? Is there a photograph or a list of names? Somebody anonymously claims 20 and everyone else repeats it without any investigative corroboration,â she said. âAfter the cabinet expansion, I think one or two MLAs openly expressed their displeasure and that was there for everyone to see. Isnât that normal? Doesnât this happen in all political parties? Some MLAs are happy while others are unhappy. This is common practice across the country,â she said. âEver since Omar Sahib (Omar Abdullah) took oath, the leader of the opposition BJP's Sunil Sharma, has been claiming that the government will fall next week. Unfortunately, nobody is asking why. Every disagreement is being viewed through the prism of âgovernment will fall rumoursâ without any evidence. We consider any claim of large-scale discontent within the party as a rumour,â she added. Sunil Sharma said it seems Omar Abdullah government has only eight MLAs with it and those eight are cabinet Ministers. Nazir Gurezi, who was part of the meeting, told the TOI that Lone had invited all MLAs and âlarge number of MLAs were at his residence. We just had food thereâ. On Tuesday morning Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha administered the oath of office and secrecy to the newly inducted ministers, Ali Mohammad Sagar, Shamima Firdous, Mir Saifullah and Altaf Ahmad Kaloo at Lok Bhawan in Srinagar taking the number to eight with Omar including nine. Omar dropped Satish Sharma, who was Minister for food, consumer affairs, transport science, IT, youth affairs, sports, and training. Omar was sworn in as chief minister on October 16, 2024, along with five ministers. Under the prescribed norms, the council of Ministers cannot exceed 10% of the total strength of the legislative assembly. With 90 members, the Jammu and Kashmir Assembly can have a maximum of nine ministers, including the chief minister. Three cabinet berths had remained vacant for nearly two years as the party struggled to decide whom to induct. I felt very sad not to be part of the cabinet. I was deserving of it (cabinet seat). Till the last moment, I was expecting to be part of the cabinet,â Larmi said. âI am a law graduate, while the MLA chosen has not even passed matriculation,â he had said. Mubarak Gulâs supporters lodged a protest at the party headquarters. In the 90-member Assembly, the NC has 41 MLAs and is backed by six independent legislators, while the Congress, with six MLAs, extends support to the government from outside. title: RLD leader projects Jayant Chaudhary as NDA's face for 2027 UP polls
text: NEW DELHI: Rashtriya Lok Dal general secretary Trilok Tyagi on Monday projected Union minister and party chief Jayant Chaudhary as a key face of the BJP-led NDA's campaign for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, saying the alliance would form the next government under his leadership. Tyagi said the RLD was working to strengthen its organisation across Uttar Pradesh, "from Baghpat to Ballia and Ghaziabad to Ghazipur", with Chaudhary at the forefront. "Politics does not mean merely wearing kurta-pyjama. It also means sitting among people and understanding their problems," he said. "The NDA would form the government in Uttar Pradesh after the 2027 assembly elections under Jayant Chaudhary's leadership," he added. Recalling former prime minister Chaudhary Charan Singh, Tyagi said he was opposed to giving election tickets to people who consumed alcohol. He described Charan Singh as a leader committed to his ideology and Arya Samaj principles, adding that he had no reservations about Muslims and had fielded a Muslim candidate from Ghaziabad. Tyagi said Charan Singh had united farmers and promoted Mulayam Singh Yadav as a political leader in the 1980s. Appealing to people to support Jayant Chaudhary, he said the RLD chief would emerge as a major national leader one day. He said the process of seeking and distributing election tickets would continue, but political leaders should learn to sit among people and understand their concerns. Referring to Charan Singh's tenure, Tyagi said farmers earlier feared travelling with their carts as they faced challans on canal embankments and roads leading to tube wells. Charan Singh had worked to change the situation, he said. Tyagi claimed that Jayant Chaudhary had raised the issue of sugarcane prices, following which the government fixed the rate at Rs 400 per quintal. He said farmers earlier had to take to the streets to demand remunerative prices for potato and sugarcane, but could now raise their demands directly before the chief minister and the prime minister. title: Rahul can be PM only in mock Parliament: Amit Shah
text: BJP calls INDIA blocâs âvote choriâ rally a flop, Shah takes jibe at Rahul Gandhiâs PM ambitions CHANDIGARH/NEW DELHI: BJP derided INDIA bloc's rally against 'vote chori' as a "flop show", while Union minister Amit Shah said Rahul Gandhi could hope to be PM only in a 'mock parliament', referring to Congress's mock CEC impeachment. Addressing a gathering on Chandigarh Police's 60th Raising Day on Sunday, Shah said Sonia Gandhi had resorted to the move since her dream of Rahul becoming PM was not fulfilled. "You (Rahul) want to become PM, stay in mock parliament your entire life; your turn won't come," Shah said. Watch âFirmly Planted Like Angadâs Footâ: Amit Shah Predicts BJP Victories In UP, Uttarakhand And Punjab His remarks highlighted BJPâs counterpunch to the oppositionâs campaign against Election Commission and govt over Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, with BJP functionaries, including CMs, participating in âSave Democracy, Defeat Anarchyâ marches across the country. BJP president Nitin Nabin, who travelled to Rohtak as part of the anti-Congress campaign, accused Rahul of deliberately destroying the credibility of constitutional bodies as part of his plan to sow anarchy. As BJP functionaries, like former party chief and Union health minister J P Nadda, expressed jubilation over what they called a âsuper flop showâ at Ramlila Maidan, the party also homed in on Congressâs choice of the date for the rally â the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots which took place in the wake of former PM Indira Gandhiâs assassination â to accuse the opposition party of mocking the tragedy suffered by the community. âThey chose the very day when genocide of Sikhs happened to hold a rally. It is like rubbing salt into the wounds of 1984 victims,â said Shah in Chandigarh. Recalling Rajiv Gandhiâs controversial âwhen a big tree falls, the earth shakesâ remark, which was seen by many as the former PM seeking to rationalise the mass killings of Sikhs, a combative Shah emphasised that BJP had urged Congress not to hold the rally between Nov 1 and 3, days associated with the massacre. title: India moves to resolve Scotch tariff dispute, assures 75% duty on bulk imports: Report
text: The government has moved to resolve a dispute over Scotch whisky imports under the UK trade pact, assuring liquor companies that bulk shipments qualify for the reduced 75 percent import duty after tax officials questioned their eligibility for the concession. According to a Reuters report citing six people with direct knowledge of the matter, commerce ministry officials gave the assurance during a closed-door meeting with liquor industry executives on Monday, saying New Delhi would honour the trade agreement in letter and spirit. One government source said, "We are potentially moving towards a resolution. Bulk Scotch whisky imports are indeed part of concessions under the trade deal." A second source said commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal told attendees that necessary steps were being taken to address the issue "so that the duty concession on bulk Scotch whisky is not impaired". The dispute centres on the agreement to reduce import duty on Scotch whisky in India from 150 per cent to 75 percent under the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), which came into effect in July 2026. However, tax officials had told liquor companies that the reduced duty did not apply to Scotch imported in bulk containers. The disagreement is significant because around 80 percent of Scotch whisky shipped to India arrives in bulk rather than in finished bottles. These imports are used by Indian manufacturers to produce Indian-Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL) whisky by blending Scotch with other spirits and ingredients. The industry maintains that both bottled and bulk Scotch imports should qualify for the reduced tariff under the trade agreement. The dispute has affected major liquor companies, including Diageo and Pernod Ricard, as well as Indian manufacturers Radico Khaitan and Allied Blenders and Distillers. Tax officials searched the offices of several companies in recent days and questioned executives over the classification and eligibility of bulk Scotch imports. The issue has also drawn attention from Britain and Scotland. The British government said it was working with New Delhi to resolve the matter, while the Scottish government separately raised concerns over the treatment of bulk Scotch imports. Scotch exports to India were valued at $335 million in 2024, and the Scotch Whisky Association has projected that the trade agreement could increase exports by an additional $1.34 billion over five years. title: 'Why should I wake up at 5 am?': Sarfaraz Khan opens up on India snubs, motivation and father's support
text: Sarfaraz Khan (PTI Photo) MUMBAI: The shrug of the shoulder said it all when Sarfaraz Khan was asked about his absence from the India Test set-up. The latest snub came when he was overlooked for India A's three-match tour of New Zealand. This was after he had been included in the Test squad for the Sri Lanka tour as Sai Sudharsan's replacement. Quizzed about what keeps him motivated despite repeatedly being overlooked, the 29-year-old said he often finds himself questioning the effort he puts in every day. Watch Inside Gill and KL Rahul's intense training | Why no Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma | Nets footage "I wake up every morning and ask myself the same question. Why should I work harder? Why do the same things? Why should I wake up at 5 am (for practice)? I have already played for India. So even with basic effort, I can still play for Mumbai. With that effort, I can still get those 50s and 100s. So sometimes I start questioning it (the effort). But when I see Abbu (father Naushad) putting in that effort, I think of going out there and performing for him. So there is something or the other that keeps motivating me," said the Mumbai batter. Sarfaraz last played for India when New Zealand toured the country in 2024. He was also part of the squad for India's 2024-25 tour of Australia but did not get a game Down Under. He added: "Right now, the motivation is to play cricket. I don't like to sit at home. I think I'm made for cricket. Wherever I get an opportunity... Ranji Trophy , Mushtaq Ali, Vijay Hazare , IPL, or if the Indian team calls me. I just want to play cricket." As far as communication from the national selectors is concerned, Sarfaraz feels let down by the perception that he is only being considered for Indian conditions. "The selector didn't say it directly. But when I went with the Indian team, I heard that they are looking at me more for Indian conditions. But I will question that (thinking). I have scored centuries in South Africa and England (during intra-squad matches). In India, you get such big rank turners. You struggle so much when you come from domestic cricket. And suddenly, you will not be able to perform on such a difficult wicket. .. so you can't get more than 30-40 runs," said Sarfaraz, who made a 100-ball 55 on Day One of Mumbai's Group D match against Railways at the Brabourne Stadium on Monday. The centuries Sarfaraz is referring to came during intra-squad games. In 2023, he scored a 61-ball century in Pretoria, while during the 2025 England tour, he made a 76-ball 101 for India A against the Indian Test squad. Despite the setbacks, he focused on improving his fitness, and skills, in the off-season and shedding a few kilos as well. He has lost 22kg and now tips the scales at 77kg, having once weighed 97kg. Right now, he is looking forward to scoring runs in the domestic season and staying ready for an India call-up so that he is not found wanting. But when it comes to Sarfaraz, a tongue-in-cheek comment is never far away, even if his career is at a crossroads. "I used to play better when I was fat," he said cheekily, before adding: "It is not like I'm not getting runs. You can't get the same amount of runs every year. Sometimes it's up and down. As long as you are not out of form, you don't have to worry. In reality, my weight was more." Sarfaraz still boasts a healthy first-class record, having scored 5,354 runs in 66 matches at an average of 63.73, including 18 centuries. He feels restarting every season isn't easy, nor is scoring truckloads of runs year after year. All he can do is work as hard as possible. "It's very difficult to make runs. My routine, after playing for so many years in the Ranji Trophy, hasn't changed. There's no off-season for me... I just keep practising. I don't know how many runs I am going to make, but the hard work I put in is the same. Everyone knows, if you want to meet Sarfaraz, you don't have to come to his home. It's very difficult to restart. Sometimes you get success, sometimes you don't. But this is the job," said Sarfaraz. One regret Sarfaraz has is not getting enough support in his push for an India spot. "Everyone knows that I don't have support in my life. Only my father has supported me. But it's okay. I have fulfilled my father's dream (of me playing for India). And it's not like I scored once or twice and immediately played for India. title: A âmellowed downâ Akash Anand hits campaign trail
text: BSP national convener Akash Anand Lucknow: The Bahujan Samaj Party public meeting at Anupshahr assembly constituency in Bulandshahr on Wednesday saw a âmellowed downâ party national convener Akash Anand. Though he hit out at UP govt for its functioning and policies, and also Congress and Samajwadi Party for failing people of UP, Akash exercised caution and restraint in his tirade against them. It was his first public meeting after his return to the party and reinstatement as national convener on Oct 5. Akash, who has been expelled thrice from the party by his aunt and BSP president Mayawati for being âimmatureâ in handling the national-level responsibilities in the party, had recently won her appreciation when she publicly acknowledged his display of âwisdom and maturityâ as the partyâs national convener in her post on X. On Wednesday, he lived up to his auntâs expectations when he avoided being drawn into any kind of personal attacks on his political opponents. When the crowd at the venue jeered âAkhilesh uncleâ as soon as Akash started talking about the SP chief and his PDA-model, his reaction was placid: âYou said Akhilesh uncle. Yes he is elder to me. But I will keep my views here with respect. This is not the time to indulge into banter. That is something we would do later on.â Akash had addressed Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav as âunclesâ in his Sadabad public meeting on Aug 10. âIf a 30 year old like me will not call a 50-year old as uncle then who else. To me, he is not Akhilesh bhaiya, but Akhilesh uncle,â were his words. His statements had soon gone viral online. He had also attacked CM Yogi Adityanath and said, âUP CM Yogi Adityanath goes on calling himself an encounter specialist, when crime is rife in the state. While he calls himself an encounter specialist, UP topped the country in terms of murders.â This time, there was no mention of UP CM or other senior BJP members, like Nitin Gadkari, whom Akash had lavishly attacked in his previous speeches. The change in his tone and tenor may have been because of Mayawatiâs schooling of him before he restarted his election campaign in UP. Akash was removed from the party on Sept 10 by Mayawati for being âimmatureâ in handling the national-level responsibility of the party. In fact, after his Sadabad public meeting on Aug 10 and his personal attacks on the opposition leaders going viral, the party did not play up his second public meeting which was at Jewar on Aug 25. Before he could continue, he was dropped from the party by Mayawati. The way Mayawati had reacted this time was similar to how she had reacted to Akashâs election speech in Sitapur during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Akash had faced an FIR for his speech in Sitapur on April 28, and days after that, Mayawati had sacked him from the party for his lack of maturity. title: WMO reports record-high Greenhouse Gas levels in 2025, says the long lifetime of CO2 commits planet to warmer future
text: NEW DELHI: Levels of globally averaged surface concentrations of carbon dioxide (CO2) and other major greenhouse gases (GHGs) - methane and nitrous oxide - in the atmosphere reached âunprecedented highsâ in 2025, locking in more long-term temperature increase for the planet, said a new report from the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) on Tuesday. It noted that the intensifying El Nino may lead to a further surge as this climatic phenomenon of warming of ocean surface temperatures in the central and eastern Equatorial Pacific has the potential to reduce the efficiency of the biosphere to absorb carbon dioxide. The report is one of the WMOâs flagship annual publications in which it shared levels of GHG concentrations - the amount of gas that accumulates in the atmosphere - and not new annual emissions. Since about half of the total CO2 emitted each year remains in the atmosphere and it has a very long lifetime, it leads to a rise in its levels of concentration that traps heat and eventually contributes to a warmer future. âThe past 11 years have been the warmest on record and this trend is set to continue. CO2 has a very long lifetime and so will affect the global climate not just for years but for decades and even centuries,â said WMO deputy secretary-general Ko Barrett. The report noted that though the increase in CO2 from 2024 to 2025 was lower than the anomalously high increase from 2023 to 2024, it was slightly higher than the average annual growth rate over the last decade (2016â2025). âThe more modest growth rate from 2024 to 2025 reflects recovery of the land carbon sinks and reduced fire carbon emissions in 2025 after the strong 2023/2024 El Nino, which reduced the efficiency of the biosphere through more drought, drier vegetation and more wildfires,â said WMO senior scientific officer Oksana Tarasova. The annual GHG Index, flagged by the report, shows that from 1990 to 2025, radiative forcing â the warming effect on climate â by long-lived greenhouse gases increased by 56%, with CO2 accounting for about 81% of this increase and its growth rates having tripled since the 1960s. Quantitatively, the globally averaged surface concentration of CO2 in 2025 was 426.8 parts per million, or 153% of the 1750 pre-industrial baseline. Concentrations of methane and nitrous oxide â the second and third most important long-lived greenhouse gases related to human activities â also rose to new records. Methane accounts for about 16% of the warming effect on climate by long-lived GHG but it has a much shorter lifetime than CO2. Approximately 35% of methane is emitted into the atmosphere by natural sources (for example, wetlands) which are sensitive to climate as well, and about 65% comes from anthropogenic sources such as cattle, rice farming, fossil fuel exploitation, landfills and biomass burning. âThe globally averaged methane concentration in 2025 was 1948 parts per billion (ppb) â or 267% of the 1750 level,â said the WMO in its annual bulletin, which provides authoritative scientific information for negotiators at the UN Climate conference. This year, the Conference is going to held in Antalya, TÃ¼rkiye from Nov 9-20.

title: Hackers disrupt US election watchdogâs filing system days before midterm polls
text: The US Federal Election Commission (FEC) has temporarily shut down its electronic filing system following a suspected hacking attempt. The outage occurred on Monday night, 26 October 2026, just one week before the November 3 midterm elections The US Federal Election Commissionâs (FEC) electronic filing system was taken offline after an attempted cyberattack, disrupting campaign finance disclosures a week before the November 3 midterm elections, Reuters reported, citing an email sent to campaign compliance firms. The outage has prevented political organisations from submitting mandatory 24-hour and 48-hour spending reports, which provide details of campaign expenditure on specific races. The disruption comes as political groups and super PACs spend record amounts in the final days of the campaign. In a statement, the FEC said, "At this time, the FEC's electronic filing system is currently offline and our IT staff are actively working to restore service." An FEC electronic filings officer said in an email to campaign compliance firms on Monday night, "We have a bad actor attempting to breach FEC systems. As a result, weâve had to temporarily shut down our web-facing services," Reuters reported. The agency later said the issue had been identified and a fix was being implemented. However, its filing system remained offline, while users could still search the website for previously filed reports. Steven Mele, president and CEO of political finance compliance firm MBA Consulting Group, said he had never seen such an incident in 26 years. The FEC tracks campaign spending by candidates and political committees but does not administer elections. The disruption is therefore not expected to affect votersâ ability to cast their ballots. Campaign spending reaches record levels The outage comes as the November 3 midterm elections have become the most expensive US election in history, with around $11.21 billion spent on advertising and future reservations so far, according to political advertising tracker AdImpact. The figure surpasses the $11.2 billion spent across all races in the 2024 elections, including $3.2 billion on the presidential contest between Donald Trump and Kamala Harris. Super PACs, which can accept unlimited contributions from wealthy individuals and corporations and spend heavily on campaigns, are driving much of the expenditure. Dark money groups are also spending large sums in the final stretch. Brendan Glavin, research director at nonpartisan campaign watchdog OpenSecrets, said super PACs and dark money groups had spent an average of more than $50 million a day over the previous week. More than $250 million in spending was reported on October 20 alone, he said. "It's a big deal," Glavin said of the outage, which has left voters without timely access to the latest spending disclosures. "These are the key reports that tell us what is happening," he said. "In the last days of the election this is the only way for us to keep track of where the money's being spent" and who's spending it. Midterms to decide control of Congress The November 3 elections will determine whether Trumpâs Republican Party retains its majorities in Congress for the next two years. All 435 seats in the House of Representatives and around one-third of the Senate seats are being contested. The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and the FBI referred questions about the cyber incident to the FEC. The agency did not immediately respond to Reutersâ request for comment. The FECâs filing system had been down since around 10pm ET on Monday, according to a status notice posted on its website.
